The purpose of this “good,” however, is that they may the more effectively “do his will.”
**Working in you.** See on Phil. 2:13.
**Through Jesus Christ.** See on Gal. 2:20.
**To whom be glory.** See on Gal. 1:5.
**For ever and ever.** See on Matt. 25:41; Rev. 1:6.
**Amen.** See on Matt. 5:18; Rom. 15:33.
21.zh:
在各樣善事上成全你們，叫你們遵行他的旨意；又藉著耶穌基督在你們心裡行他所喜悅的事。願榮耀歸給他，直到永永遠遠。阿們！

**善事。**“善”是保羅期望他的讀者所擁有併成為的，而不是他希望他們去行的。但“善事”的目的是使他們更有效地“遵行祂的旨意。”
**成全你們。**katartizō（見彼前5:10註釋；參太5:48註釋）。
**藉著耶穌基督。**見加2:20註釋。
**在你們心裡行。**見腓2:13註釋。
**願榮耀歸給祂。**見加1:5註釋。
**直到永永遠遠。**見太25:41；啟1:6註釋。
**阿們。**見太5:18；羅15:33註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷四第543頁。

6.en: **Boldly.** Or, “confidently.” The quotation is from the LXX of Ps. 118:6 (see comment there).
6.zh:
所以我們可以放膽說：主是幫助我的，我必不懼怕；人能把我怎麼樣呢？

**放膽。**或“放心。”引自七十士譯本詩118:6（見該節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第411頁；《基督教育原理》第348頁；《給傳道人的證言》第148頁；《證言》卷二第271頁。

8.en:
**Jesus Christ.** For the significance of the two names used together see on Matt. 1:1.
**The same.** The comment of v. 8 was apparently intended to prepare the way for the warning of v. 9. In view of the fact that Christ never changes, the message about Him can never change. Teachings that differ from the pure gospel already proclaimed may be dismissed without further examination. See on Gal. 1:6–8.
8.zh:
耶穌基督，昨日、今日、一直到永遠、是一樣的。

**耶穌基督。**關於這兩個名字合用的意義，見太1:1註釋。
**一樣的。**第8節的評論顯然為第9節的警告預備道路。鑑於基督是永不改變的，有關祂的信息也是永不改變的。凡與過去所傳的純正福音不同的各種道理都要予以拋棄，無需進一步查驗。見加1:6-8註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第209頁；《今日的生活》第300頁；《醫療佈道論》第92頁；《先祖與先知》第630頁；《給傳道人的證言》第81頁；《證言》卷五第62頁。

5.en:
**Conversation.** Gr. tropos, “way of life,” “turn of mind,” “conduct,” “character.” In Old English “conversation” had essentially these meanings.
**Covetousness.** See on Luke 12:13–34.
**Content.** See on Phil. 4:11; 1 Tim. 6:6.
**Such things as ye have.** If men could only learn to be content with what they have, and not covet what others have, most of the problems that torment the human race would automatically be solved. For comment on the Christian attitude toward the material things of life see on Matt. 6:19–34.
**He.** That is, God. The quotation is from the LXX of Deut. 31:6, 8.
**Never leave thee.** Concerning God’s beneficent provision for our needs see on Matt. 6:26–34.
5.zh:
你們存心不可貪愛錢財，要以自己所有的為足；因為主曾說：我總不撇下你，也不丟棄你。

**存心。**tropos，“生活方式，”“思想傾向，”“行為，”“品格。”古英語中的“conversation”基本上是這些意思。
**貪愛錢財。**見路12:13-34註釋。
**自己所有的。**如果人學會了滿足於自己所有的，不貪戀別人所有的，那麼困擾人類的大部分問題自然就得到了解決。關於基督徒對待今生物質財富的態度，見太6:19-34註釋。
**為足。**見腓4:11；提前6:6註釋。
**主。**就是上帝。引自七十士譯本申31:6,8。
**總不撇下你。**關於上帝仁慈地供應我們的需要，見太6:26-34註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第29頁；《復臨信徒家庭》第343頁；《傳道良助》第152頁；《醫療佈道論》第184頁；《證言》卷二第623頁；《證言》卷三第293頁；《證言》卷四第447，618頁；《證言》卷五第283頁；《證言》卷六第157頁；《證言》卷七第274頁。

9.en:
**Be not carried about.** Some are easily influenced by any new or strange teaching. Lacking spiritual discrimination, they are unable to differentiate between truth and error by comparing the new teaching with Scripture. For comment see on Eph. 4:14; Col. 2:4, 8.
**Divers.** Or, “diverse,” that is, differing from the pure gospel message already received.
**Established with grace.** That is, so as not to be “carried about” with fads in religion and in theology. The stabilizing power of the grace of Christ is the Christian’s best protection against errant teachings. For comment on “grace” see on Rom. 1:7; 3:24.
**Not with meats.** That is, “not with foods.” Apparently some, at least, of the religious faddists went beyond the plain teachings of Scripture with respect to diet, and made their dietary scruples a test of faith. For comment on the relationship of diet to religion, and for a warning against fads in diet disguised as religious obligations, see on Rom. 14:17; 1 Tim. 4:3.
**Not profited.** Even those who so vehemently lauded the value of the dietary fads they advocated had received no practical benefit therefrom. Doubtless, reference is to one or more of the Judaizing factions that troubled the early Christian church, such as the Ebionites and the Nazarenes (see Vol. VI, pp. 53, 54).
9.zh:
你們不要被那諸般怪異的教訓勾引了去；因為人心靠恩得堅固才是好的，並不是靠飲食。那在飲食上專心的從來沒有得著益處。

**不要被勾引了去。**一些人很容易受新奇教訓的影響。他們缺乏屬靈的辨別力，不能將新教訓與聖經比較，從而辨別真理與謬論。見弗4:14；西2:4,8註釋。
**諸般。**幾是與已經接受的純正福音信息不同。
**靠恩得堅固。**就是不要被宗教和神學上的時尚“勾引了去。”基督恩典堅固的能力乃是基督徒防範錯誤教訓的最佳保障。關於“恩典”，見羅1:7；3:24註釋。
**不是靠飲食。**一些追求時尚的信徒在飲食問題上超越了聖經的明白教訓，把飲食的禁忌作為信仰的試石。關於飲食與宗教的關係，以及不要把飲食的時尚作為宗教義務的警告，見羅14:17；提前4:3註釋。
**得著益處。**即使那些熱心鼓吹他們所倡導飲食時尚價值的人，也沒有從中得到任何實際益處。這裡無疑是指幾個騷擾早期基督教會的猶太教派別，如伊比奧尼派和拿撒勒派（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷六第53,54頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第438頁。

3.zh:
你們要記念被捆綁的人，好像與他們同受捆綁；也要記念遭苦害的人，想到自己也在肉身之內。

**被捆綁的……好像同受捆綁。**幫助在監牢裡的人，是另一項其重要性足以在最後的審判中予以考慮的事項（見太25:36）。和聖經其他地方一樣（見林前9:22），這裡所提出的原則，即基督徒應該設身處地為在危難中需要幫助的人著想，是符合黃金律的（見太7:12註釋）。
**遭苦害。**直譯是“遭到虐待。”
**自己也在肉身之內。**要設身處地為那些遭受苦害的人著想，並照顧他們的需要。黃金律的原則再次應用到實際情況中去。基督徒不要問那些遭受苦難的人值不值得幫助。對於他而言，知道他們需要幫助就夠了。
3.en:
**In bonds, as bound.** Ministry to men in prison is another activity of sufficient importance to come up for consideration in the final judgment (see Matt. 25:36). As elsewhere in Scripture (see 1 Cor. 9:22), the principle is here set forth that the Christian should endeavor to think of himself as being in the same circumstances as any person he finds in need and minister to him accordingly, in harmony with the golden rule (see on Matt. 7:12).
**Suffer adversity.** Literally, “are being illtreated.”
**Yourselves also in the body.** Think how you would feel if you were in the same situation as those who have met with illtreatment; then minister to their needs accordingly. The principle set forth in the golden rule is again applied to a practical situation. The Christian is not to inquire as to whether those suffering adversity may or may not deserve help. It is enough for him to know that they are in need of help.

7.zh:
從前引導你們、傳神之道給你們的人，你們要想念他們，效法他們的信心，留心看他們為人的結局。

**引導你們。**直譯是“嚮導，”“領袖，”這裡指教會的領袖。關於對教會領導的忠誠，見帖前5:12,13註釋。
**傳。**這裡指過去的領袖，可能現在已經在耶穌裡安息了。
**效法。**或“隨從。”
**他們的信心。**來11章所提到的信心英雄都生活在很久以前。但現代也有忠心的人。他們的榜樣完全值得效法。
**為人。**anastrophē，“生活方式，”“行為，”“舉止”（見弗4:22註釋）。
**結局。**作者心中無疑想到一些人，但沒有提他們的名字。
7.en:
**Them which have the rule.** Literally, “guides,” “leaders,” here meaning church leaders. For comment on loyalty to the leadership of the church see on 1 Thess. 5:12, 13.
**Have spoken.** Literally, “spoke,” implying that former leaders, perhaps now resting in Jesus, are here referred to.
**Whose faith.** The heroes of faith referred to in ch. 11 had all lived in the long ago. But there had also been faithful men in more recent times whose example might safely be followed.
**Follow.** Or, “imitate.”
**End.** The phrase reads literally, “result of their conduct.” The writer doubtless has certain particular persons in mind, though he does not name them.
**Conversation.** Gr. anastrophē, “manner of life,” “conduct,” “behavior” (see on Eph. 4:22).

10.zh:
我們有一祭壇，上面的祭物是那些在帳幕中供職的人不可同吃的。

**我們有一祭壇。**作者在這裡指祭司和利未人奉命將祭牲的一些部分帶到古時的聖所或聖殿（見利6:16-18；7:15,16,31-34；民18:8-10；申18:1,2；參林前9:13）。來13:9所提到的謬道可能強調基督徒必須遵行古時涉及飲食的猶太教禮儀，彷彿因此可以達到更聖潔狀態。但是基督徒有一座祭壇，就是髑髏地的十字架，並有其價值和功效遠超過古時祭牲的祭物（見來9:14,24-28；10:10,12,14註釋），那就是“上帝的羔羊，除去世人罪孽的”（約1:29）。基督還呼籲信祂的人要吃祂的肉（見約6:33-58）。
**供職的人。**就是祭司和利未人。
**不可同吃。**在猶太人的宗教制度下，祭司和利未人享有尊貴的地位和特權。他們的地位雖然很高，但由於他們拒絕了耶穌，就不配享受所有真正基督徒的權利。保羅可能還想到了聖餐的餅和葡萄汁。在任何情況下，第9節所提到“諸般怪異的教訓”自吹自擂的宗教體系都絕對比不上因信耶穌基督的得救之道。
10.en:
**We have an altar.** The writer here alludes to the fact that the priests and the Levites were assigned certain portions of some of the sacrificial animals brought to the ancient sanctuary or to the Temple (see Lev. 6:16–18; 7:15, 16, 31–34; Num. 18:8–10; Deut. 18:1, 2; cf. 1 Cor. 9:13). Perhaps the false doctrines referred to in Heb. 13:9 had stressed the importance of requiring Christians to practice the ancient rites and ceremonies of Judaism, which dealt with meats and drinks, as if a superior state of holiness could thereby be attained. But Christians have an altar, the cross of Calvary, and a sacrifice far surpassing the ancient animal sacrifices in value and efficacy (see on chs. 9:14, 24–28; 10:10, 12, 14). This was none other than “the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world” (John 1:29). Furthermore, Christ calls upon those who believe in Him to eat of His flesh (see John 6:33–58).
**They … which serve.** That is, the priests and the Levites.
**No right to eat.** Within the orbit of the Jewish religious system the priests and Levites enjoyed an honored position and special privileges. But, having rejected Jesus, they were unworthy, in spite of their exalted position, to partake of that to which all true Christians have a right. Paul may also have been thinking of the bread and the wine of the Lord’s table. Under any circumstances, the vaunted merits of the system of religion referred to as “divers and strange doctrines” in v. 9 were infinitely inferior to the way of salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.

11.zh:
原來牲畜的血被大祭司帶入聖所作贖罪祭；牲畜的身子被燒在營外。

**牲畜。**當贖罪祭的血被帶進聖所時，如為受膏的祭司或全會眾贖罪，祭司就不可吃祭肉，而要將它在營外燒掉（利6:30）。同樣，耶穌“也就在城門外受苦”（來13:12；參約19:17），然後祂用自己的血在天上的聖所中供職（來9:12）。在古代的獻祭制度中，祭司無權吃這種祭物通常屬於他們的部分（來13:10），但是基督說：“拿去，吃：這是我的身體，為你們擘開的”（林前11:24）。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《給管家的勉言》第54頁。
11.en: **Those beasts.** When the blood of the sin offering was carried into the sanctuary, as in the case of the anointed priest or the whole congregation, the priest was not to eat of the flesh but to burn it without the camp (Lev. 6:30). Similarly, Jesus “suffered without the gate” (Heb. 13:12; cf. John 19:17), after which He ministered His own blood in the heavenly sanctuary (Heb. 9:12). Under the old sacrificial system the priests would have had no right to eat their usual portion of such a sacrifice (ch. 13:10), but Christ said, “Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you” (1 Cor. 11:24).

12.zh:
所以，耶穌要用自己的血叫百姓成聖，也就在城門外受苦。

**叫百姓成聖。**基督在耶路撒冷“城門外受苦”，是為了用祂自己的血為悔改的罪人在天上的聖所中服務。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第741頁；見提前2:5懷愛倫註釋。
12.en: **That he might sanctify.** In order that Christ might minister His own blood on behalf of repentant sinners, in the heavenly sanctuary, He appropriately “suffered without the gate” of Jerusalem.

13.zh:
這樣，我們也當出到營外，就了他去，忍受他所受的凌辱。

**我們也當……就了祂去。**猶太籍的基督徒們不必再從猶太教的禮儀中尋求救恩。他們仍是以色列人，從寓意上說，他們也是耶路撒冷的居民。但是如果他們要跟從彌賽亞，就必須隨祂到耶路撒冷城外去。在《希伯來書》的背景中，這種情況就成了對猶太籍基督徒的呼籲，勸他們將視線轉離猶太教的禮儀，注視耶穌基督以及祂在天上聖所中作我們的大祭司（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七第389頁）。
**忍受祂所受的凌辱。**當耶穌作為被定了罪的犯人前往各各他時，那些同情祂的人與祂同受“凌辱”。猶太籍的基督徒擁護基督教會招致他們猶太同胞的仇恨。對於他們來說，轉離猶太人作為得救手段的獻祭制度，會招致背道和叛國的指控。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第508頁；《證言》卷一第692頁；《證言》卷三第49，423頁；《證言》卷五第461頁；《證言》卷六第332，412頁；《證言》卷八第53，71頁。
13.en:
**Let us go forth.** Jewish Christians would no longer seek salvation in the rites and ceremonies of the Jewish religion. They were still Israelites, and as such, figuratively speaking, inhabitants of the city of Jerusalem. But if they followed the Messiah, they must go with Him beyond the bounds of Judaism. In the setting of the book of Hebrews this situation constitutes an appeal to Jewish Christians to turn their eyes from the rites and ceremonies of Judaism and to fix them upon Jesus Christ and His ministry as our great High Priest in the heavenly sanctuary (see p. 389).
**Bearing his reproach.** Those who manifested sympathy for Jesus when He went forth to Golgotha as a condemned criminal suffered “reproach” with Him. For Jewish Christians to espouse Christianity was to incur the hatred of their fellow Jews, and for them to turn their backs on the Jewish sacrificial system as a means of salvation would be to incur the charge of apostasy and treason.

14.zh:
我們在這裡本沒有常存的城，乃是尋求那將來的城。

**沒有常存的城。**猶太人視耶路撒冷為“常存的城。”他們認為上帝的計劃與這座城是密不可分的，所以她一定會永遠堅立。他們覺得在耶路撒冷的範圍之內是安全的。但是基督徒並沒有這種“常存的城。”他們的期盼和願望與地上的任何城市或宗教制度無關。這對於希伯來籍基督徒是多麼重要啊！他們不久將目睹耶路撒冷的毀滅！
**尋求那將來的城。**就是新耶路撒冷（參來12:22）。參先祖亞伯拉罕的經驗（來11:10）。
14.en:
**No continuing city.** The Jews looked upon Jerusalem as a “continuing city.” that is, they considered that the divine plan was inextricably bound up with the city and that it was, therefore, destined to stand forever. They felt security within the arms of Judaism. But Christians have no such “continuing city.” Their hopes and aspirations are not associated with any earthly city or religious system. How significant for Hebrew Christians who in a short time were to witness the destruction of Jerusalem!
**Seek one to come.** That is, the New Jerusalem (cf. ch. 12:22). Compare the experience of the patriarch Abraham (ch. 11:10).

16.zh:
只是不可忘記行善和捐輸的事；因為這樣的祭，是神所喜悅的。

**不可忘記。**有人可能在這方面疏忽了。
**行善。**就是服務他人的需要。上帝不喜悅公牛和山羊的血（見來10:5-8註釋）。它們是沒有用處的。但是祂喜歡為他人服務的犧牲精神（見太25:24-40註釋）。那“清潔沒有玷汙的虔誠”（雅1:27）在祂眼中永遠是值得悅納的。
**捐輸。**或“捐獻。”
**上帝所喜悅的。**外表的禮儀對於上帝而言是沒有意義的。祂要人用“心靈和誠實”來敬拜祂（約4:23），那就是藉著反映祂的品格，在服務他人的生活中表明他們對祂的愛和獻身。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《醫療佈道論》第184頁。
16.en:
**Do good.** That is, to minister to the needs of others. God is not pleased with the blood of bulls and goats (see on ch. 10:5–8). It serves no useful purpose. But He is pleased with the spirit of sacrificial service for others (see on Matt. 25:24–40). The practice of “pure religion and undefiled” (James 1:27) is ever acceptable in His sight.
**Communicate.** Or, “share.”
**Forget not.** Perhaps some had grown careless in this respect.
**God is well pleased.** Formal rites and ceremonies have no meaning to God. He seeks men to worship Him in “spirit and in truth” (John 4:23), that is, by reflecting His character and by demonstrating their love and devotion to Him in a life of service for others.

17.zh:
你們要依從那些引導你們的，且要順服；因他們為你們的靈魂時刻警醒，好像那將來交帳的人。你們要使他們交的時候有快樂，不致憂愁；若憂愁就於你們無益了。

**依從。**見第7節註釋。
**要順服。**上帝已經任命領袖牧羊祂的羊群。祂呼籲祂的羊群要順服奉命管理他們的人，而這些領袖也要順服主。這裡指的是現在的領袖，而不是第7節所指從前的領袖。
**為你們的靈魂。**就是“為你們”（參來12:9,23註釋）。
**警醒。**上帝所任命管理教會的領袖要為祂子民的福利而向祂負責。祂必嚴格地要求他們為管家的職責交賬。
交帳。管家要為受託照管的任何物品向主人交賬，深知他必須對自己的管家職責負責。信徒與上帝所任命的領袖們合作，就能使他們更容易遞交管家的忠心賬目。
**有快樂。**因為知道他們已經忠實地履行了他們的職責。參蒙召進來享受主人快樂的忠心僕人的經驗（見太25:21）。
**不至憂愁。**直譯是“不至呻吟。”參不忠心的僕人的經驗（太25:28-30）。
**無益。**教會的信徒如果使上帝所任命的領袖交不出管家的好帳目，他們自己也得不到任何益處。雙方要共嘗交帳日子的“快樂”或“憂愁”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第371頁；《復臨信徒家庭》第528頁；《基督徒的服務》第169頁；《安息日學訓言》第44，50，80頁；《基督教育之研究》第47，65，102頁；《佈道論》第326，339頁；《早期著作》第61頁；《基督教育原理》第55，264頁；《傳道良助》第189頁；《服務真詮》第173頁；《給傳道人的證言》第122，150頁；《證言》卷一第138，153，471頁；《證言》卷二第457，706頁；《證言》卷三第242頁；《證言》卷四第343頁；《證言》卷五第11，237，684頁；《證言》卷六第62，70，75，86，92，248，302，434頁；《證言》卷七第13，68，117頁；《證言》卷九第45，58頁。
17.en:
**Obey.** See on v. 7.
**Submit yourselves.** God has appointed leaders to shepherd His flock, and He calls upon His sheep to submit to those appointed over them, the while these leaders themselves obey the Master. Here reference is to present leaders, not to former leaders as in v. 7.
**They watch.** The leaders God has appointed over the church are responsible to Him for the welfare of His people, and He will require a strict account of their stewardship.
**For your souls.** That is, “for you” (cf. on ch. 12:9, 23).
**Must give account.** A steward is accountable to his master for any goods entrusted to his care, and knows that he must answer for his stewardship. By cooperating with their appointed leaders church members make it much easier for them to render a faithful account of their stewardship.
**With joy.** That is, in the knowledge that they have faithfully discharged their responsibility. Compare the experience of the faithful servants who were summoned to enter into the joy of their Lord (see Matt. 25:21).
**Not with grief.** Literally, “not with groaning.” Compare the experience of the unfaithful servant (Matt. 25:28–30).
**Unprofitable.** Church members gain no advantage by making it difficult for their appointed leaders to render a good account of their stewardship. Both will share together the “joy” or the “grief” of the accounting day.

19.zh:
我更求你們為我禱告，使我快些回到你們那裡去。

**更。**或“更加誠懇地”。
**求。**作者懇求讀者為他禱告，使他擺脫妨礙他到他們那裡去的環境，其語氣非常感人，反映了他個人對祈禱能的信心。
**回到你們那裡去。**第23節提到提摩太當時還在監獄中，似乎暗示《希伯來書》的作者是自由的。可能是其它環境因素，如生病或傳道工作的壓力妨礙保羅回到他的讀者們那裡去。
19.en:
**I beseech.** The earnestness with which the writer appeals to his readers to pray for his release from circumstances that prevented fellowship with them is touching indeed and reflects his personal faith in the power of prayer.
**The rather.** Or, “the more earnestly” (RSV).
**Restored to you.** Verse 23 suggests that Timothy was in prison at the time and seems to imply that the writer of Hebrews was at liberty. Other circumstances such as illness or the pressure of missionary duties may have prevented Paul’s return to his readers.

22.zh:
弟兄們，我略略寫信給你們，望你們聽我勸勉的話。

**略略寫信。**關於這個題目，他還有更多的話要說，但是篇幅不允許。
**聽。**或“忍受。”
**勸勉的話。**就是《希伯來書》中的信息（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七第389頁）。
22.en:
**Suffer.** Or, “endure,” “bear.”
**Word of exhortation.** That is, the message contained in the book of Hebrews (see p. 389).
**In few words.** There was much more that he would like to have said on the subject, but space did not permit.

23.zh:
你們該知道，我們的兄弟提摩太已經釋放了；他若快來，我必同他去見你們。

**提摩太。**見徒16:1註釋。
**釋放了。**這裡所說的囚禁在聖經其他地方沒有提到。
**他若快來。**關於這裡所提到的訪問，我們不知道進一步的情況。
23.en:
**Timothy.** See on Acts 16:1.
**Set at liberty.** The imprisonment here alluded to is otherwise unknown.
**If he come.** Nothing further is known of the visit here proposed.

24.zh:
請你們問引導你們的諸位和眾聖徒安。從義大利來的人也問你們安。

**問安。**或“致意”。
**引導你們的。**指教會的領袖（見第7節註釋）。
**從意大利來的人。**就是基督的信徒。無法從這句話中確定這些信徒當時是在意大利，這封書信是從意大利帶來的，還是這些人從意大利來，與作者同在另外一個地方。
24.en:
**Salute.** Or, “greet.”
**Them that have the rule.** That is, the leaders of the church (see on v. 7).
**They of Italy.** Rather, “they from Italy,” that is, Christian believers. Whether these believers were in Italy at the time, and the epistle thus sent from Italy, or whether they had come from Italy and were with the writer in some other place, cannot be determined from this expression.

25.zh:
願恩惠常與你們眾人同在。阿們！

**恩惠與你們眾人同在。**見多3:15註釋。
**阿們。**見太5:18；羅15:33註釋。
第25節後面的後記“從意大利藉提摩太寫給希伯來人”在原信中是沒有的，最初出現在第6世紀的一份文稿裡。
25.en:
**Grace be with you all.** See on Titus 3:15.
**Amen.** See on Matt. 5:18; Rom. 15:33.
The postscript following v. 25 was not part of the original epistle. It appears first in a 6th-century manuscript.

9.en:
**Being made perfect.** Gr. teleioō (see on ch. 2:10). The verb form may be translated “having been made perfect,” or “having been completed.” The thought is that of having attained a goal, of having finished a task. Christ achieved that which He had set out to accomplish through His humanity. He had demonstrated His obedience to the point of death, and was perfected. He was now qualified for the office of high priest (see on ch. 5:1–3).
**Author.** Gr. aitios, “cause,” “source.” It was the fulfillment of the plan laid before the foundation of the world with regard to His incarnation, life, death, resurrection, and glorification, that made Him the source of salvation. See Acts 4:12.
**That obey him.** Obedience is directly involved in the plan of salvation, not that salvation is earned by obedience, but that faith leads to obedience. For the relationship of works to faith see on Rom. 3:31.
9.zh:
他既得以完全，就為凡順從他的人成了永遠得救的根源、

**既得以完全。**teleioō（見來2:10註釋）。說明已經達到了一個目標，完成了一項任務。基督藉著人性完成了祂所開始的工作。祂證明自己順從至死，達到完全的地步。祂現在有資格擔任大祭司了（見來5:1-3註釋）。
**凡順從祂的人。**順從與救恩的計劃有直接的關係。但救恩不是靠順從賺來的。順從是信心的結果。關於信心與行為的關係，見羅3:31註釋。
**根源。**aitios，“原因，”“來源”，“作者”。 祂成為得救的根源，是因為祂執行了創世以前就已經制定的有關祂道成肉身，生，死，復活和得榮耀的計劃。見徒4:12。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第370頁；《證言》卷三第18頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–12節）**。見林前3:1.2懷愛倫註釋。

12.en:
**For the time.** Rather, “on account of the time [elapsed].”
**Ought to be teachers.** These were not new converts, or this statement could not be true. But they had apparently not progressed as far and as rapidly as it was their privilege to do.
**Teach you again.** They had been taught before, but they had forgotten their lessons and needed to be taught again. The same condition exists today. Old and young waste time on that which is not essential, fail to improve their opportunities, and need to learn again the first principles of Christianity. This is a lamentable condition.
**Principles.** Gr. stoicheia, “elements [of learning],” “fundamental principles” (see on Gal. 4:3; Col. 2:8).
**Oracles.** Gr. logia (see on Acts 7:38; Rom. 3:2).
**Milk … strong meat.** By these are indicated the fundamental principles of the gospel and the advanced principles. For this figure see on 1 Cor. 3:1, 2. God wants all to grow up into the full stature of manhood in Christ, and “henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine” (see on Eph. 4:14).
12.zh:
看你們學習的工夫，本該作師傅，誰知還得有人將神聖言小學的開端另教導你們，並且成了那必須吃奶，不能吃乾糧的人。

**工夫。**或“所化的時間。”
**本該作師傅。**他們不是新信徒，否則就不該這樣說了。但他們顯然沒有像他們本來有特權作到的那樣，取得迅速而長足的進步。
**聖言。**logia（見徒7:38；羅3:2註釋）。
**開端。**stoicheia，“（學習的）原理，”“基本原理”（見加4:3；西2:8註釋）。
**另教導你們。**他們曾受過教，但是他們忘記了所學的教訓，需要重新受教。今日也有這種情況。人們都把時間化在次要的事上，沒有利用自己的機會。他們需要重新學習基督教的基本原理。這是一種可悲的狀況。
**奶……乾糧。**比喻福音的基本原理和高級原理。關於這個比喻，見林前3:1,2註釋。上帝希望大家都長大成人，滿有基督長成的身量，“此後不再作小孩子，被一切異教之風搖動，飄來飄去”（見弗4:14註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《佈道論》第355頁；《基督教育原理》第266頁；《證言》卷七第24頁。

6.en:
**He.** That is, God, the speaker in v. 5.
**Thou art a priest.** A citation from Ps. 110:4, here quoted as evidence that God had appointed His Son to priestly office. The priesthood of Christ is fully discussed in subsequent chapters (Heb. 7–10).
**For ever.** In contrast with earthly high priests, who because of death held office for limited periods.
**Order.** Gr. taxis, “fixed succession,” “order,” “position,” “nature,” “quality,” “post,” “rank.” Here the definitions “fixed succession” or “order” do not appear suitable, for Melchisedec had no line of successors. Preferable are definitions like “quality” or “nature,” “manner.” The passage may be rendered, “according to the nature of Melchisedec.” In Ps. 110:4 the Hebrew word for “order” is dibrah, which means “manner.” This supports the idea that succession is not the point of comparison here intended.
**Melchisedec.** A transliteration of the Gr. Melchisedek, which in turn is from the Heb. Malki–ṣedeq. The spelling “Melchizedek” (Gen. 14:18) is a transliteration of the Hebrew. For the identity of Melchisedec see on Heb. 7:2.
6.zh:
就如經上又有一處說：你是照著麥基洗德的等次永遠為祭司。

**又有一處說。**就是第5節中說話的上帝說。
**麥基洗德。**Melchisedek，源於希伯來語Malki-edeqs。“Melchizedek”（創14:18）的拼法來自希伯來語。關於麥基洗德的身份，見來7:2註釋。
**等次。**taxis，“繼任，”“順序，”“職位，”“性質，”“品質，”“崗位，”“等級。”在這裡“繼任”或“次序”的意思似乎並不適合，因為麥基洗德並沒有繼任者的家系。比較合適的定義是“品質”“性質”或“方式。”這句話可譯為：“按照麥基洗德的性質。”在詩110:4中，“等次”的希伯來語是dibrah，意為“方式”說明這裡所指的並不是繼任。
**永遠。**與因為會死亡而暫時任職的地上大祭司不同。
**為祭司。**引自詩110:4，證明上帝任命祂的兒子擔任祭司。下面幾章充分論述了基督的祭司職任（來7-10）。

8.en:
**Though he were a Son.** This has reference to the divinity of Christ. Though He took humanity, Christ was nevertheless divine. The two natures were mysteriously blended in Him (see on John 1:14). The resurrection especially declared Him to be the Son of God (see on Rom. 1:4), but prior to that event He was already Son (see on Luke 1:35). The thought of the passage is that though He was divine, He learned “obedience by the things which he suffered.”
**Learned.** Gr. manthanō, “to learn,” “to come to know,” “to come to understand.” Christ came to understand what obedience meant. For Him it entailed suffering and death; He “became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross” (Phil. 2:8). He came to this earth to do the will of God (Heb. 10:9), and from this course He could not be swerved. Doing His Father’s will involved Jesus in constant conflict, but not once did He yield to temptation. Knowing by personal experience the involvements of human obedience to the divine will, He is able “to succour” those who are tempted to swerve from the path of obedience (ch. 2:18).
Sometimes the question is raised how it could be said that Christ, who is perfect and at every moment has been perfect, needed to learn obedience. Two observations may help to answer this query: (1) As far as His earthly life is concerned Christ developed like other human beings. He “increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man” (see on Luke 2:52). He learned by observation and experience as do others. (2) Though as God prior to the incarnation Christ was omniscient, yet He did not know by experience the problems confronting men as they seek to render obedience to God. By becoming man and by facing the temptations of life as a man, Christ gained this knowledge. He thus met one of the essential qualifications for the high priesthood, namely that the appointee belong to the human family (see on Heb. 5:1–3).
8.zh:
他雖然為兒子，還是因所受的苦難學了順從。

**祂雖然為兒子。**這是指基督的神性。基督雖然取了人性，仍具有神性。這兩種本性在祂身上神秘地結合在一起（見約1:14註釋）。復活時特別宣佈祂是上帝的兒子（見羅1:4註釋），但祂在復活之前就已經是上帝的兒子（見路1:35註釋）。這句話的意思是：祂雖為神聖之主，仍“因所受的苦難學了順從。”
**學了。**manthanō，“學習，”“開始明白，”“開始理解。”基督來要體驗順從的意義，所以祂必須受苦和受死。祂“存心順服，以至於死，且死在十字架上”（腓2:8）。祂來到這個世上，是要遵行上帝的旨意（來10:9），祂不能偏離這個目標。遵行祂父的旨意使祂處於不斷的鬥爭中，但祂沒有一次屈服試探。祂既親身經歷了人類順從上帝旨意所涉及的一切情況，就能“搭救”那些受試探要離開順從之路的人（來2:18）。
有時人們會問，基督既是完全的，並且時時刻刻都是完全的，為什麼還說祂需要學習順從呢？以下兩點可以幫助解答這個問題：一，基督在地上的生命是和別人一樣逐漸發育的。祂的“智慧和身量，並上帝和人喜愛他的心，都一齊增長”（見路2:52註釋）。祂與別人一樣通過觀察和經驗學習。二，基督雖然在道成肉身之前是無所不知的上帝，但祂並沒有從經驗上了解人尋求順從上帝時所面臨的種種問題。基督藉著成為人，並象人那樣面對生活的種種試探，而獲得了這方面的知識。這樣，祂就滿足了擔任大祭司的一個重要資格，被任命者必須屬於人類的家庭（見來5:1-3註釋）。

5.en:
**So also Christ.** Verses 5–10 show that Christ met the qualifications for high priesthood set down in vs. 1–4. These are: (1) the high priest must share humanity (vs. 1–3); (2) he must be appointed by God (v. 4).
**Glorified not himself.** Christ did not assume the honor of the high priest’s office uninvited. It was God who appointed Him. Compare John 8:54.
**Thou art my Son.** See on ch. 1:5. The citation is here given to prove that Christ’s exalted position was by His Father’s appointment. See on Acts 13:32, 33.
5.zh:
如此，基督也不是自取榮耀作大祭司，乃是在乎向他說你是我的兒子，我今日生你的那一位；

**如此，基督也不是。**5-10節說明基督符合1-4節所列大祭司的資格，那就是：一，大祭司必須具有人性（第1-3節）；二，有必須由上帝所任命（第4節）。
**自取榮耀。**基督並沒有擅取大祭司職務的尊榮。任命祂的乃是上帝。參約8:54。
**你是我的兒子。**見來1:5註釋。這段引文是要證明基督的崇高職位是祂的父所任命的。見徒13:32,33註釋。

13.en:
**Unskillful.** Gr. apeiros, “unacquainted with,” “unskilled.” The one who is apeiros is not necessarily unacquainted altogether with the Word of righteousness, but his knowledge is limited and his spiritual growth retarded. As men become skillful in a trade or profession, so God wants us to become skillful and experienced in the use of the Word.
**Word of righteousness.** Here, doubtless, a general term synonymous with “gospel.”
**Babe.** Here a figure of underdevelopment (cf. on Eph. 4:14).
13.zh:
凡只能吃奶的都不熟練仁義的道理，因為他是嬰孩；

**不熟練。**apeiros，“不熟悉，”“不熟練。”一個熟練的人不一定完全不知道仁義的道理，但他的認識是有限，屬靈的發育遲緩。人怎樣需要在某一個行業上熟練起來，上帝也希望我們在運用聖道方面熟練而富有經驗。
**仁義的道理。**無疑泛指“福音”。
**嬰孩。**比喻發育不全（參弗4:14註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–14節）**。《佈道論》第200，252，300頁。

4.en:
**Honour.** Gr. timē “honor,” “respect,” “a place of honor,” “office.” Here “office” or “place of honor” would be suitable meanings. The office of high priest was a position of honor.
**Called of God.** The office of high priest was by divine appointment. It was God who selected Aaron for the position (Ex. 28:1). The succession in the family of Aaron was also presumably ordered by God as implied in the text under consideration. In the course of Israel’s history many priests held the office who were unworthy of their position, but the author is here not concerned with this. It is his purpose to set forth divine appointment as an essential qualification of the true high priesthood, in order to show that Christ met this as well as other requirements (Heb. 5:5–10).
4.zh:
這大祭司的尊榮，沒有人自取。惟要蒙神所召，像亞倫一樣。

**尊榮。**timē，“榮譽，”“尊敬，”“尊位，”“職位。”這裡用“職位”或“尊位”的意思比較合適。大祭司的職位乃是一個尊位。
**上帝所召。**大祭司的職位是上帝所任命的。是上帝揀選亞倫擔任這個職位（出28:1）。本節暗示亞倫家族的繼承人也是上帝所任命的。在以色列的歷史中，曾有許多不配的人擔任祭司，但作者在這裡並沒有考慮這一點。他的目的是要指出上帝的任命乃是真正大祭司的一個重要資格，說明基督既符合其他要求，也符合這個要求（來5:5-10）。

1.en:
**High priest.** The essential qualifications of the office of high priesthood are here set forth (vs. 1–4) to show that Christ possessed these qualifications (vs. 5–10).
**Taken from among men.** This phrase qualifies the term “high priest.” The author is here discussing human high priests. Later (vs. 5–10) he will discuss Christ as high priest.
**Ordained.** Gr. kathisetēmi, “to appoint,” “to put in charge.” The appointment is by God (see v. 4).
**For men.** Or, “in behalf of men.” The service of the high priests was in behalf of men, as mediators between them and God.
**Things pertaining to God.** See on ch. 2:17.
**May offer.** This was doubtless the most significant function of the high priestly office.
**Gifts.** Gr. dōra, in the LXX denoting specifically the “meat offerings” (Heb. minchoth, sing. minchah, see on Lev. 2:1), though in Gen. 4:4 the word is used of the offering of Abel.
**Sacrifices.** Gr. thusiai in the LXX generally denoting blood sacrifices, though not without exception. In Gen. 4:5 thusiai is used of the bloodless offering of Cain. It is doubtful that any distinction should be sought between dōra and thusiai. The two terms are probably used together as a generic phrase denoting the whole round of offerings and sacrifices involved in the Jewish ceremonial system.
**For sins.** The gifts and sacrifices had to do with the sins of the people. The ceremonial system was designed to teach men God’s abhorrence of sin and His plan for dealing with it.
1.zh:
凡從人間挑選的大祭司，是奉派替人辦理屬神的事，為要獻上禮物和贖罪祭（或作：要為罪獻上禮物和祭物）。

**從人間挑選的。**修飾 “大祭司”。作者在這裡討論人間的大祭司。然後（第5-10節）討論基督作大祭司。
**大祭司。**這裡指出擔任大祭司的必要資格（第1-4節），說明基督有這些資格（第5-10節）。
**奉派。**kathisetēmi，“任命，”“委任。”這是上帝委任的（見第4節）。
**替人。**大祭司的工作是為了人類，作人與上帝之間的中保。
**屬上帝的事。**見來2:17註釋。
**為要獻上。**這無疑是大祭司最重要的職任。
**禮物。**dōra，在七十士譯本中特指“素祭”（希伯來詞語minchoth，單數形式是minchah，見利2:1註釋），但在創4:4中，該詞用來指亞伯的供物。
**贖罪。**禮物和祭物都與百姓的罪有關。儀文制度的目的就是告訴人上帝憎恨罪，以及祂處理罪惡的計劃。
**祭。**thusiai，在七十士譯本中一般指流血的祭物，但不是沒有例外。在創4:5中，thusiai用來指該隱不流血的祭物。不知是否要對dōra和thusiai進行區別。這兩個詞用在一起可能泛指猶太教儀文制度所涉及的所有供物和祭物。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《安息日學訓言》第179頁；《基督教育之研究》第196頁。

14.en:
**Strong meat.** See on v. 12. The author is preparing his readers to receive advanced instruction in certain matters relating to the true position of Christ. He wishes to stir up his readers to a greater degree of interest in that which he is about to impart. He thinks the time has come for them to take a forward step, throw off their infantile habits, and become adults.
**Them that are of full age.** Gr. teleioi, “mature” (see on Matt. 5:48).
**Use.** Gr. hexis, “exercise,” “practice.”
**Senses.** Gr. aisthētēria literally, “the organs of sense,” figuratively, “the senses,” here the faculties for making the proper moral decisions. The passage may be translated, “having the faculties trained to distinguish between good and evil.”
**Exercised.** Gr. gumnazō, “to train,” “to exercise.” Our word “gymnasium” is derived from this root (cf. on 2 Peter 2:14).
14.zh:
惟獨長大成人的才能吃乾糧；他們的心竅習練得通達，就能分辨好歹了。

**長大成人。**teleioi，“成熟”（見太5:48註釋）。
**乾糧。**見第12節註釋。作者預備他的讀者接受有關基督真地位的高級教訓。他想激發讀者對他即將傳播的信息產生更大的興趣。他認為時候已到，他們應該更前進一步，擺脫他們嬰兒的習性，長大成人。
**心竅。**aisthētēria，直譯是“感官，”指能作出正確的道德判斷。這句話可譯為：“練好本領就能辨別是非。”
**習練。**gumnazō，“訓練，”“練習。”英語的“gymnasium”（健身房）就來自這個詞根（參彼後2:14註釋）。hexis，“練習，”“實踐。”

2.zh:
他能體諒那愚蒙的和失迷的人，因為他自己也是被軟弱所困。

**他能。**因為他自己也有軟弱的人性。
**體諒。**metriopatheō，“緩解人的情緒，”“溫和地對待，”“溫柔地探索。”
**愚蒙。**agnoeō，“不知道”，“不明白，”“無知，”“作錯，”“出於無知的犯罪。”最後一種意思似乎特別適合於本節。要溫柔地對待那些因無知而犯罪的人，因為他們犯罪不是故意的。他們需要啟發和鼓勵。他們是在無意中犯罪的人，不應與明知故犯的人同樣對待。
**失迷。**或“被誘入歧途的人，”“受騙的人。”
**被軟弱所困。**大祭司和他的百姓經受一樣的磨難，對肉體的軟弱和試探有親身的體驗，使他能體諒別人的軟弱和失敗，並勸勉和幫助那些受試探的人。參來2:17；4:15註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第297，499頁；《教育論》第270，294頁；《證言》卷二第509頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–3節）**。《基督教育原理》第268頁。
2.en:
**Who can.** Literally, “being able.” The basis of his ability is his own frail humanity.
**Have compassion.** Gr. metriopatheō, “to moderate one’s feelings,” “to deal gently with,” “to feel gently toward.”
**The ignorant.** Gr. agnoeō, “not to know,” “not to understand,” “to be ignorant,” “to do wrong,” “to sin in ignorance.” The last meaning seems to be particularly appropriate here. Those who sin through ignorance need to be gently dealt with inasmuch as their offense is not willful. They need enlightenment and encouragement. They are unwitting offenders and should not be classed with those who commit the same offenses with full knowledge of the evil of their course.
**That are out of the way.** Rather, “those who are being led astray,” or “those who are being deceived.”
**Compassed with infirmity.** The high priest was subject to like passions as his people were. His personal, experimental knowledge of the weaknesses and temptations of the flesh led him to have a sympathetic understanding of the weaknesses and failures of others, and qualified him to give counsel and help to those in temptation. Compare on chs. 2:17; 4:15.

3.zh:
故此，他理當為百姓和自己獻祭贖罪。

**故此。**由於他自己也被軟弱所困，他和他的百姓同樣有犯罪的傾向。古時的儀文制度要求他為自己的罪獻祭。
**理當。**opheilō。基於儀文律法的要求（見利16:6；參來4:3）。要求大祭司為自己的罪獻祭，這使他能同情百姓。他自己既犯了同樣的或可能更嚴重的錯誤時，他怎麼能責備別人呢？他需要保持謙卑的態度，以深切的同情看待那些失敗的人。當一個人想到自己的軟弱時，就不會無情地責備別人了。參加6:1。
**為百姓。**可能指贖罪日。那時大祭司要“為以色列人贖罪”（利16:34）。
**和自己。**見上面“理當”註釋。
3.en:
**By reason hereof.** Or “on account of this,” that is, on account of the fact that he himself was beset with infirmity. He had the same propensities toward sin as had his people, and the ancient ceremonial system required him to offer sacrifice for his personal sins.
**Ought.** Gr. opheilō, “to be obligated.” The obligation was based on the requirements of the ceremonial law (see Lev. 16:6; cf. ch. 4:3). The fact that the high priest was required to offer sacrifices for his own sins would lead him to have compassion on the people. How could he blame others when he himself committed the same, or perhaps worse, wrongs? He needed to maintain a humble attitude, and regard with deep compassion those who failed. As a man considers his own weaknesses, he is not likely to condemn others mercilessly. Compare Gal. 6:1.
**For the people.** The reference is probably to the Day of Atonement, when the high priest made “an atonement for the children of Israel” (Lev. 16:34).
**For himself.** See above under “ought.”

7.zh:
基督在肉體的時候，既大聲哀哭，流淚禱告，懇求那能救他免死的主，就因他的虔誠蒙了應允。

**基督。**見第5節註釋。這裡的語法結構有點複雜。句子的主要動詞是“學了”（第8節），主題思想是基督“學了順從”。
**在肉體的時候。**就是祂在地上生活的時候（見約1:14註釋）。
**大聲哀哭，流淚。**似乎特指基督在客西馬尼園的經歷。雖然福音書作者沒有提到救主在極其痛苦時流淚，但這是很容易想像得到的。有人認為作者是指基督在十字架上的經歷。見太26:36-44；27:46；可14:32-41；15:34；路22:39-44；23:46。
**禱告。**deēseis，“請求，”“懇求，”“祈禱，”源於動詞deomai（“要求，”“求恩”）。 這句話是指耶穌因禱告懇求，蒙了應允而學了順從。順從是通過經驗而學的，而不是隨著經驗而來的。
**懇求。**hiketēriai，指懇求者手裡拿著的橄欖枝。該詞依據這個習俗表示懇切祈求。
**能救。**聖父能救聖子免死，這使得考驗更為嚴峻。上帝兒子的人性在與天父分離的恐懼面前畏縮了。雖然祂願意獨自滿經過深水，但祂懇求免喝那杯，假如有另一條道路的話。但不存在其他的道路，於是祂喝了那杯。
**免死。**可能暗示基督要經歷死亡，但上帝要救祂，讓祂復活。
**因祂的虔誠。**apo tēs eulabeias，或“因祂的憂慮”。關於eulabeia究竟是指虔誠還是憂慮，註釋家們有不同的意見。如果是指憂慮，這句話的意思就是：“祂蒙了應允脫離了祂的憂慮。”但聖經對eulabeia及其相關詞的用法支傾向於理解為“虔誠”或“敬畏”。例如eulabeia在來12:28中譯為“虔誠敬畏”。參形容詞eulabēs在路2:25；徒2:5；8:2的用法，以及動詞eulabeomai在徒23:10；來11:7中的用法。
**蒙了應允。**這句話有些難解，因為基督並沒有免死，這裡卻說基督“蒙了應允”。如果按上面的解釋理解“免死”，這句話就不難接受了。如果“免死”理解為基督不願意經歷死亡，下面解釋就比較合適：這裡並不是說基督懇求免死，而是求那能救祂免死的天父；同觀福音書清楚地記載基督禱告說：“倘若可行，便叫那時候過去”（可14:35）。《馬太福音》記載祂禱告說：“我父啊，這杯若不能離開我，必要我喝，就願你的意旨成全”（太26:42）。這些話只能理解為如果可能並符合上帝旨意的話，基督希望免死。
如果基督在禱告中貿然要求免死，那就得承認祂的要求被拒絕了。但基督並沒有這樣求。當祂加添了順服的話“願你的意旨成全”時，祂就為天父按自己的美意去作掃清了道路，並保證自己會接受天父的決定。因為基督的意思就是天父的意思。無論天父怎樣決定，都是基督的決定。基督就這樣蒙了應允；每一個達到上帝面前順從祂旨意的禱告也這樣蒙了應允。
基督徒不要以為自己的禱告沒有蒙應允。每一個懇切的祈禱都已蒙垂聽，即使回答並不那麼理想。回答既有肯定的，也有否定的。但上帝的回答往往既不肯定，也不否定，而是“等候”。順從上帝的旨意乃是有效祈禱的大訣竅。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》第31頁；《證言》卷二第508頁；《證言》卷三第379頁；《證言》卷七第42頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。見來2:18懷愛倫註釋。
7.en:
**Who.** That is, Christ (see on v. 5). The grammatical construction is somewhat involved. The principal verb of the sentence is “learned” (v. 8), and the principal thought, Christ learned obedience.
**Days of his flesh.** That is, the period of his earthly life (see on John 1:14).
**When he had offered up.** That is, by offering up, or, in offering up. The idea of the passage is that in offering up his prayers and supplications and in being heard Jesus learned obedience. The obedience was learned by these experiences, not following them.
**Prayers.** Gr. deēseis, “petitions,” “entreaties,” “prayers,” from the verb deomai, “to ask,” “to beg as a favor.”
**Supplications.** Gr. hiketēriai, used of olive branches held in the hands of suppliants, from which custom the word came to denote the earnest supplications themselves.
**Strong crying and tears.** This seems to refer especially to the experience in the Garden of Gethsemane. Although the gospel writers do not mention tears in connection with the agony there experienced, these can easily be imagined. Some believe the author is referring also to the experience on the cross. See Matt. 26:36–44; 27:46; Mark 14:32–41; 15:34; Luke 22:39–44; 23:46.
**Able to save.** The fact that the Father was able to save the Son from death made the trial so much the greater. The humanity of the Son of God shrank from the horror of separation from the Father. While He was willing to go through the deep waters alone, He prayed earnestly to be exempted from drinking the cup if there was another way. But there was not other way, and so He drank it.
**From death.** Literally, “out of death,” which may imply that Christ would experience death, but that God would save Him out of it, that is, raise Him.
**Was heard.** This statement has caused some difficulty, because of the fact that Christ was not saved from death; and yet the assertion is made that Christ “was heard.” If the phrase “from death” be understood as explained above, the passage presents no difficulty. If “from death” be understood as signifying that Christ would not experience death, then the following explanation is pertinent: The text does not say that Christ asked to be saved from death, but that He prayed to Him who is able to save Him from death; and the accounts in the Synoptics clearly state that Christ prayed that “if it were possible, the hour might pass from him” (Mark 14:35). In Matthew He is quoted as praying, “O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done” (Matt. 26:42). These statements can be understood only in the light of Christ’s desire to be spared from death, if it were possible and consistent with God’s will.
Had Christ in His prayer peremptorily demanded that He be saved from death, then it must be admitted that His request was denied. But Christ did not demand this. When He added the words of submission, “Thy will be done,” He cleared the way for the Father to do as He thought best, and pledged Himself to accept His decision. As Christ’s will was also the Father’s will, whatever He should decide would likewise be Christ’s decision. In this way Christ was heard, and in this way every prayer is heard that ascends to God in submission to His will.
Let no Christian think that his prayer is not heard. Every earnest prayer is heard, even though it be not answered favorably. No is as definite an answer as Yes; though often the answer is neither Yes nor No, but Wait. Submission to the will of God is the great secret of effective prayer.
**In that he feared.** Gr. apo tēs eulabeias, “from his piety,” that is, because of his piety, or from his anxiety. Commentators are divided as to whether eulabeia should be regarded as reverent fear or as ordinary fear and anxiety. If as ordinary fear, the passage would mean, “he was heard [that is, delivered] from his anxiety.” However, scriptural usage of eulabeia and its related forms favors the definition “piety,” or “reverent fear.” For example, eulabeia is rendered “godly fear” in ch. 12:28. Compare the use of the adjective eulabēs in Luke 2:25; Acts 2:5; 8:2, and of the verb eulabeomai, in Acts 23:10; Heb. 11:7.

10.zh:
並蒙神照著麥基洗德的等次稱他為大祭司。

**麥基洗德的等次。**見第6節註釋。
**稱。**prosagoreuō，“問候，”“致敬，”“提名，”“叫作。”該詞在《新約》中只出現在這裡。“稱”的常用詞是kaleō，在第4節中用出現過。Prosagoreuō指基督被上帝正式任命為大祭司。
**大祭司。**基督教界一般都瞭解基督是“除去世人罪孽的”“上帝的羔羊”（約1:29）。他們知道基督是被釘十字架的主，為拯救我們而捨己。但並不是所有的基督徒都知道基督作為大祭司用自己的血在天上的聖所中服務。然而如果沒有這種服務，救恩的計劃就無效。上帝在埃及設立逾越節時曾吩咐以色列人不單要宰殺羊羔，還要將羊羔的血塗在門框上（見出12:7-13）。照樣在原型中，我們逾越節的羔羊基督的血（林前5:7）不僅要流出來，而且要由我們的大祭司在天上為我們供奉，作為上帝拯救我們計劃的一個重要部分。
10.en:
**Called.** Gr. prosagoreuō, “to greet,” “to salute,” “to name,” “to designate.” The word occurs only here in the NT. The usual word for call is kaleō, the word used in v. 4. Prosagoreuō refers to Christ’s being formally designated by God as high priest.
**High priest.** The Christian world in general is acquainted with Christ as “the Lamb of God” that “taketh away the sin of the world” (John 1:29). It is acquainted with Christ as the crucified One, who gave Himself for us that we might be saved. But not all Christians are acquainted with Christ as the high priest who ministers His blood in the sanctuary above. Yet without that ministry the plan of salvation would be ineffective. In the institution of the Passover in Egypt God commanded the Israelites not simply to slay the lamb, but to put its blood on the doorposts (see Ex. 12:7–13). So in the antitype the blood of Christ, our Passover (1 Cor. 5:7), is not simply shed, it is ministered for us in heaven above by our great High Priest, as a vital part of God’s plan to save us.
**Order of Melchisedec.** See on v. 6.

11.zh:
論到麥基洗德，我們有好些話，並且難以解明，因為你們聽不進去。

**論到麥基洗德。**或“論到他。”原文既可理解為指作者講了好多話的麥基洗德（見來第7章），也可理解為照著麥基洗德的方式作大祭司的基督。
**難以解明。**作者意識到他話題的困難之處，以及教會在這方面需要屬靈的悟性。他顯然很瞭解自己的讀者，否則他就不敢這樣對他們說了。
**聽不進去。**或“聽得遲鈍。”這種狀況使作者很難闡明他的主題。他的困難在於主題和遲鈍的聽眾兩個方面。學生的侷限就是老師的侷限。
11.en:
**Of whom.** Or, “concerning which.” The Greek may be understood either way. “Of whom” would apply to Melchisedec, concerning whom the author says many things (see ch. 7). “Concerning which” would apply to the high priesthood of Christ after the manner of Melchisedec.
**Hard to be uttered.** Or, “hard to explain.” The author realized the difficulty of his subject, and that spiritual perception was needed on the part of the church. It is evident that he was well acquainted with his readers, or he would not dare speak of them as he does.
**Dull of hearing.** Or, “slow [or “sluggish”] of hearing.” This condition makes it difficult for the author to present his subject. His difficulty is twofold: a hard subject and dull hearers. The limitation of the student is the limitation of the teacher.

26.en:
**Whose voice then shook.** Compare Ex. 19:18.
**Yet once more.** The quotation is adapted from the LXX of Haggai 2:6, 7 (see comment there). In its original setting the prophecy applied to the Temple as restored following the Babylonian captivity and to the first advent of Christ. Here it applies to the second advent (see Rev. 16:17, 18).
26.zh:
當時他的聲音震動了地，但如今他應許說：再一次我不單要震動地，還要震動天。

**當時祂的聲音震動了。**參出19:18。
**再一次我不單要。**這句話源於七十士譯本的該2:6,7（見該節註釋）。這段預言原指被擄巴比倫迴歸之後聖殿的重建和基督的第一次降臨，在本節指基督的第二次降臨（見啟16:17,18）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第780頁；《先祖與先知》第340頁；《證言》卷一第184頁；見帖後2:7-12懷愛倫註釋。

2.en:
**Looking unto Jesus.** That is, for grace and strength to overcome every difficulty and to endure unto the end. As Peter found when he essayed to walk on the wind-tossed waves of Galilee (see Matt. 14:24–32), it is dangerous to turn one’s eyes away from the Saviour, even for a moment. To keep the eye of faith fixed upon Jesus is to maintain uninterrupted contact with Him who is the source of power, Him who can strengthen us to endure and to overcome.
**Author.** Gr. archēgos, “leader,” “originator,” “founder,” “pioneer” (RSV). Archēgos is rendered “Prince” in Acts 3:15; 5:31 and “captain” in Heb. 2:10, in each instance with reference to Christ, as here. Christ is the center of the plan of salvation and the source of every Christian grace. It is He who calls fallen men out of the dismal darkness of sin and into the glorious light of the gospel. It is He who cleanses them from their previous life of sin and qualifies them to become sons and daughters of God. It is He who justifies them by His grace, by virtue of His atonement on Calvary. It is He who plants their feet on the pathway to heaven.
**Finisher.** Gr. telēiotēs, “perfecter.” The work of justification is only the beginning of the Christian experience. We are not only to lay the “foundation of repentance from dead works” but are to “go on unto perfection” (see on ch. 6:1). We are to “grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ” (2 Peter 3:18). We are to gain victory after victory over our besetting sins (see on Heb. 12:1) and to “grow up into him [Christ] in all things” (Eph. 4:15). Our characters are to be “transformed” by the renewing of our minds (Rom. 12:2). This is the work of the indwelling Christ (Gal. 2:20) as the “perfecter” of faith. This is the work of sanctification. See on Matt. 5:48.
**Our faith.** That is, faith as an active principle in our lives.
**For.** Gr. anti, “instead of,” “in return for,” “in consideration of.” Christ endured the cross in return for the joyous prospect of a universe free from sin.
**Joy.** If the meaning “in consideration of” be adopted for anti (see above under “for”), the passage may be understood as follows: Looking at the cross from a human point of view, we might say that it was faith in the future results of His suffering and death that gave Christ strength to endure the shame and ignominy of the cross. He knew that He would live to see the results “of the travail of his soul,” and was “satisfied” (Isa. 53:11). To share eternity with the ransomed of all ages and the unfallen beings of other worlds was a prospect that brought utter joy to our Lord as He suffered in Gethsemane and on the cross of Calvary. See on Matt. 5:12; James 1:2.
If the meaning “instead of” be adopted for anti (see above under “for”), the passage teaches that instead of the joy that was within His grasp, either the joy of His pre-incarnate existence or that of His incarnate existence apart from the cross, Christ chose to endure the cross.
**Endured the cross.** Christ “endured the cross” in order that we might have strength to endure in our individual conflicts with the powers of darkness. He endured the cross that He might win the crown. The Captain of our salvation was made “perfect through sufferings” (ch. 2:10), and as we learn to endure the cross we are called upon to bear we too may expect to be found perfect in Him at His coming. As a future joy inspired Christ to endure the cross, so in the difficult and trying experiences of life it is our privilege to look forward to the joy of eternity.
**Despising the shame.** Or, “disregarding the shame,” “caring nothing for the shame.” “The sufferings of this present time” are nothing in comparison with “the glory which shall be revealed” (Rom. 8:18), and are therefore to be disregarded. We may “greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be,” we “are in heaviness through manifold temptations” (1 Peter 1:6). Like Paul, we can count all earthly things but loss for the exquisite joy of knowing Christ Jesus as Lord (see Phil. 3:8).
**Is set down.** Textual evidence attests the reading “has sat down.” The form of the Greek verb of the preferred reading implies that Christ not only seated Himself at the right hand of the Father but that He has retained that position of honor ever since.
**At the right hand.** See on ch. 1:3.
2.zh:
仰望為我們信心創始成終的耶穌（或作：仰望那將真道創始成終的耶穌）。他因那擺在前面的喜樂，就輕看羞辱，忍受了十字架的苦難，便坐在神寶座的右邊。

**仰望耶穌。**為了獲得恩典和力量戰勝一切困難並忍耐到底。彼得試圖在加利利海洶湧的波浪上行走時發現（見太14:24-32），即使讓目光片時轉離救主也是很危險的。信心的眼睛要注視耶穌，不間斷地與祂保持聯絡。祂是能力的泉源，能使我們有力量忍耐並取得勝利。
**我們信心。**就是信心作為我們生活中的積極原則。
**創始。**archēgos，“領導人，”“創始者，”“奠基人，”“先驅”。Archēgos在徒3:15；5:31中譯為“君王”，在來2:10中譯為“元帥”，都是指基督，與本節一樣。基督是救恩計劃的中心，和每一種基督徒恩典的來源。祂呼召墮落的人類離開罪惡的黑暗，進入福音的榮耀光明。祂潔淨了人過去生活的罪惡，使他們有資格成為上帝的兒女。祂用祂的恩典，藉著祂在髑髏地的贖罪而使他們稱義。祂使他們的腳站在通天的道路上。
**成終。**telēiotēs，“完成者。”稱義的工作只是基督徒經驗的開始。我們不僅要“立根基，懊悔死行”，而且要“進到完全的地步”（見來6:1註釋）。我們要“在我們主救主耶穌基督的恩典和知識上有長進”（彼後3:18），要對纏累我們的罪勝了又勝（見來12:1的註釋），並“凡事長進，連於元首基督”（弗4:15）。我們的品格要藉著我們心意的更新而“改變”（羅12:2）。這是住在我們裡面的基督作為“使信心成終者”的工作（加2:20）。這是成聖的工作。見太5:48註釋。
**因。**anti，“代替，”“回報，”“鑑於。”基督看到了宇宙脫離罪惡的喜樂前景，就忍受了十字架。。
**喜樂。**如果將anti譯為“鑑於”（見上面“因”註釋），本節可以理解為：從人的角度看十字架，我們可以說，基督受難和受死時對於將來的信心，使祂有力量忍受十字架的恥辱。祂知道自己將活著看見“自己勞苦的功效”，並“心滿意足”（賽53:11）。當我們的主在客西馬尼和髑髏地的十字架上受苦時，與各世代的贖民和未曾墮落之其他世界的生靈共享永恆的前景，給他帶來了滿足的喜樂。見太5:12；雅1:2註釋。
如果將anti理解為“代替”（見上面“因”的註釋），本節經文教導的就是，基督沒有選擇祂所擁有的喜樂，就是祂道成肉身以前的喜樂，和祂道成肉身以後擺脫十字架的喜樂，而是選擇了忍受十字架。
**忍受了十字架。**基督“忍受了十字架”，是為了讓我們個人在與黑暗勢力的鬥爭中有忍受的力量。祂忍受了十字架，為了贏得冠冕。我們救恩的元帥因“受苦難得以完全”（來2:10）。當我們學會忍受我們蒙召要背的十字架時，我們也可以指望當祂來時能在祂裡面得到完全。將來的喜樂鼓舞了基督忍受十字架，同樣，我們在生活的困難和考驗的經歷中，也有權利期盼那永遠的喜樂。
**輕看羞辱。**“現在的苦楚”若比起“將來要顯於我們的榮耀”就算不得什麼了（羅8:18），所以就不足介意了。我們可以“大有喜樂，雖然如今在百般的試煉中暫時憂愁”（彼前1:6）。我們可以像保羅一樣，把世上的萬事都當作有損的，為要以認識主基督耶穌為至寶（見腓3:8）。
**便坐在。**原文動詞的形式暗示基督不僅坐在天父的右邊，而且從那時起一直坐在那裡。
**右邊。**見來1:3註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第299，320頁；《文字佈道》第114頁；《給管家的勉言》第213頁；《安息日學訓言》第17頁；《歷代願望》第523，659頁；《佈道論》第645頁；《基督教育原理》第383頁；《傳道良助》第28頁；《服務真詮》第504頁；《今日的生活》第99，105，176頁；《醫療佈道論》第21，41，99頁；《給青年人的信息》第104頁；《先知與君王》第172頁；《餘民教會》58頁；《拾級就主》第69，77頁；《成聖的人生》第56頁；《證言》卷二第115，491，686頁；《證言》卷三第387，432頁；《證言》卷四第54，147，366，375，461，583，615頁；《證言》卷五第199，385，744頁；《證言》卷六第335，449，472頁；《證言》卷七第94頁；《證言》卷八第209，210頁；《證言》卷九第59頁；《論福利工作》第49頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–3節）**。《使徒行述》第465頁；《早期著作》第114頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–4節）**。《證言》卷二第709頁。

6.en:
**Whom the Lord loveth.** Patient, persistent discipline is an expression of solicitous affection. Experiences designed to ennoble and perfect character constitute the best evidence that the Lord loves us. Whether it be a child, or an adult Christian, discipline is essential to character.
**Scourgeth.** God administers whatever discipline may be required for the formation of character, or permits experiences that will accomplish this objective (see on v. 5). However, the statement is not to be pressed too literally, as if God personally or directly authorized or ordered the suffering and sorrow that attend some of the disciplinary experiences of life. See on v. 5.
**Every son.** For our relationship to God as sons of a heavenly Father see on Matt. 6:9; 1 John 3:1.
**Whom he receiveth.** That is, every one whom He receives as a son. Every son of God from this earth has become such by adoption into the heavenly family.
6.zh:
因為主所愛的，他必管教，又鞭打凡所收納的兒子。

**主所愛的。**忍耐和持久的管教表現出牽掛之情。使我們品格高尚和完善的經驗乃是上帝愛我們的最好憑據。無論是孩童還是成人的基督徒，管教對於品格來說都是不可少的。
**鞭打。**上帝實施陶冶品格所必需的各種管教，允許以此為目的的經驗臨到（見第5節註釋）。但不要太按字面解釋這句話，似乎是上帝親自或直接授權或命定了伴隨著某些管教性生活經驗的苦難與悲傷。見第5節註釋。
**所收納的。**就是祂所接納為兒子的每一個人。世上的每一個上帝兒女都是通過被接進天上的家庭而成為祂兒子的。
**兒子。**我們與上帝的關係，就像天父的兒子那樣，見太6:9；約壹3:1註釋。

17.en:
**Would have.** That is, “desired to.”
**Rejected.** Gr. apodokimazō, “to reject [after testing, because of failure to measure up to required standards].” For the record of the incident here referred to see Gen. 27:1–40.
**No place of repentance.** Long years of living for earthly pursuits had deprived Esau of the capacity to bear the more serious responsibilities of life. By his own choice his mind and character had become fixed. The writer of Hebrews does not imply that Esau actually desired to repent of his worldly ways, but simply that he repented of having sold his birthright. He wished he had it back again, but realized that his decision was irrevocable. He had lost it forever. No arbitrary act of God kept Esau from receiving the inheritance that would normally have been his. His own character disqualified him for its privileges and responsibilities.
**With tears.** When Esau realized what he had lost “he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry” (Gen. 27:34).
17.zh:
後來想要承受父所祝的福，竟被棄絕，雖然號哭切求，卻得不著門路使他父親的心意回轉。這是你們知道的。

**想要。**就是“想得到。”
**被棄絕。**apodokimazō，“（經考驗後，因達不到所要求的標準而遭）拒絕。”關於這裡所提到的事件，見創27:1-40。
**號哭。**當以掃意識到自己的損失時，“就放聲痛哭”（創27:34）。
**得不著門路使他心意回轉。**多年追求世俗的生活使以掃無法承擔更為嚴肅的生活責任。因他自己的選擇，他的思想和品格已經固定了。《希伯來書》的作者並沒有暗示以掃真地願意改變他世俗的生活方式，只是說他後悔賣掉長子的名分。他想重新得回，卻意識到他的決定是不可改變了。他已經永遠失去了長子權。上帝使以掃得不到通常該由他來承受的產業，並非武斷之舉。以掃自己的品格使他喪失了產業的特權和責任。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷二第39頁。

9.en:
**Furthermore.** There is a further point of comparison between earthly parental discipline and that of our heavenly Father.
**Fathers of our flesh.** That is, earthly fathers.
**Gave them reverence.** Or, “respected them.” This is the opposite of despising them (see on v. 5). Respect for duly constituted authority, whether it be that of the home, of society, or of God, is basic to peace, harmony, and security.
**Be in subjection.** Or, “submit.” Should we not recognize, appreciate, and benefit by the discipline of the Lord? Should we be less receptive to the discipline of our heavenly Parent than children should be to their earthly parents?
**Spirits.** Gr. pneumata, “living beings,” or, possibly, “life” (see on Luke 8:55). “Father of spirits” refers to God as the source of all life and being. This expression stands in contrast with “fathers of our flesh,” as Heb. 12:10 makes evident. The argument is from the lesser to the greater: if we respect the discipline of an earthly father, to whom we owe our bodily existence, how much more should we “be in subjection” to—or “reverence”—the correction of our heavenly Father, to whom we owe life itself?
The word “spirits” stands in contrast with the word “flesh.” Both refer to living human beings, as the context and the Greek construction make clear. The entire context deals with the way in which God, as our heavenly Father, chastens His earthborn children. The Greek reads literally, “the spirits,” which in idiomatic Greek is equivalent to “our spirits.”
9.zh:
再者，我們曾有生身的父管教我們，我們尚且敬重他，何況萬靈的父，我們豈不更當順服他得生嗎？

**再者。**進一步在地上父母的管教和我們天父的管教之間進行對比。
**生身的父。**就是地上的父親。
**敬重他們。**與輕看他們相反（見第5節註釋）。尊敬包含著義務的權威，不論是家裡的，社會上，還是屬於上帝的，都是平安，和諧與安全的基礎。
**萬靈。**pneumata，“生靈”或“生命”（見路8:55註釋）。“萬靈的父”指一切生命和生靈之源上帝。這個稱呼與“我們生身的父”形成了對比，正如來12:10所證明的。論據是從小到大的。我們既敬重生身的父親，對於賜生命的天父，我們豈不更應“順服”或“敬重” 祂的管教嗎？
“萬靈”與“生身”形成了對比。二者都是指人類，正如原文結構所表明的。上下文都涉及我們的天父上帝管教祂地上兒女的方法。
**順服。**我們難道不應該承認，感激、受益於主的管教嗎？我們難道接受我們天父的管教比兒童接受地上父母的管教更少嗎？

16.en:
**Fornicator.** Or, “immoral person.”
**Profane.** Gr. bebēlos, “worldly,” “godless,” “irreligious.” In the NT bebēlos describes a person who has no appreciation of, or desire for, sacred things, one whose desires and ambitions rise no higher than the things of this earth.
**Esau.** For comment on the character of Esau and on the incident here referred to see on Gen. 25:27–34.
**One morsel.** Or, “one meal.”
**Birthright.** For comment on the significance of the birthright see on Gen. 25:31.
16.zh:
恐怕有淫亂的，有貪戀世俗如以掃的，他因一點食物把自己長子的名分賣了。

**淫亂。**或“不道德的人。”
**貪戀世俗。**bebēlos，“世俗，”“不敬虔，”“沒有信仰。”在《新約》中bebēlos形容不欣賞不仰慕神聖事物的人，一個願望和志向只限於今生事物的人。
**以掃。**關於以掃的品格和這裡所提到的事件，見創25:27-34註釋。
**一點食物。**或“一餐飯。”
**長子的名分。**關於長子名分的意義，見創25:31註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第110頁；《給管家的勉言》第139頁；《證言》卷二第38頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–17節）**。《先祖與先知》第181頁；見創25:29-30懷愛倫註釋。

7.en:
**If ye endure chastening.** See on vs. 3, 5. Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the reading “endure unto chastening.” According to this reading these words constitute an imperative sentence, an admonition based on the principle stated in v. 6. Too often we pray for victory over particular sins, only to find that God answers our prayers by permitting circumstances that will develop strength at the very points where we are weak. Let us recognize God’s answer to our prayers, and not falter. Let us courageously and submissively “endure unto chastening.”
**As with sons.** Parents are usually reluctant to administer discipline to children not their own, but a wise parent does not hesitate to discipline his own children when they need it. Discipline is the prerogative, duty, and responsibility of parents. Thus, in a sense, the administration of discipline is evidence of parenthood.
**What son?** No child is born with a mature character, and every child therefore needs discipline in order that he may fill a useful place in the world and be a credit to the family.
7.zh:
你們所忍受的，是神管教你們，待你們如同待兒子。焉有兒子不被父親管教的呢？

**你們所忍受的……管教。**見第3,5節註釋。有文本為祈使句，是基於第6節原則的勸勉。我們往往為克服特定的罪祈禱，結果發現上帝回答我們的禱告是藉著在我們的弱點上賜予力量的環境臨到。但願我們認識到上帝應允了我們的禱告，不要猶豫。讓我們勇敢而順從地“忍受……管教。”
**如同待兒子。**父母通常不會管教別人的孩子，但明智的父母會毫不猶豫地在需要的時候管教自己的兒女。管教是父母的特權，義務和責任。因此從某種意義說，管教是父母身份的證據。
**焉有兒子。**沒有一個孩子生下來就有成熟的品格，所以每一個孩子都需要管教，以便在世上成為有用之人和家庭的榮譽。

1.zh:
我們既有這許多的見證人，如同雲彩圍著我們，就當放下各樣的重擔，脫去容易纏累我們的罪，存心忍耐，奔那擺在我們前頭的路程，

**我們既有。**來12:1,2是作者對來11章的總結。把章劃分在來12章的第2節和第3節之間更為合適。
**這許多見證人。**第1節的比喻將基督徒設想成一個在古時的運動場上為賽跑作最後準備的運動員。有觀眾坐在周圍的椅子上，一排高過一排。想要獲勝的運動員掃視一下週圍雲彩般的觀眾。本節的“見證人”是指第11章中所提到的無數信心英雄。他們每一個人都克服了一切障礙和困難，快樂地完成了自己的賽程。他們的忠誠和忍耐給他們的人生賽跑帶來了勝利。這位基督徒運動員意識到歷代忠心之人的眼目似乎都盯著他看，他就有了強烈的願望，要盡一切努力贏得這場他註定要參加的比賽。
希臘的運動競賽早已在地中海各地普及。來12:1的比喻是每一位讀者所熟悉的。《希伯來書》的作者經常用競賽作為比喻，來說明他在外邦人中傳道的生涯（加2:2；腓2:16；提後4:7），或像在本節那樣，說明基督徒的生活經驗（見林前9:24-27）。
**圍著。**在聖史中我們可以看到許多以信心和忠心戰勝一切障礙的“見證人”。
**重擔。**ogkos，“擔子，”“障礙，”這裡指障礙。在第1節的比喻中，ogkos指多餘的重量，如可能妨礙賽跑者的衣物。有信心的人會毫不猶豫地拋棄妨礙他們達到目標的任何事物。
作者讓讀者自己去發現妨礙他作為基督徒賽手前進的事物。在這場賽跑中，每一個參賽者都可以獲得勝利，因為他不是與別人競爭，而是與自己競爭。他不必勝過他的競爭者，或超越以前的參賽者所達到的水準。他唯一的競爭對手就是自我；唯一的要求就是要他在與自我的鬥爭中運用信心和忍耐，靠著基督的恩典，克服每一個“重擔”，就是一切罪惡的傾向。
**罪。**每一個人都有纏累的罪，邪惡的傾向，阻礙他參加賽跑。當他克服了某一種罪惡的傾向時，就有另一種罪惡的傾向取而代之想要掌權。得救的道路就這樣要經歷一個又一個的戰鬥。但是每一個基督徒都有權利在這條道路上步步獲勝。無論罪惡多麼容易纏累我們，我們都應象古時的賽跑者那樣把自己飄拂的衣袍放在一邊，束上腰參賽。
**容易纏累。**或“容易分心。”有人認為該詞原意為“緊緊依附。”無論一種罪依附得多麼緊密，分離的過程多麼痛苦，若要在人生的賽跑中獲勝，都必須予以拋棄。
**忍耐。**hupomonē，或“堅強，”“堅定，”“剛毅。”基督徒的賽跑是終生的經驗，所以要求在一連串的困難和失望面前堅持和忍耐，耐心等候賽程終點的獎賞。《希伯來書》一再出現要人忍耐的勸勉（見來3:6；4:14；6:1,11,12；10:23,36-39等）。
**路程。**就是基督徒的賽程，發展品格的經驗。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第449頁；《基督教育原理》第134頁；《證言》卷二第517頁；《證言》卷三第43頁；《證言》卷五第83頁；《證言》卷九第136頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《使徒行述》第312頁；《基督教育原理》第402頁；《證言》卷二第358頁；《證言》卷四第35頁。
1.en:
**Wherefore.** Chapter 12:1, 2 constitutes the writer’s conclusion to ch. 11. A chapter division, if any, would preferably occur between vs. 2 and 3 of ch. 12.
**Compassed.** Or, “surrounded.” Wherever we turn in sacred history we find “witnesses” to the principle that faith and faithfulness triumph over every obstacle.
**Cloud of witnesses.** Or, “host of witnesses.” The metaphor of v. 1 imagines the Christian to be an athlete making final preparations to run a race in an ancient stadium, with the spectators seated on benches rising tier above tier on all sides. The athlete, intent upon winning the race, glances momentarily at the mass of faces that surrounds him like a cloud. Here, the “witnesses” are the uncounted worthies of faith mentioned in ch. 11, each of whom, despite handicaps and hindrances of every kind, finished his course with joy. Their faithfulness and endurance brought them victory in the race of life. Conscious that the eyes of the faithful of all ages are now intently fixed upon him, as it were, the Christian athlete experiences an urgent impulse to put forth every effort to win the race that has been marked out for him.
Greek athletic contests had long been popular throughout the Mediterranean world, and the illustration of ch. 12:1 would be familiar to every reader. The writer of Hebrews often makes figurative use of the race to represent his career as missionary to the Gentiles (Gal. 2:2; Phil. 2:16; 2 Tim. 4:7) or, as here, to represent the life experience of the Christian (see 1 Cor. 9:24–27).
**Weight.** Gr. ogkos, “weight,” “burden,” “impediment,” here in the latter sense. In the metaphor of v. 1 ogkos refers to the weight of anything superfluous, such as clothing, which might tend to hinder, or handicap, the runner. Men who are motivated by faith will not hesitate to dispose of anything and everything that might keep them from achieving their goal.
The writer leaves it to each reader to discover what may be hampering his progress as a Christian runner. In this race every entrant may win, for he is not competing with others, but with himself. He is not required to excel his competitors or to surpass a mark made by some previous contestant. Self is his only competitor, and the only requirement is that he exercise faithfulness and patience in his contest with self, and, by the grace of Christ, overcome every “weight”—every tendency to evil.
**The sin.** Every man has some besetting sin, some tendency to evil that seeks to impede him as he runs the race. When he gains the victory over that particular evil propensity, another takes its place and presses for the mastery. Thus the pathway of salvation is beset by one battle after another. But it is every Christian’s privilege to achieve victory each step of the way. Whatever may be the sin that so easily besets us, we are to lay it aside like an ancient runner laying aside his flowing robes and girding himself for the race.
**Easily beset.** Or, “easily distract.” Some suggest that “close clinging” may have been the original reading. However close a sin may cling and however painful the process of separation may be, it must be laid aside if victory in the race of life is to be attained.
**Patience.** Gr. hupomonē, “patience,” “endurance,” “fortitude,” “steadfastness,” “perseverance.” Because the Christian race is a lifelong experience, it calls for patience and perseverance—perseverance in the face of successive difficulties and disappointments and patience to await the reward at the end of the course. Admonitions to patient endurance occur again and again in the book of Hebrews (see chs. 3:6; 4:14; 6:1, 11, 12; 10:23, 36–39; etc.).
**The race.** That is, the Christian race, the experiences by means of which character is developed.

3.zh:
那忍受罪人這樣頂撞的，你們要思想，免得疲倦灰心。

**忍受。**見第1節註釋。
**頂撞。**或“敵意。”基督在地上服務的時候，祭司和官長、文士和法利賽人的敵意步步追隨著祂的腳蹤。最後公眾都轉過來反對祂，祂自己的同胞也要流祂的血。罪人所累積的敵意以其殘暴智慧的全部力量來對付受難者的大君。
**要思想。**第3-11節涉及上帝教育的性質，目的和結果。沒有一個基督徒蒙召經受比基督更為嚴格的訓練。通過思考祂應付考驗和試探的方法，我們就能避免疲倦灰心。基督既已忍受，我們靠著祂的恩典也能忍受。
**免得疲倦。**瞻仰基督所揹負的重擔，我們就會覺得自己的擔輕省多了（見太11:28-30）。如果我們單單仰望耶穌，思考祂所忍受的苦，我們所遭遇的一切困難和失望都會比較容易忍受了。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第701頁；《證言》卷三第434頁；見來2:14懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–4節）**。《證言》卷五第597頁。
3.en:
**Consider him.** Verses 3–11 deal with the nature, purpose, and results of divine discipline. No Christian is called to undergo a more strict course of discipline than Christ was. By considering the way in which He met trials and temptations we can avoid growing weary or fainthearted. Christ endured, and by His grace we too may endure.
**Endured.** See on v. 1.
**Contradiction.** Or, “hostility.” The hostility of priests and rulers, scribes and Pharisees, dogged the footsteps of Christ throughout His earthly ministry. Eventually, the tide of popularity turned against Him, and His own people demanded His life blood. The cumulative hostility of a race of sinners was turned with the full force of diabolical ingenuity on the Prince of sufferers.
**Lest ye be wearied.** A glance at the burden Christ bore will make our burdens seem light by comparison (see Matt. 11:28–30). If we will only look unto Jesus and consider what He endured, every difficulty and disappointment we meet will be easier to bear.

4.zh:
你們與罪惡相爭，還沒有抵擋到流血的地步。

**抵擋到流血的地步。**就是到死亡的地步。本節對第1節和第2節的比喻稍作改變。基督徒仍在賽場上，有“許多的見證人，如同雲彩”注視著他，但他現在有了一個敵手，要和他進行殊死的較量。基督徒還沒有經歷惡者對他的全部襲擊；他也不要以為自己在與罪惡作鬥爭中所受的苦超過了上帝理當要他受的（見林前10:13）。但他在解脫纏累他的罪時，蒙召要用堅定的信心抵擋試探。他在對付敵手的殊死戰鬥中也要用堅定的信心。
基督曾與黑暗的權勢曾作這樣的鬥爭，其高潮是在客西馬尼園和十字架上。殉道者們也曾“抵擋到了流血的地步。”但是《希伯來書》的讀者還沒有蒙召去應付基督和殉道者們所對付的試煉。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五第222頁；見來4:15懷愛倫註釋；太4:1-11。
4.en:
**Resisted unto blood.** That is, unto death. Here the metaphor of vs. 1 and 2 changes slightly. The Christian is still in the arena with the figurative “cloud of witnesses” gazing intently at him, but now he is confronted by an antagonist waiting to engage him in mortal combat. The Christian has not yet experienced all that the evil one can bring against him, nor should he think that he is suffering more in his struggle with sin than God can rightfully expect of him (see 1 Cor. 10:13). Nevertheless, in disentangling himself from his besetting sin he is called upon to resist temptation with all the resolute firmness that he would employ in meeting an antagonist in mortal combat.
Christ once engaged in such combat with the powers of darkness, a combat that reached its climax in Gethsemane and on the cross. The martyrs likewise “resisted unto blood.” But those to whom the book of Hebrews was written had not as yet been called upon to meet what Christ and the martyrs had met.

5.zh:
你們又忘了那勸你們如同勸兒子的話，說：我兒，你不可輕看主的管教，被他責備的時候也不可灰心；

**你們又忘了。**原文既可被視為疑問句，也可視為陳述句。疑問句似乎更有力而又不那麼嚴厲。一個受管教的孩童可能認識到自己受懲罰是對的，他該受懲罰，但他可能認識不到那是出於愛心的管教。基督徒往往容易疏忽艱難經歷的管教價值，而這種忽視使他們得不到本來可以學到的寶貴教訓。他們往往不滿上帝允許這樣的經歷臨到，並抱怨自己的命運。
**勸。**paraklēsis，“鼓勵，”“勸勉，”“安慰。”關於paraklēsis及其相關詞，見太5:4；約14:16註釋。
**如同勸。**第5,6節引自箴3:11,12。
**兒子。**5-11節的教誨集中在父子關係上，最後強調父親希望兒子學到某些成功的生活所必需的教訓。
**我兒。**這是本節所引《箴言》中常見的稱呼，暗示一位慈父的關懷。
**輕看。**oligōreō，就是不當回事。管教的目的是要產生一種印象。管教如果不產生印象就沒有益處。
**主的。**要不是主的許可，沒有什麼事情會臨到我們。從這個意義上說，生活的經驗都是“主的”。上帝決不是苦難和悲傷的創始者，但祂有時會允許我們經歷苦難。見代下18:18；伯42:5；詩38:3；39:9註釋。
**管教。**paideia，“教養，”“訓練，”“教育，”“管教，”“糾正”（見弗6:4註釋），源於paidion（“孩子”）。管教是一種訓練，為了糾正，陶冶，加強並完善品格。該詞往往侷限於懲罰的狹義。其實管教是一門教育學生的藝術，因為學生是接受某種教育或訓練的人。paideia含有補救，處罰或懲戒的意思。Paideia指預備孩子們承擔成人生活的各項職責的整個過程。
**責備。**elegchō，或“糾正，”“懲罰，”“管教。”受責備或管教決不是愉快的事情，更不用說受懲罰了。所以輕看責備是很自然的反應。迴避責備的方便之法就是躲開。但聰明的態度則是從中獲益。
**灰心。**ekluō，“厭倦，”“疲倦，”“喪失勇氣。”一個灰心的門徒絕對無法從經驗的學校中畢業。凡喪失勇氣想要放棄的人，都受到邀請將自己的視線轉向耶穌並“思想祂”（見第2,3節註釋）。最重要的是要記得上帝並沒有生他的氣，而是像一位慈父親那樣地愛他，設法幫助他學到一個非常需要的教訓。使人生艱難的，往往不是管教本身，而是人對待它的態度。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《福山寶訓》第11頁。
5.en:
**Ye have forgotten.** The Greek may be taken either as a question or as a statement. A question would seem to be more forceful and at the same time less severe. A child undergoing discipline may realize that his chastisement is just and that he deserves it, but he may not realize that it is administered in love. Too often Christians are prone to overlook the disciplinary value of difficult experiences, and this carelessness deprives them of precious lessons they might otherwise learn. Too often they resent the fact that God permits such experiences to come upon them and complain about their lot.
**Exhortation.** Gr. paraklēsis, “encouragement,” “exhortation,” “consolation.” For comment on paraklēsis and related words see on Matt. 5:4; John 14:16.
**Which speaketh.** The quotation in vs. 5, 6 is from Prov. 3:11, 12.
**Children.** Literally, “sons.” The line of instruction contained in vs. 5–11 centers in the father-son relationship and comes to a focus on the desire of the father that his son shall learn certain lessons necessary to his success in life.
**My son.** A form of address common in the book of Proverbs, whence the quotation is taken. It implies the solicitude of a loving father.
**Despise.** Gr. oligōreō, “to think lightly of,” “to make light of [something],” that is, to fail to take it seriously. The purpose of discipline is to make an impression. Discipline that makes little or no impression has served no useful purpose.
**Chastening.** Gr. paideia, “upbringing,” “training,” “instruction,” “discipline,” “correction” (see on Eph. 6:4), from paidion, “child.” Discipline is training that corrects, molds, strengthens, and perfects character. Too often the word is restricted to the narrower meaning of punishment or chastisement. Discipline has been defined as the fine art of making disciples, inasmuch as a disciple is one who submits himself to a particular pattern of discipline, or training. The Greek word paideia may include, but does not specifically denote, remedial discipline, as implied in the words punishment or chastening. Paideia refers to the entire process by which children are prepared for the responsibilities of adult life.
**Of the Lord.** The experiences of life are all “of the Lord” in the sense that nothing can happen to us except by His permission. God is never the author of suffering and sorrow, though He may, at times, permit us to experience them. See on 2 Chron. 18:18; Job 42:5; Ps. 38:3; 39:9.
**Faint.** Gr. ekluō, “to become weary,” “to give out,” “to lose courage.” A faint disciple will never graduate from the school of experience. He who loses courage and feels like giving up is invited to turn his eyes unto Jesus and “consider him” (see on vs. 2, 3). Above all else, he should remember that God is not angry with him, but loves him like a devoted father and is attempting to help him learn a much-needed lesson. Often it is not the discipline itself, but one’s attitude toward it, that makes life difficult.
**Rebuked.** Gr. elegchō, “to reprove,” “to correct,” “to punish,” “to discipline.” It is never pleasant to be reproved or corrected, much less to undergo punishment. The natural reaction is to despise it. The easy way of escape is to faint before it. The wise attitude is to profit from it.

8.zh:
管教原是眾子所共受的，你們若不受管教，就是私子，不是兒子了。

**不受管教。**不接受管教的孩子正在預備履行人生各項職責的工作上受到誤導。凡不對兒女進行必要管教的父母必有一日要向上帝嚴肅地交帳。我們的天父如果不管教我們，不讓我們經受具有管教價值的環境，那就既不公平也不公正。
**私子。**或“非婚生兒女。”
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第632頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–11節）**。《證言》卷五第683頁。
8.en:
**Without chastisement.** Children who do not receive discipline are being cheated of the very preparation they need for the duties and responsibilities of life. Parents who withhold needed discipline will one day have a fearful account to render to God. It would not be either fair or just for our heavenly Father to fail to discipline us, or to protect us from circumstances and situations that have disciplinary value.
**Bastards.** Or, “illegitimate children.”

10.zh:
生身的父都是暫隨己意管教我們；惟有萬靈的父管教我們，是要我們得益處，使我們在他的聖潔上有分。

**暫。**就是在青少年時期。我們的天父一生都不斷地管教我們。
**隨己意。**“按照他們所認為最好的。”
**管教。**“訓練”或“糾正”（見第5節註釋）。
**要我們得益處。**我們生身的父母在管教我們時可能會因錯誤的判斷或自私的情緒而出錯，“我們尚且敬重他”。我們難道不更應聽從並感激我們天父的管教嗎？祂的智慧和慈愛全是為了我們的益處。
**在祂的聖潔上有份。**上帝一切管教的目的都是為了品格的改變。其目標就是完全（見太5:48註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《福山寶訓》第10頁；《今日的生活》第292頁；《證言》卷五第742頁。
10.en:
**For a few days.** That is, during childhood and youth. Our heavenly Father’s chastening continues throughout life.
**Chastened.** Or, “disciplined” or, “corrected” (see on v. 5).
**After their own pleasure.** Or, “as seemed [good] to them,” that is, as they deemed best.
**For our profit.** That is, for our good. Our earthly parents may have erred in discipline because of defective judgment or selfish emotions, yet “we gave them reverence.” How much the more should we heed and appreciate the discipline of our heavenly Father, whose wisdom and love ordain only what is for our good?
**Partakers of his holiness.** The objective of all divine discipline is character transformation. Perfection is its goal (see on Matt. 5:48).

11.zh:
凡管教的事，當時不覺得快樂，反覺得愁苦；後來卻為那經練過的人結出平安的果子，就是義。

**凡管教的事。**或“凡與訓練有關的事”（見第5節註釋）。
**當時。**充分理解所受到的管教通常是需要時間和經驗的。只有當青少年長大以後，才可能認識到他們的父母，老師和朋友對他們品格的發展所作的貢獻。事實上這種認識乃是成熟的標誌。成熟的基督徒在經歷了各種人生的經歷之後，才會理解其管教價值。他認識到埋怨上帝的管教乃是幼稚和不成熟的表現。
**快樂。**或“愉快”。
**愁苦。**不是指嚴厲，緊張或壓抑，而是指引起悲傷和痛苦。
**後來。**牲畜一般只為眼前而活著。智能生靈的一個顯著特徵就是能夠通過回憶和想象，考慮自己的過去和將來，根據歷史和經驗，對目前的狀況進行評估，並且聰明地作出決定，採取行動。一個人能根據過去和將來觀察現在，證明他已經從童年發育到成熟的階段。基督徒的成長也是如此，特別涉及生活中的管教性經驗。那些已經學會用永恆的眼光審視今生事物的基督徒是有福的。
**經練過。**那些接受生活經驗中管教的人，有特權享受“平安的果子”。它是從順從上帝所啟示之旨意的樹上結出來的。
**結出。**如果接受管教，就一定會結出“平安的果子”；如果埋怨管教，結果子就少；如果拒絕管教，就決不會結果子。
**就是義。**當天然的傾向和慾望與正確的原則發生衝突時，就需要進行管教。管教的目的是要解決矛盾，讓天然的傾向和慾望與原則相和諧。這樣作，管教就會帶來平安。經受管教的人發現自己與上帝、與自己、與同胞都能和諧相處。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第119頁；《今日的生活》第93頁；《先祖與先知》第238頁；《證言》卷三第416頁。
11.en:
**No chastening.** Or, “no discipline” (see on v. 5).
**For the present.** The perspective of time and experience is usually necessary to a full appreciation of discipline received. Only after children and youth reach maturity are they likely to realize all that parents, teachers, and friends have contributed toward their development of character. In fact, such appreciation is one sure mark of maturity. The mature Christian appreciates the disciplinary value of the various experiences of his life while he is passing through them. He realizes that resentment at divine discipline is a mark of childishness and immaturity.
**Joyous.** Or, “pleasant” (RSV).
**Grievous.** Not in the sense of being severe, intense, or oppressive, but of causing grief, suffering, or pain.
**Afterward.** Generally speaking, the brute creation lives only in the present and for the present. It is one of the distinguishing characteristics of intelligent beings to be able to project themselves into the past or into the future, by means of memory and imagination. It is thus possible for them to form an estimate of their present situation in the perspective of time and experience, and to decide and act intelligently. The degree to which a person is able to view the present in terms of the past and the future, and does so, is a remarkably accurate measure of his progress from childhood to maturity. The same is true of Christian maturity, particularly with respect to the disciplinary experiences of life. Happy are those Christians who have learned to weigh the things of time in the light of eternity.
**It yieldeth.** Discipline bears “the peaceable fruit” always if it is accepted, seldom if it is resented, never if it is rejected.
**Fruit of righteousness.** Discipline becomes necessary when a conflict arises between the natural tendencies and desires on the one hand, and right principle on the other hand. The purpose of discipline is to resolve that conflict by bringing the natural tendencies and desires into harmony with principle. In so doing, discipline brings peace. The person undergoing discipline finds himself at peace with God, with himself, and with his fellow men.
**Exercised.** Or, “trained.” Those who accept the training provided by the disciplinary experiences of life are privileged to enjoy “the peaceable fruit of righteousness” that grows on the tree of obedience to the revealed will of God.

12.zh:
所以，你們要把下垂的手、發酸的腿、挺起來；

**所以。**鑑於人生的管教經歷是由智慧慈愛的天父所安排的，為了使我們在生活中結出“平安的義果”，達到成熟。
**下垂的。**就是灰心失望。
**手。**這是希臘慣習語，意為“你們的手。”參第13節“自己的腳”。
**發酸的腿。**發酸的腿不利於基督徒的賽跑（見第1,2節註釋）。
**挺起來。**下垂的手和發酸的腿象徵灰心和怠惰，與“忍耐”相反（見第2節註釋）。成熟的基督徒在經受管教時不會“疲倦灰心”（第3節）；他的手不會下垂，他的腿也不會發酸。他既明白管教的性質和目的，相信天父的智慧和良善，就不會埋怨，灰心和怠惰。他必以勇氣和信心執行他的任務。
太多的基督徒有“發酸的腿”和“下垂的手”。他們不接受上天的管教，卻因自己的不利環境而責怪別人。他們拒絕天父所提供發展品格的機會。不久他們的生活就結出愛爭吵的苦果（見第13,15節註釋），而不是“平安的義果”（第11節）。參賽35:3。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》第496頁；《證言》卷四第131頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–13節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第184頁；見加6:1，2懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–15節）**。《證言》卷八第79頁。
12.en:
**Wherefore.** That is, in view of the fact that the disciplinary experiences of life have been ordained by a wise and loving heavenly Father for the purpose of bringing “the peaceable fruit of righteousness” to maturity in our lives.
**Lift up.** Drooping hands and weak knees typify discouragement and inactivity. They represent the antithesis of endurance (see on v. 2). The mature Christian will not become “wearied and faint” in his mind (v. 3) when passing through discipline; his hands will not droop and his knees will not falter. Understanding something of the nature and purpose of the discipline and having confidence in the wisdom and goodness of his heavenly Father, he will banish resentment, discouragement, and inaction. He will go about his tasks with courage and confidence.
Too many Christians have “feeble knees” and hands that “hang down.” Instead of accepting Heaven’s discipline they begin to blame others for the unfavorable circumstances in which they find themselves. They refuse the opportunity for character development provided by their heavenly Father. Soon their lives begin to bear the contentious fruit of bitterness (see on vs. 13, 15) instead of “the peaceable fruit of righteousness” (v. 11). Compare Isa. 35:3.
**The hands.** Here, idiomatic Greek meaning “your hands.” Compare “your feet” in v. 13.
**Hang down.** That is, in disappointment and discouragement.
**Feeble knees.** Weak knees are not an asset in the Christian race (see on vs. 1, 2).

13.zh:
也要為自己的腳，把道路修直了，使瘸子不致歪腳（或作：差路），反得痊癒。

**把道路修直了。**不肯接受生活的管教往往會使一個人走彎路。成熟的基督徒會努力走直路，勇敢而充滿信心地接受那造就勻衡的基督徒品格所需要的管教性經驗，既不猶豫也不後悔。他不會尋求避免管教的旁門左路，而會遵循人生的大道，充分利用它所提供的機會。
**瘸子。**還是指手下垂腿發酸，需要為自己的腳“把道路修直”的人（第12,13節）。他們既為“瘸子”，就難以經歷生命路程中不愉快的管教。
**不至歪腳。**ektrepō，“歪腳”或“走差路。”不很清楚ektrepō在本節指什麼。兩種解釋都有可能：一，瘸腳的人會“走差路”，從“直路”走入彎“路”，致使他們更容易絆跌。二，Ektrepō按醫學術語理解為“脫臼”。瘸腿使行走困難；脫了臼就無法走路了。如果這樣理解，那就是警告說，如果不讓瘸子走“直路”，他們就有脫臼的危險。第二種意義“脫臼”或更符合上下文。比起“走差路”，“瘸子”更有可能脫臼。況且“反得痊癒”的告誡更適合於脫臼而不是走差路。
**反得痊癒。**不願接受管教會會使人陷入更大的困難。但智慧的基督徒不會這樣，反而會著手進行適當的補救。身體的疾病如果沒有得到必要的關注，往往就會惡化而不是好轉。心理的病態，例如不願接受管教或抱有怨恨，若不以聰明的努力進行診斷並予以適當的治療，也一定會惡化。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第575頁；《文字佈道》第150頁；《給管家的勉言》第256頁；《安息日學訓言》第13頁；《對作者和編輯的勉言》第174頁；《佈道論》第366，404，590頁；《基督教育原理》第222頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第327頁；《給青年人的信息》第32頁；《給傳道人的證言》第219，229，406，468頁；《證言》卷三第441頁；《證言》卷四第400頁；《證言》卷五第348，518頁；《證言》卷七第130，238頁；《證言》卷八第196，212頁；《證言》卷九第266頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–15節）**。《證言》卷七第184頁。
13.en:
**Straight paths.** Reluctance to accept the discipline of life often leads a person into devious paths. The mature Christian will press forward in a straight path, courageously and confidently accepting the disciplinary experiences that are necessary to the formation of a symmetrical Christian character, without hesitation and without regret. He will not seek some bypath to avoid discipline, but will keep to the highway of life and take full advantage of the opportunities it offers.
**That which is lame.** Reference is still to the persons with limp hands, weak knees, and feet in need of “straight paths” (vs. 12, 13). Being “lame,” they find it difficult to walk through the unpleasant disciplinary experiences along the highway of life.
**Be turned out of the way.** Gr. ektrepō, “to turn,” “to turn away.” The sense in which ektrepō is here used is not altogether clear. Either of two interpretations is possible: (1) Lame feet will be “turned out of the way”; that is, they will stray from “straight” into crooked “paths,” where lame persons would be more likely to stumble and fall. (2) Ektrepō is to be understood in its technical medical sense, “to be dislocated,” “to be put out of joint.” Lameness would make walking difficult; dislocation would make it impossible. Understood thus, the warning would be that unless “straight paths” are provided for lame feet there is danger that dislocation of the joints will result. The second sense, “be dislocated,” or “be put out of joint,” accords more closely with the context. There is more likelihood that “that which is lame” will get out of joint than that it will stray. Furthermore, the admonition “let it rather be healed” forms a more appropriate alternative to getting out of joint than it does to going astray.
**Let it rather be healed.** Reluctance to accept discipline will get him into even greater difficulty. But instead of permitting this, the wise Christian will set about applying the appropriate remedy. When physical ailments are not given the attention they need they often tend to become worse rather than better. Conditions of mind and heart, such as reluctance to accept discipline, or resentment because of it, are sure to become aggravated unless intelligent effort is put forth to diagnose the situation and to apply the appropriate remedy.

14.zh:
你們要追求與眾人和睦，並要追求聖潔；非聖潔沒有人能見主。

**追求與眾人和睦。**作者現在從基督徒的個人問題，轉到基督徒與同胞的關係。關於“追求……和睦”的勸勉，見羅12:18；彼前3:11註釋；見詩34:14。
**聖潔。**只有心地純潔的人才能看見上帝（見太5:8註釋）。
**見主。**就是安然見主。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第429頁；《基督教育原理》第136，385頁；《善惡之爭》第541頁；《醫療佈道論》第52頁；《拾級就主》第35頁；《給傳道人的證言》第447頁；《證言》卷一第23頁；《證言》卷二第401頁；《證言》卷四第332頁；《證言》卷五第743頁；見羅6:19，22懷愛倫註釋；弗4:20-24。
14.en:
**Follow peace.** Or, “strive for peace” (RSV). Leaving the personal problems of the individual Christian, the writer now turns to the Christian’s relationship with his fellow men. For comment on the admonition to “follow peace” see on Rom. 12:18; 1 Peter 3:11; see Ps. 34:14.
**Holiness.** Only the pure in heart can expect to see God (see on Matt. 5:8).
**See the Lord.** That is, in peace.

15.zh:
又要謹慎，恐怕有人失了神的恩；恐怕有毒根生出來擾亂你們，因此叫眾人沾染汙穢；

**又要謹慎。**沒有人是漂進天國的。“我們進入上帝的國，必須經歷許多艱難”（徒14:22；見太7:21-27；10:23的註釋）。我們必須“努力”進去（路13:24）。三心二意是得不到天國財寶的（見太13:44-46）。
**失了。**hustereō，“缺少，”“不足，”“達不到，”“被排除。”該動詞原文的形式暗示連續的失敗，而不是一種缺陷。關於從恩典中墜落，見加5:4註釋。
**毒根。**這句話是依據七十士譯本的申29:18，原來是對偶像崇拜的警告（見申29:18註釋）。在本節似乎是警告教會中喜歡埋怨的人。這種人故意在弟兄們中搬弄是非，挑起爭端。“毒根”通常生長在枯萎黑暗的心靈裡，表現在對上帝所任命地上聖工的領袖們公開而惡意的批評中，致使弟兄們彼此不睦。
**叫眾人沾染汙穢。**那些自己心靈苦毒的人總是設法讓儘可能多的人沾染他們的不滿和叛逆精神。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第207頁；《基督比喻實訓》第85頁；《佈道論》第543頁；《先知與君王》第86頁；《證言》卷一第480頁；《證言》卷三第440，452頁；《證言》卷四第229，610頁；《證言》卷五第241頁；見雅3:15，16懷愛倫註釋；彼前2:1，2。
15.en:
**Looking diligently.** No one will drift into heaven. “We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God” (Acts 14:22; see on Matt. 7:21–27; 10:23). We must “strive” to enter in (Luke 13:24). No halfhearted effort will procure the heavenly treasure (see Matt. 13:44–46).
**Fail.** Gr. hustereō, “to be lacking in,” “to come short of,” “to fail to reach,” “to be excluded from.” The form of the verb in Greek implies a continuing failure, not a single defection. For comment on falling from grace see on Gal. 5:4.
**Root of bitterness.** The statement is based on the LXX of Deut. 29:18. In its original setting this was a warning against idolatry (see comment on Deut. 29:18). Here, it seems to be a warning against any querulous person in the church who deliberately sets out to foment ill will and contention among brethren. It is usually a “root of bitterness” growing in the darkness of some shriveled-up soul that blossoms into open and malicious criticism of the appointed leaders of God’s work on earth and that sets brethren at variance with brethren.
**Many be defiled.** Those whose own souls are bitter always seek to involve as many others as possible in their disaffection and rebellion.

18.zh:
你們原不是來到那能摸的山；此山有火焰、密雲、黑暗、暴風、

**你們原不是來到。**關於第18-21所提到的事件，見出19:9-25。古以色列人怎樣來到西奈山並聽到上帝的聲音（來12:18-21），基督徒也照樣“來到錫安山”（第22,23節），要聽基督的聲音（第24-27節）。
