**那能摸的。**不是地上的某一座山。
**有火焰。**關於第18,19節的用語，見出19:16。
18.en:
**Ye are not come.** For the incident referred to in vs. 18–21 see Ex. 19:9–25. As ancient Israel came to Mount Sinai and heard the voice of God (Heb. 12:18–21), so Christians have “come unto mount Sion” (vs. 22, 23) and are to heed the voice of Christ (vs. 24–27).
**That might be touched.** That is, not to some literal mountain here on earth.
**That burned with fire.** For the descriptive phrases of vs. 18, 19 see Ex. 19:16.

19.zh:
角聲與說話的聲音。那些聽見這聲音的，都求不要再向他們說話；

**說話的聲音。**就是上帝的聲音。
**求。**見出20:19；申5:5。
19.en:
**Voice of words.** That is, the voice of God.
**Intreated.** See Ex. 20:19; Deut. 5:5.

21.zh:
所見的極其可怕，甚至摩西說：我甚是恐懼戰兢。

**極其可怕。**強調對所見所聞的印象，特別是上帝說話的聲音。當百姓面對面站在全地的立法者和審判者面前時，他們體驗了“主的可畏”（林後5:11）。西奈頒佈律法伴隨著上帝大能和威嚴最感人的展示。世人目睹如此可畏的場面乃是空前絕後的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》304頁；《證言》卷四第342頁。
21.en: **So terrible.** Emphasis is on the impressiveness of what was seen and heard, particularly the sound of God’s voice. As the people stood face to face with the Lawgiver and Judge of all the earth they experienced something of “the terror of the Lord” (2 Cor. 5:11). The giving of the law at Sinai was attended with a most impressive exhibition of the power and majesty of God. Never before or since has the world witnessed anything so awe inspiring.

22.zh:
你們乃是來到錫安山，永生神的城邑，就是天上的耶路撒冷。那裡有千萬的天使，

**你們乃是來到。**作者現在從古代以色列人的經驗，轉到基督徒的經驗。作者在這裡用比喻性的語言說到了活著的基督徒聚集在天上上帝的寶座周圍。這是看不見之教會的大聚集。
**錫安山。**古耶路撒冷所坐落的山（見詩48:2註釋）。這是在詩歌中表示耶路撒冷的名字。在本節指“天上的耶路撒冷”。
**永生上帝。**見來3:12；9:14；10:31註釋。
**天上的耶路撒冷。**關於耶路撒冷或新耶路撒冷指“永生上帝的城邑”，見啟3:12；21:2註釋。
**千萬的。**直譯是“無數的。”見啟5:11註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第512頁。
22.en:
**But ye are come.** The writer now turns from the experience of ancient Israel to that of Christians. The writer here speaks figuratively of living Christians as being assembled about the throne of God in heaven, a great gathering of the church invisible.
**Mount Sion.** The name of one of the mountains on which ancient Jerusalem was situated (see on Ps. 48:2). This became a favorite poetical name for the city of Jerusalem. Here reference is to “the heavenly Jerusalem.”
**Living God.** See on chs. 3:12; 9:14; 10:31.
**Heavenly Jerusalem.** For the application of the name Jerusalem, or New Jerusalem, to “the city of the living God” see on Rev. 3:12; 21:2.
**Innumerable company.** Literally, “myriads.” See on Rev. 5:11.

23.zh:
有名錄在天上諸長子之會所共聚的總會，有審判眾人的神和被成全之義人的靈魂，

**名錄在天上。**就是羔羊的生命冊（見腓4:3；啟3:5註釋）。
**諸長子之會。**就是諸長子的教會，這裡指重生的基督徒。本節無形的教會。
**共聚的總會。**直譯是“節日聚會”，在這裡顯然是“教會”的同義詞。
**審判眾人的上帝。**上帝是西奈山的立法者；祂在錫安山顯現為“審判眾人的”，要按著祂在西奈山所頒佈的律法審判他們。當上帝照律法的標準審判眾人時，站在祂面前是非常可怕的。
**被成全之義人。**他們是成熟的基督徒（見太5:48註釋）。來12:22中的“你們乃是來到”，根據上下文，是對活著的基督徒說的。作者並不是對過去已死的義人說話，彷彿他們真的在“錫安山”，“天上的耶路撒冷”聚集在“審判眾人的上帝”面前（第22,23節）。所有的人都贊同22-24節中所描述活著基督徒聚集在上帝的寶座前，乃是從象徵的意義上說的。在來4：16中，他也是以象徵的意義邀請他們“坦然無懼地來到來到施恩的寶座前”。同樣在象徵的意義上，活著的基督徒看見其他“被成全之義人的靈魂”聚集在那裡，不是處在一種假想的沒有實體的狀態。“被成全之義人的靈魂”如果是指假想中沒有實體的“靈”，《希伯來書》的作者就與聖經有關人死後狀況的明言相矛盾了（見傳3:21；12:7；約11:11註釋；參創2:7註釋）。
**靈魂。**pneumata（見第9節註釋）。pneuma（複數為pneumata）本身並沒有意思指人假想中的離開肉體而存在的有意識實體，故在《新約》中也不會自然而擁有這樣的意思。這種觀念完全是出於一些人的想象。他們認為人肉身死亡之後仍有一個有意識的實體存在，並將這種觀念賦予“靈”和“魂”等詞。關於pneuma在希伯來語中的對應詞ruach，見傳12:7註釋。
23.en:
**General assembly.** Literally, “festal gathering.” Here the term appears to be synonymous with “church.”
**Church of the firstborn.** That is, church of first-born ones, here referring to born-again Christians. Reference here is to the church invisible.
**Written in heaven.** Or, “recorded in heaven,” that is, in the Lamb’s book of life (see on Phil. 4:3; Rev. 3:5).
**God the Judge.** God was the lawgiver at Mt. Sinai; on Mt. Zion He appears as “the Judge of all” men, to judge them by the law He proclaimed from Sinai. It will be no less awe inspiring to stand before God when He judges all men according to the standard of the law.
**Spirits.** Gr. pneumata (see on v. 9). The idea that the word pneuma (pl., pneumata) denotes some supposedly conscious entity of man capable of existence apart from the body is not inherent in the word itself nor can such a meaning be derived objectively from its usage in the NT. Such a concept is based exclusively on the preconceived opinions of those who believe that a conscious entity survives the body at death and who read this preconceived opinion into such words as “spirit” and “soul.” For comment on ruach, the Hebrew equivalent of the Gr. pneuma, see on Eccl. 12:7.
**Just men made perfect.** These are mature Christians (see on Matt. 5:48). The words “ye are come” in Heb. 12:22 are addressed to living Christians, as the context makes evident. The writer is not addressing the righteous dead of ages past, as if they were actually assembled before “the Judge of all” men on “mount Sion” in “the heavenly Jerusalem” (vs. 22, 23). All will agree that it is only in a figurative sense that living Christians can assemble before the throne of God as pictured in vs. 22–24. It is in this same sense that in ch. 4:16 he invites them to “come boldly unto the throne of grace.” In this same figurative sense living Christians find “the spirits” of all other “just men made perfect” assembled there in spirit, not in an imaginary disembodied state. To make “the spirits of just men made perfect” refer to supposedly disembodied “spirits” would be to set the writer of Hebrews at variance with the clear statements of the Holy Scriptures concerning the state of man in death (see on Eccl. 3:21; 12:7; John 11:11; cf. on Gen. 2:7).

24.zh:
並新約的中保耶穌，以及所灑的血；這血所說的比亞伯的血所說的更美。

**新約。**見來8:8-10註釋。
**中保。**關於基督擔任新約的中保，見來8:6；9:15註釋。
**所灑的血。**見出24:6,8；來9:19,21；10:22註釋。這裡指的是基督的贖罪寶血。新約藉此而生效，罪惡藉此而赦免。
**所說的。**見創4:10註釋；參來11:4註釋。
**更美。**亞伯的血要求復仇。基督的血則雄辯地宣揚上帝的憐憫和饒恕。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第166頁；《先祖與先知》第371頁；見來8:5-13懷愛倫註釋。
24.en:
**Mediator.** For comment on Christ as mediator of the new covenant see on chs. 8:6; 9:15.
**New covenant.** See on ch. 8:8–10.
**Blood of sprinkling.** See on Ex. 24:6, 8; Heb. 9:19, 21; 10:22. Here reference is to the atoning blood of Christ, by which the new covenant was ratified and by means of which sin is pardoned.
**Speaketh.** See on Gen. 4:10; cf. on Heb. 11:4.
**Better things.** The blood of Abel cried forth for vengeance. The blood of Christ speaks eloquently of divine mercy and forgiveness.

25.zh:
你們總要謹慎，不可棄絕那向你們說話的。因為，那些棄絕在地上警戒他們的尚且不能逃罪，何況我們違背那從天上警戒我們的呢？

**不可棄絕。**作者從18-24節的論據中得出第25-29節的結論。古代以色列人曾因上帝在西奈山發言的聲音而恐懼（第18-21節）。基督徒既因信來到“審判眾人的上帝”和“新約的中保耶穌”面前（第23,24節），也會有一樣深刻的印象。然而，以色列人不聽上帝的聲音（出20:18,19），說明他們執意不順從（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷四第32,33頁）。基督徒要避免重蹈古代以色列人的覆轍（見林前10:1-12；來3:11；4:1註釋）。
**那說話的。**在來1:1,2中，父上帝藉著祂兒子對我們說話。在這裡說話的，不清楚是聖父還是聖子。
**在地上警戒。**就是從西奈山。
**尚且不能逃罪。**見來2:2,3；4:1註釋。
**何況。**見來2:3註釋。
**從天上。**就是對於如今在地上的基督徒。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第236頁。
25.en:
**See that ye refuse not.** In vs. 25–29 the writer draws his conclusion from the line of argument presented in vs. 18–24. Ancient Israel was terrified by the voice of God, who spoke from Mt. Sinai (vs. 18–21). Entering by faith into the presence of “God the Judge of all” and of “Jesus the mediator of the new covenant” (vs. 23, 24), Christians will be no less profoundly impressed. However, Israel refused to listen to the voice of God (Ex. 20:18, 19), and this refusal prefigured persistent disobedience (see Vol. IV, pp. 32, 33). Christians are to beware of making the same mistake that ancient Israel made (see on 1 Cor. 10:1–12; Heb. 3:11; 4:1).
**Him that speaketh.** In ch. 1:1, 2 God the Father is presented as speaking to us through His Son. Whether the speaker here is the Father or the Son is not evident.
**If they escaped not.** For comment see on chs. 2:2, 3; 4:1.
**Him that spake on earth.** That is, from Mt. Sinai.
**Much more.** See on ch. 2:3.
**From heaven.** That is, to Christians on earth, today.

27.zh:
這再一次的話，是指明被震動的，就是受造之物都要挪去，使那不被震動的常存。

**被震動的。**就是能夠被震動的。罪及其一切作品都要被“震動”。今世以及世上的一切都將過去。
**就是受造之物。**這個分句與整個思路的關係不甚明顯。原文簡要而含糊。作者可能指正如太初上帝用祂的話語創造了天地（見創1:3；來11:3註釋；參詩33:6,9），祂必再次說話，將凡能被震動的都挪去。
**指明……要挪去。**“再一次”暗示第二次震動是最後的。不需要再震動了。所以凡能被震動的，都要在第二次震動時被挪去。
**不被震動的。**就是“不能震動的國”（第28節），包括所有“被成全之義人”（第23節）。
**常存。**當上帝的聲音再一次震動天地時，只有公義，純潔，真誠的人才能常存。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《書報服務》第9，12頁；《佈道論》第363頁；《給青年人的信息》第30頁；《證言》卷一第355頁；《證言》卷六第332頁；《證言》卷七第219頁；《證言》卷九第15，62頁。
27.en:
**Signifieth the removing.** The phrase “yet once more” implies that the second shaking is to be final. No further shaking will be required. Accordingly, whatever can be shaken will be removed at the time of the second shaking.
**That are shaken.** That is, that can be shaken. Sin and all its works will be “shaken.” This present world and all that is in it will pass away.
**As of things that are made.** The relationship of this clause to the line of thought is not readily apparent. The Greek is brief and cryptic. The writer may be alluding to the fact that as God spoke the heavens and the earth into being at the beginning (see on Gen. 1:3; Heb. 11:3; cf. Ps. 33:6, 9), so He will speak again to remove all that can be shaken.
**Things which cannot be shaken.** That is, the “kingdom which cannot be moved” (v. 28), including all “just men made perfect” (v. 23).
**May remain.** When God’s voice again shakes heaven and earth only that which is right and pure and true will remain.

28.zh:
所以我們既得了不能震動的國，就當感恩，照神所喜悅的，用虔誠、敬畏的心事奉神。

**國。**作者描述上帝在地上的子民彷彿已經擁有他們永恆的產業（見來11:1註釋）。
**就當感恩。**該希臘習語在《新約》其他地方（見路17:9；提前1:12；提後1:3）也表示感恩，但是約叄4中表示喜樂。
**照上帝所喜悅的侍奉。**沒有什麼比感激救恩計劃的豐富恩典更蒙上帝悅納的了，因為感激必然導致忠心的侍奉。
**用虔誠、敬畏的心。**見詩19:9；來5:7註釋，在來12:18-21,26,27中強調人類在上帝面前的敬畏。
28.en:
**A kingdom.** The writer pictures the people of God on earth as if they were already in possession of their eternal inheritance (see on ch. 11:1).
**Let us have grace.** Probably, “let us be thankful,” or “let us be grateful.” Elsewhere in the NT (see Luke 17:9; 1 Tim. 1:12; 2 Tim. 1:3) the same Greek idiom is used in this sense, though in 3 John 4, in the sense of experiencing joy.
**Serve God acceptably.** Nothing can be more acceptable to God than gratitude for the gracious provisions of the plan of salvation, for gratitude inevitably leads to loyal service.
**Reverence and godly fear.** Or, “reverence and awe.” See on Ps. 19:9; Heb. 5:7. The reverential awe human beings feel in the presence of God is stressed in ch. 12:18–21, 26, 27.

29.zh:
因為我們的神乃是烈火。

**烈火。**西奈山證明了這個事實（見出24:17）。末日的火必消滅一切被罪所汙染的人（見瑪4:1註釋；參彼後3:7,10-12；啟20:9,15）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第107，600頁；《善惡之爭》第673頁；《拾級就主》第18頁；《救贖的故事》第429頁。
29.en: **A consuming fire.** This fact was demonstrated at Mt. Sinai (see Ex. 24:17). The fires of the last day will destroy all that is tainted with sin (see on Mal. 4:1; cf. 2 Peter 3:7, 10–12; Rev. 20:9, 15).

5.en:
**Tasted.** Gr. geuomai (see on v. 4). The word suggests more than a superficial acquaintance. It suggests study, meditation, and acceptance.
**Powers.** Gr. dunameis (see on Acts 1:8), here probably meaning “miracles,” as in Heb. 2:4. In the early apostolic age many miracles were wrought, deliverances effected, the sick healed, and even the dead restored to life (Acts 3:6–9; 5:15, 16; 6:8; 8:6; 12:7; 20:9–12). To taste these powers is to have a part in them, either as the subject of healing or of some other miracle, or as having performed them, or as having witnessed them. Those here brought to view had seen the mighty power of God in doing that which it was not possible for man to perform.
**World to come.** Or, “coming age,” here probably a reference to the future age, of which the Gospel Era with its miracles was a foretaste, or an earnest.
These different qualifications are enumerated to show that these persons had had a genuine experience. They had witnessed God’s mighty power in their own lives and in the lives of others. Much had been entrusted to them, and much might be expected.
5.zh:
並嘗過神善道的滋味、覺悟來世權能的人，

**嘗過。**geuomai（見第4節註釋）。不止是膚淺的認識。它表示研究，思考和接受。
**來世。**可能指將來的世代。福音時代及其奇蹟只是那個時代的預嘗或保證。
**權能。**dunameis（見徒1:8註釋），這裡可能指“異能”，如來2:4。在使徒時代的初期，曾發生許多奇蹟，被囚的獲得釋放，患病的得到醫治，甚至還有死人復活（徒3:6-9；5:15,16；6:8；8:6；12:7；20:9-12）。體驗這些權能就是與這些權能有分，要麼是得到醫治或接受其他異能，要麼是施行這些異能，或親眼看見。這些人見過上帝大能的運行。這種奇蹟是人所無法施行的。
列舉出這些不同的資歷是要說明他們有真實的經驗。他們在自己和別人的生活中看見了上帝的大能。交託給他們的既然多，向他們所要的也就多。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第33頁；《基督教育原理》第173頁；《今日的生活》第293頁；《證言》卷五第745頁；《證言》卷六第444頁。

6.en:
**If they shall fall away.** Or, “having fallen away.” The extent of the fall may be judged by the privileges enjoyed. The context suggests a major apostasy.
**To renew … unto repentance.** That is, to bring about a desire for repentance. The case is not that of a man seeking to return to God, finding repentance impossible, but that of a man with no desire to return to the experience from which he has fallen away. For the meaning of repentance see on v. 1.
**Seeing.** The interpretation of the passage depends to a large extent upon the translation here. The Greek has simply the participle for “crucifying.” The word “seeing” is supplied in the KJV in an endeavor to show the relationship between the participle and the rest of the sentence. But it is possible to supply other words. The Greek participial construction may express time, cause, condition, or purpose. Some commentators suggest that the sense here is temporal and that the passage should be rendered, “It is impossible to renew while they keep on crucifying the Son of God.” Such a temporal use of the participle is common. If adopted, the passage teaches that those who fall away cannot be restored as long as they continue unrepentant.
If the causal use of the participle (“seeing,” “since,” “because,” etc.) be adopted, then the passage should be treated as dealing with the unpardonable sin, for only those guilty of this sin cannot be renewed to repentance. This sin ordinarily manifests itself in continued resistance to the call of God and the wooing of the Spirit. It consists in a hardening of the heart, till there is no longer any response to the voice of God. Hence, a person who has sinned against the Spirit has no remorse, no feeling of sorrow for sin, no desire to turn from it, and no conscience that accuses him. If one has a sincere desire to do right, he may confidently believe that there is still hope for him.
This should be a source of comfort to the discouraged soul, but it is by no means to be used as an incentive to carelessness. God desires to comfort the disconsolate, but He would also warn His people of the danger of reaching the point of no return.
**Crucify … afresh.** Gr. anastauroō, “to crucify,” “to crucify afresh.” In non-Biblical writings anastauroō means simply “to crucify,” but in the present passage the context favors the figurative meaning “to crucify again,” or “to crucify afresh.” Such a meaning is especially significant since those addressed are Jewish Christians whose race had been guilty of crucifying the Son of God the first time (Acts 3:14, 15). Now if these Christians should reject their Saviour and return to their former ways, it would be as if they crucified Him anew.
**Put him to an open shame.** Or, “hold him up to contempt.” This phrase may be rendered: “as long as they keep on holding up Christ to contempt” (see above under “seeing”).
6.zh:
若是離棄道理，就不能叫他們從新懊悔了。因為他們把神的兒子重釘十字架，明明的羞辱他。

**若是離棄。**或“已經離棄。”離棄的程度按所享有的特權來判斷。這裡暗示一種大背道。
**就不能。**4-6節講述背離上帝之人的命運，討論那些有過深刻基督徒經驗卻離棄真道的人有沒有恢復的可能。他們能不能回到基督徒團體，重得憐憫？這段經文曾使許多人困惑和灰心。它似乎教導說：離棄真道的人的無可救藥的。
在各種觀點中，有兩種是值得考慮的。一，這裡所說的背道乃是犯了不可饒恕的罪（見太12:31,32註釋），因為這是唯一無可救藥的背道。二，如果正確理解這段經文，就可知道這裡所說背道的無可救藥不是絕對的，而是有條件的（見來6:6註釋）。大多數註釋者接受前一種觀點，但後一種觀點也有價值，並有原文的依據。
在當時在猶太人中，流行著在某些情況下不可能悔改的觀念。例如他們教導說，犯罪放縱，相信將來會悔改的人情況是這樣的：“如果一個人說：我要犯罪，再悔改，再犯罪，再悔改，就不會給他悔改的機會了。（如果一個人說）：我要犯罪，而贖罪日會為我贖罪，贖罪日就不能為他贖罪了”（《密西拿》Yoma 8. 9,蘇西諾版《塔木德》第423頁）。他們還教導說，引多人犯罪的人是不可能悔改的：“凡使多人行義的，罪就不藉著他發生；凡使多人犯罪的，他們就不能給他悔改的能力”（《 密西拿》Aboth 5. 18, 蘇西諾版《塔木德》，第71頁）。《西拉書》中的一段話也很有意思：“不要說：‘我犯了罪，那又會有什麼事臨到我呢？’因為耶和華有恆久的忍耐。不要指望赦免，這會使你罪上加罪。也不要說：‘祂有大憐憫，會赦免我眾多的罪’；因為祂既有憐恤也有忿怒。祂的義怒常降在不虔不敬的人身上。要歸向祂，不要耽擱，也不要一天一天拖延；因為祂的忿怒會突然來臨，在復仇的時候你將滅亡”（ 《西拉書》5:4-7； 查爾斯《舊約次經和偽經》卷一第332頁）。
**從新懊悔。**就是生出悔意。這裡不是說一個人想要回歸上帝，卻發現不可能悔改了，而是說指一個人不願意回到他墮落前的狀態。關於悔改的意義，見第1節註釋。
**因為。**這段經文的解釋在很大程度上取決於翻譯。原文只是“釘十字架”的分詞形式。“因為”是外加的，為要說明該分詞與句子其餘部分的關係。但也可以外加其它的詞。原文分詞的結構可以表示時間，原因，條件或目的。有些註釋家認為這裡是表示時間。故這句話應譯為：“當他們繼續把上帝的兒子釘十字架的時候，就不可能從新懊悔了。”用分詞表示時間是常見的。如果採用這種解釋，這段經文就是教導說，離棄道理的人如果繼續不悔改，就無法得到恢復。
如果把分詞理解為原因，這段經文就當視為涉及不可饒恕的罪，因為只有犯這種罪的人才無法從新懊悔。這種罪一般表現為持續抗拒上帝的呼召和聖靈的懇勸。它的特點是心地剛硬，直到不再回應上帝的聲音。因此，得罪聖靈的人是不懊悔，不為罪感到悲哀，不希望轉離罪惡，良心也不自責的。如果一個人真希望行義，他就可以確信自己仍有希望。
這應該成為灰心的人安慰的泉源，但決不要因此而疏忽大意。上帝願意安慰憂傷的人，但祂也警告祂的子民不要到了無可救藥的地步。
**重釘十字架。**anastauroō。在聖經以外的著作中，anastauroō只是指“釘十字架，”但在本文中是指“重釘十字架”。這層意思特別重要，因為本書信的收信人是猶太籍的基督徒。他們的民族已第一次將上帝的兒子釘十字架（徒3:14,15）。如果這些基督徒拒絕他們的救主，故態復萌，那就好比將祂重釘十字架。
**明明地羞辱祂。**或“把祂舉起來受辱。”（見上面“因為”註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第306頁；《復臨信徒家庭》第328頁；《基督教育原理》第284頁；《福山寶訓》第10頁；《先祖與先知》第580頁；《給傳道人的證言》第39，147頁；《證言》卷一第133頁；《證言》卷三第438頁；《證言》卷五第243頁。

2.en:
**Baptisms.** Gr. baptismoi (sing. baptimos). This is not the usual word for Christian baptism, which is baptisma (cf. on Matt. 3:6). Baptismos occurs only here and in Mark 7:4, 8; Heb. 9:10. Important textual evidence may also be cited (cf. p. 10) for its reading in Col. 2:12. In Mark 7:4, 8; Heb. 9:10, the word has reference to the many acts of purification in the Jewish ritual. This, however, could not be its primary meaning here, since the regulations concerning these washings would not be considered a fundamental doctrine of Christianity. It is possible, however, that the author is thinking of Christian baptism but is employing the term baptismoi as representing the rite in its most elemental aspects.
Some see in baptismoi a reference to the two baptisms in the Christians church, baptism by water and baptism by the Spirit. Concerning the two John the Baptist said, “I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost” (Mark 1:8). After His resurrection Jesus said, “John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence” (Acts 1:5; cf. John 3:5; Acts 11:16; 1 Cor. 12:13). However, if these two forms of Christian baptism were primarily in the author’s mind we would expect him to use the form baptismata instead of baptismoi, especially since the latter term occurs later in the epistle with a clear reference to ceremonial washings (Heb. 9:10). Therefore the explanation that regards baptismoi as representing Christian baptism in its most elemental aspects seems preferable.
**Laying on of hands.** This is the fourth of the fundamental doctrines being presented. The gesture of laying on of hands on OT times signified the transference of blessing and office (see Gen 48:9–14; Num. 8:10, 11, Deut. 34:9). In the NT the same custom was followed. Particularly significant was the apostles’ laying on of hands following baptism, an act by which believers received the Holy Spirit (see Acts 8:17, 18; 19:6). Since the author has immediately before mentioned “baptisms,” he probably had this particular function in mind. For the gesture in ordination see Acts 6:6; 1 Tim. 4:14.
**Resurrection of the dead.** For the importance of this doctrine see on 1 Cor. 15.
**Eternal judgment.** The doctrine of the judgment occupies a prominent place in both the OT (cf. Ps. 9:3–8, 15, 16; Dan. 7:9, 10; cf. Jude 14, 15), and the NT (see Matt. 12:41, 42; 25:31–46; Luke 11:31, 32; 2 Cor. 5:10). It should be noted that with these six principles Jewish Christians would have no difficulty, for these are all set forth in the OT. The danger confronting these Christians lay in contentment with what they had brought over from Judaism and a reluctance to accept wholeheartedly the tenets of Christianity.
2.zh:
各樣洗禮、按手之禮、死人復活，以及永遠審判各等教訓。

**各樣洗禮。**baptismoi（單數是baptimos）。這不是表達基督徒洗禮的常用詞baptisma（參太3:6註釋）。Baptismos只出現在本節以及可7:4,8和來9:10中。有文本在西2:12中也出現該詞。在可7:4,8和來9:10中，該詞指猶太禮儀中許多洗濯之舉。但這不可能是該詞在這裡的主要意思，因為這些洗濯的規則不可能被視為基督教的一個基本要道。作者想到的可能是基督徒的洗禮，但用baptismoi來表達洗禮的最基本方面。
有些人認為baptismoi是指基督教會中的兩種洗禮：水的洗禮和聖靈的洗禮。關於這兩種洗禮，施洗約翰說：“我是用水給你們施洗。祂卻要用聖靈給你們施洗”（可1:8）。耶穌在復活以後說：“約翰是用水施洗，但不多幾日，你們要受聖靈的洗”（徒1:5；參約3:5；徒11:16；林前12:13）。但如果作者心裡想的主要是基督教這兩種洗禮的話，他就會用baptismata，而不用baptismoi，尤其是因為baptismoi出現在這封書信的後面，顯然是指儀文上的洗濯（來9:10）。所以把baptismoi解釋為基督教洗禮的最基本方面似乎更為可取。
**按手之禮。**這是所列的是第四個基本道理。在舊約時代，按手代表祝福和任職（見創48:9-14；民8:10,11；申34:9）。新約時代沿襲了這個禮儀。特別有意義的是使徒在施洗後的按手，以此來象徵信徒領受聖靈（見徒8:17,18；19:6）。由於作者在上面剛提到“各樣洗禮”，他心裡所想的很可能就是這種按手。關於聖職任命時的按手，見徒6:6；提前4:14。
**死人復活。**關於這個道理的重要性，見林前15註釋。
**永遠審判。**審判的道理在《舊約》（參詩9:3-8,15,16；但7:9,10；參猶14,15）和《新約》（見太12:41,42；25:31-46；路11:31,32；林後5:10）中都佔據重要的地位。值得注意的是，這六項原則對於猶太籍的基督徒來說並不困難，因為它們都已經在《舊約》中闡明。這些基督徒所面對的危險是滿足於猶太教帶給他們的道理，不願意全心全意地接受基督教的原則。

4.en:
**It is impossible.** Verses 4–6 deal with the fate of those who fall away from God. The question at issue is the possibility of restoring such as have had a deep Christian experience but have fallen away. Can they be restored to Christian fellowship and again receive mercy? This passage has been the source of great perplexity and discouragement to many. It seems to teach that those who fall away from the faith are irrevocably lost.
Among the various views that have been held two are worthy of consideration. (1) That the apostasy here spoken of is the commission of the unpardonable sin (see on Matt. 12:31, 32), since this is the only form of apostasy that is hopeless. (2) That the passage correctly understood does not teach the absolute hopelessness of the apostasy here described but a conditional hopelessness (see on Heb. 6:6). Most commentators accept the former view, although the latter has merits and can be defended on the basis of the Greek.
The idea that repentance was impossible under certain circumstances was current among the Jews. They taught, for example, that such was the case of the man who sinned wantonly, trusting in future repentance: “If one says: I shall sin and repent, sin and repent, no opportunity will be given to him to repent. [If one says]: I shall sin and the Day of Atonement will procure atonement for me, the Day of Atonement procures for him no atonement” (Mishnah Yoma 8. 9, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 423). They taught also that repentance was impossible for the man who led the multitude into sin: “Whoever causes the many to be righteous, sin occurs not through him; and whoever causes the many to sin, they do not afford him the faculty to repent” (Mishnah Aboth 5. 18, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 71). Of interest also is a passage from the Book of Sirach: “Say not, ‘I have sinned, but what happened unto me?’ For Jahveh is longsuffering. Count not upon forgiveness, That thou shouldst add sin to sin. And say not, ‘His mercies are great, He will forgive the multitude of mine iniquities’; For mercy and wrath are with Him, And His indignation abideth upon the ungodly. Delay not to turn unto Him, And put (it) not off from day to day; For suddenly doth His wrath come forth, And in the time of vengeance thou shalt perish” (ch. 5:4–7; R. H. Charles, The Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament, vol. 1, p. 332).
**Enlightened.** Or, “illuminated” (see on Eph. 1:18).
**Tasted.** Gr. geuomai (see on ch. 2:9). The meaning “to experience” seems to apply here. Compare Ps. 34:8.
**Heavenly gift.** That is, the gift of salvation or perhaps a special gift of the Spirit (Rom. 5:15; 1 Cor. 12).
**Partakers of the Holy Ghost.** That is, they have received an outpouring of the Spirit either as the divine energy in conversion (John 3:5) or through the impartation of some special gift (1 Cor. 12).
4.zh:
論到那些已經蒙了光照、嘗過天恩的滋味、又於聖靈有分，

**光照。**或“啟發”（見弗1:18註釋）。
**嘗過。**geuomai（見來2:9註釋）。這裡似乎指“體驗”。參詩34:8。
**天恩。**就是救恩或聖靈的特別恩賜（羅5:15；林前12）。
**於聖靈有份。**指他們領受了聖靈的沛降，或在悔改時獲得上帝的能力（約3:5），或藉著某種特別恩賜的賜予（林前12章）。

1.zh:
所以，我們應當離開基督道理的開端，竭力進到完全的地步，不必再立根基，就如那懊悔死行，信靠神、

**所以。**作者繼續他從第5章開始的勸勉。他的讀者本應吃乾糧，卻仍在吃奶為生。他們還是小孩子，並滿足於保持這種狀態。他希望他們對上帝的事有更深的瞭解，不再滿足於他們目前的成就。
**開端。**指基督道理的基本原則。第1節的後半部分和第2節列舉了這些原理。
**完全。**或“成熟。”
**根基。**立下良好的根基是對的，但不在上面建造，就永遠蓋不成房子。作者的意思是要超越基本的原則。他認為大家在基本的原則上已經打下良好的基礎。超越並不等於放棄。超越的意思就像建造房屋的人在開始建造時要超越根基那樣。
作者列舉了建造基督教的六項基本原則。他只是提到，但沒有論述，因為他認為前面已經說得很多了。
**懊悔。**metanoia，“心靈的改變”（見林後7:9註釋）。這是基本原則中的第一項。真正悔改的人會評估自己過去的行為，用道德的天平進行衡量，拋棄一切不良的動機和行為，靠著上帝的恩典，將原來屬肉體的心換成基督的心志。他因心意更新而改變（羅12:2）。悔改主要不是情緒上的經驗，而是一種影響心靈和生活的深刻過程，以成就“新造的人”，“舊事以過，都變成新的了”（林後5:17）。
**死行。**可能指犯罪意義上的“死”。罪人“死在罪惡過犯之中”（弗2:1）。他知道在成為基督徒之前必須放棄這些行為。參來9:14。
**信靠上帝。**這是第二項基本原則。悔改意味著脫離死行，信靠卻是面對上帝。悔改呈現基督徒心意消極的一面，信靠則呈現積極的一面。舊的必須放棄，新的必須接受。懊悔死行表現了心靈的徹底改變；有一種新的屬靈態度使信徒放棄死行，歸向上帝。
悔改和信靠列在福音基本原則的前面。如果一個人徹底悔改，轉離過去的生活，放棄死行，信靠上帝，他就有了穩固的根基，在苦難的日子來到時不至失敗。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第470頁；《證言》卷二第124頁。
1.en:
**Therefore.** The author continues the exhortation he began in ch. 5. His readers have been subsisting on milk when they should have had stronger food. They were still children, and were satisfied to remain so. He wants them to go on to the deeper things of God and not continue to be satisfied with their present attainments.
**Principles.** Literally, “the beginning,” denoting the elementary principles of the doctrine of Christ. These are defined in the latter part of v. 1 and in v. 2.
**Perfection.** Or, “maturity.”
**Foundation.** It is well to lay a good foundation, but the one who does not build on it will never have a finished structure. The author proposes to leave the first principles, taking for granted that the people are well grounded in them. In leaving them he does not forsake them; he leaves them in the same sense in which a builder leaves the foundation when he proceeds with the structure itself.
The author enumerates six foundation principles upon which Christianity is built. He merely mentions them and does not discuss them, as he feels this has already been well done.
**Repentance.** Gr. metanoia, “a change of mind” (see on 2 Cor. 7:9). This is the first in the list of foundation principles. He who truly repents evaluates his past actions, weighs them in the moral scale, repudiates all unworthy motives and acts, and by the grace of God exchanges the old carnal mind for the mind of Christ. He is transformed by the renewing of his mind (Rom. 12:2). Repentance is not primarily an emotional experience; it is rather a deep process affecting the mind and life, issuing in a new creature” so that “old things are passed away,” and “all things are become new” (2 Cor. 5:17).
**Dead works.** Probably “dead” in the sense of being sinful. The sinner is “dead in trespasses and sins” (Eph. 2:1). These are works he knows he must lay off before he becomes a Christian. Compare Heb. 9:14.
**Faith toward God.** This is second in the list of fundamental principles. Repentance is from dead works, faith is toward God. Repentance presents the negative, faith, the positive, side of the Christian mind. The old must be abandoned, the new must be grasped. Repentance from dead works expresses a complete change of mind—a new spiritual attitude—which leads the believer to forsake dead works and turn toward God.
These two, repentance and faith, are placed first among the foundation principles of the gospel. If a man is thoroughly converted, if he has turned from his past life and renounced dead works, if he has turned in faith toward God, he has a solid foundation that will not fail him when the evil days come.

3.zh:
神若許我們，我們必如此行。

**上帝若許我們。**參徒18:21；林前4:19註釋；參林前16:7。
**我們必如此行。**有文本為 “讓我們行。”作者鼓勵讀者暫時超越（第1節）福音的基本原則，希望並相信他們已經充分明白。他說離開這些基本原則，意思就像一個孩子隨著學業的進步而離開初級課本一樣。但實際上沒有一個孩子，甚至連聰明的科學家會拋棄字母表。他總會使用26個字母。這些基本的原則也是如此，不應拋棄，而應作為建造的基礎。作者說的是從初級真理進到更深的真理。
3.en:
**Will we do.** Important textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 10) for the reading “let us do.” The author encourages his readers to go beyond (v. 1) the elementary principles of the gospel for the present, hoping and believing that they are well understood. He would leave these fundamentals in the sense that a child leaves his first A-B-C book when he progresses to his first reader. But in reality no child, nor the wisest scientist, will ever leave the alphabet behind. He will always use these 26 letters. So with these foundation principles; they are not discarded, they are built upon. The author would go on from primary to deeper truths.
**If God permit.** Compare on Acts 18:21; 1 Cor. 4:19; cf. 1 Cor. 16:7.

7.zh:
就如一塊田地，吃過屢次下的雨水，生長菜蔬，合乎耕種的人用，就從神得福；

**吃過屢次下的雨水。**這是一幅土地接受天上的雨水，生產出果蔬和糧食的畫面，比喻人心接受天上的甘霖，從而結出果子來榮耀上帝。
**耕種。**“耕耘”。
**從上帝得福。**就是豐收。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。《教育論》第216頁。
7.en:
**Drinketh in the rain.** The picture here is that of the earth, which receives rain from heaven, and in return brings forth herbs and food for man. This is an illustration of the human heart, which receives the blessed rain and dew from heaven and in return should produce fruit to the glory of God.
**Dressed.** Literally, “cultivated,” “tilled.”
**Blessing from God.** That is, in its productiveness.

8.zh:
若長荊棘和蒺藜，必被廢棄，近於咒詛，結局就是焚燒。

**荊棘和蒺藜。**上帝曾賜福給希伯來籍的基督徒，希望他們結出果子。他們既得到上帝所賜的一切福氣，道路上有上帝的光照，如果仍不結出果子，或離棄真理，那麼唯一的結局就是與上帝分離而滅亡。
**近於咒詛。**參創3:17,18。作者沒有說希伯來籍的基督徒已經處於來6:4-6所描述的絕望狀態。但如果他們不結果子，這種狀態就“近了”。他們得到了及時的警告，叫他們不要採取導致被棄絕的行徑（參來2:1-3；10:26-29）。
**焚燒。**參申29:23。
8.en:
**Thorns and briers.** God had blessed the Hebrew Christians, and He expected them to bring forth fruit. If with all the blessings He had given them and with all the light that had illuminated their path, they still refused to bring forth fruit, or if they fell away, there would be but one end for them: separation from God and oblivion.
**Nigh unto cursing.** Compare Gen. 3:17, 18. The author does not imply that the Hebrew Christians are already in the hopeless state described in Heb. 6:4–6. But without fruitfulness such a state is “nigh.” They are duly warned against adopting a course that will result in their rejection (cf. chs. 2:1–3; 10:26–29).
**Burned.** Compare Deut. 29:23.

9.zh:
親愛的弟兄們，我們雖是這樣說，卻深信你們的行為強過這些，而且近乎得救。

**親愛的。**這是《希伯來書》中唯一一次採用這個親切的稱呼。
**強過這些。**作者曾尖銳地警告和勸誡他的讀者。現在他安慰他們，深信他們無意拒絕上帝的呼召。但他們需要告誡。他們有不留意所聽到的道理而流失的危險（來2:1-3）。他們有重犯古代以色列人未能進迦南之錯誤的危險（來4:1）。他們的進步或成長並不令人滿意。他們在應該長大成人時卻仍為嬰孩（來5:11-14）。他在這裡告訴他們失敗的真實危險。他為了緩和語氣，就說他深信他們的行為強過這些。但他給人的印象是：他們的情況是嚴重的。他們必須知道這一點，免得失去永生。
**近乎得救。**或“屬於得救。”作者在這裡並沒有說這些事是什麼，但是根據他上面所寫的，讀者不會不明白。
9.en:
**Beloved.** This is the only occurrence of this affectionate term in Hebrews.
**Better things.** The author has spoken sharply to his readers by way of warning and admonition. Now he soothes them. He is persuaded that they have no intention of rejecting God’s call, and yet they need admonition. They are in danger of drifting, of not giving heed to the things they have heard (ch. 2:1–3). They are in danger of repeating the mistake of Israel of old of not entering in (ch. 4:1). They have not progressed or grown satisfactorily, but are still babes when they should be full grown (ch. 5:11–14). And in the present instance he is telling them that there is real danger of their losing out. He softens this somewhat by saying that he is persuaded of better things of them, and yet he leaves the impression that their condition is serious and they must beware lest they lose out on eternal life.
**That accompany salvation.** Or, “that belong to salvation.” The author does not here state what these things are, but from what he has already written, the readers could not fail to know.

10.zh:
因為神並非不公義，竟忘記你們所做的工和你們為他名所顯的愛心，就是先前伺候聖徒，如今還是伺候。

**上帝並非不公義。**這裡提出上帝的公義和公正。
**竟忘記你們所作的工。**上帝不會忘記任何一個仁慈的行為，不論它多麼微小，全都記錄下來了，在審判的日子予以考慮。連一杯涼水也不會忘記（太10:42）；悲傷或同情的淚水都得到紀念並記錄下來（參詩56:8）。
**為祂名。**就是“為了祂”。“名”經常代表該人（參詩7:17註釋）。
**伺候聖徒。**這種事情似乎不值得一提，因為有那麼多遠為重要的事需要關注。苦難中的救助，夜間留宿，為遠行的人提供飲食，好客和仁慈——這一切都記錄在上帝的冊子上。上帝不會忘記這種仁慈的行為（參太10:42；25:31-40）。
10.en:
**God is not unrighteous.** An appeal to the justice and equity of God.
**To forget.** God does not forget any act of kindness, however small. It is all recorded, and will be taken into account in the day of judgment. A cup of cold water is not forgotten (Matt. 10:42); the tear of sorrow or sympathy is remembered and recorded (cf. Ps. 56:8).
**Labour.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the omission of this word.
**Toward his name.** That is, toward Him. “Name” here, as often, stands for person (cf. on Ps. 7:17).
**Ministered to the saints.** This may seem a small matter to mention, when there are so many weightier matters that call for attention. Help in time of distress, a night’s lodging, food and drink for the wayfarer, hospitality and kindness—these are all recorded in the book of God. And God is not forgetful of such acts of kindness (cf. Matt. 10:42; 25:31–40).

11.zh:
我們願你們各人都顯出這樣的殷勤，使你們有滿足的指望，一直到底。

**願。**epithumeō，“渴望。”
**殷勤。**spoudē（見羅12:8註釋）。
**滿足的指望。**參西2:2。受信的信徒曾熱心招待聖徒。他們需要繼續這樣的服務，但是他們在有關得救的事上也要這樣殷勤。
**一直到底。**有開始是好的；有完成就更好。開始不論多麼好，不堅持到底就沒有用處。上帝的應許是“那在你們心裡動了善工的，必成全這工”（腓1:6）。太多是人有始無終。
11.en:
**Desire.** Gr. epithumeō, “to long for earnestly.”
**Diligence.** Gr. spoudē (see on Rom. 12:8).
**Full assurance of hope.** Compare Col. 2:2. The believers to whom the epistle is addressed had been zealous in entertaining the saints. They needed to continue their ministrations, but they should be as diligent in other matters relating to salvation.
**Unto the end.** It is good to begin; it is better to finish. However good a beginning may be, it is useless unless it is continued unto the end. God’s promise is that “he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it” (Phil. 1:6). Too many who begin do not finish.

12.zh:
並且不懈怠，總要效法那些憑信心和忍耐承受應許的人。

**懈怠。**nōthroi，“懶惰，”“閒懶。”該詞在來5:11中與“聽”（nōthroi）連用，譯為“聽不進去。”懶惰與殷勤是相反的。對於許多人來說，宗教是一件隨便的事，只在空閒時予以關注。在他們的計劃中，宗教並不列在首位，而是幾近末位。對他們而言，其他事情都能優先，惟獨上帝的可以放在一邊。這種情況需要顛倒過來。
**效法。**“學習。”
**信心。**《希伯來書》11章將詳細論述這一重要品質（見該章註釋）。
**忍耐。**makrothumia，“堅定，”“耐久”。
**承受應許的人。**參來4:1。
12.en:
**Slothful.** Gr. nōthroi, “lazy,” “sluggish.” Connected with hearing, nōthroi is translated “dull” in ch. 5:11. Slothfulness, or laziness, is the opposite of diligence. To many, religion is a casual matter that can be attended to at leisure. It is not first on their program, but near the end of the list. For them everything else must be done first, and God may have what is left. This needs to be reversed.
**Followers.** Literally, “imitators.”
**Faith.** This essential qualification is dealt with at length in ch. 11 (see comment there).
**Patience.** Gr. makrothumia, “steadfastness,” “endurance,” “patience.”
**Inherit the promises.** Compare ch. 4:1.

13.zh:
當初神應許亞伯拉罕的時候，因為沒有比自己更大可以指著起誓的，就指著自己起誓，說：

**上帝應許亞伯拉罕。**這裡把亞伯拉罕作為恆久忍耐“得了應許”（第15節）的榜樣。
**沒有比自己更大可以指著起誓的。**見第16節註釋。
**指著自己起誓。**見創22:16,17。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第 203頁。
13.en:
**God made promise to Abraham.** Abraham is set forth as an example of one who by patient endurance “obtained the promise” (v. 15).
**Swear by no greater.** See on v. 16.
**Sware by himself.** A reference to Gen. 22:16, 17.

14.zh:
論福，我必賜大福給你；論子孫，我必叫你的子孫多起來。

**論福，我必賜大福給你。**這是強調動作的希伯來習語。
**論子孫，我必叫你的子孫多起來。**見上面“論福，我必賜福給你”的註釋。
14.en:
**Blessing I will bless.** Rather, “surely I will bless.” The phrase “blessing I will bless” translates literally a Hebrew idiom that gives strong emphasis to the action of the verb.
**Multiplying I will multiply.** Rather, “I will surely multiply” (see above under “blessing I will bless”).

15.zh:
這樣，亞伯拉罕既恆久忍耐，就得了所應許的。

**恆久忍耐。**見第12節註釋。這裡把亞伯拉罕作為讓他人學習的榜樣。
**就得了所應許的。**指以撒的出生。這個應許之子是多子多孫的保證，尤其是藉著他，那個子孫“基督”（加3:16）將成為臨到萬國家的福氣。
15.en:
**Patiently endured.** See on v. 12. Abraham is set forth as an example for others to imitate.
**He obtained the promise.** That is, in the birth of Isaac. This son of promise was an earnest of the multitude of descendants through whom, and particularly through the seed, “Christ” (Gal. 3:16), a blessing was to come to all nations.

16.zh:
人都是指著比自己大的起誓，並且以起誓為實據，了結各樣的爭論。

**比自己大的。**人們一般都指著上帝起誓。但是上帝沒有比自己更大的可以指著起誓，就指著自己起誓（第13節）。
**實據。**bebaiōsis，這裡用作司法術語，意為“合法擔保”或“保證。”誓言有其積極的效果，就是提供合法擔保；但也有消極的效果，就是結束爭論。
16.en:
**The greater.** Men customarily swear by God. But God, not having any greater by whom He could swear, swore by Himself (v. 13).
**Confirmation.** Gr. bebaiōsis, here used as a legal term meaning “legal surety,” or “warranty.” An oath has a positive effect—it provides legal surety—and a negative effect—it ends controversy.

17.zh:
照樣，神願意為那承受應許的人格外顯明他的旨意是不更改的，就起誓為證。

**為那承受應許的人。**不僅為亞伯拉罕，也為所有的後嗣，包括亞伯拉罕的屬靈後裔（加3:29）。
**願意……顯明。**上帝不必起誓。祂的話語相當於祂的誓言。祂把自己擺在人的水準上，願意為祂應許的真實性起誓，真是一件奇妙的事。
**祂的旨意是不更改的。**或“祂的勉言是不會改變的。”
**為證。**mesiteuō，“調解，”“擔保，”“保證。”上帝用一句起誓的話為證記載在創22:16-18裡。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第164頁；《證言》卷一第203頁。
17.en:
**Willing … to shew.** It was not necessary for God to swear. His word is as good as His oath. It was a wonderful thing that He would so put Himself on a level with man that He would consent to swear to the truth of the promise.
**Unto the heirs.** Not only Abraham but all the heirs including the spiritual descendants of Abraham (Gal. 3:29).
**Immutability of his counsel.** Or, “unchangeableness of His purpose.”
**Confirmed.** Gr. mesiteuō, “to mediate,” “to act as surety,” “to guarantee.” The confirmation of God’s word by an oath is recorded in Gen. 22:16–18.

18.zh:
藉這兩件不更改的事，神決不能說謊，好叫我們這逃往避難所、持定擺在我們前頭指望的人可以大得勉勵。

**兩件不更改的事。**就是上帝的應許和祂的誓言。上帝的話本身是不改變的。沒有任何誓言能增加上帝話語的分量，使之更加確定。上帝用誓言來證實祂的話語，完全是為了我們的緣故。人是用誓言來確認自己話語的，於是上帝也屈尊這麼作，為要幫助我們堅固信心。這個誓言無疑對生活在基督面前的人是很有幫助的。如果他們心中起了疑惑，就應想到上帝不僅發出應許，而且用誓言來確認。所以祂一定會遵守諾言。誓言就是這樣幫助堅固了他們的信心。
**逃往避難所。**這個比喻可能來自古代的慣例。當一個人認為自己有危險時，就逃往會幕作為避難之所（見出21:13,14；王上2:28-34）。
**持定。**或“抓住。”應與“勉勵”連在一起。
**擺在我們前頭。**得救的指望擺在所有的人前頭；大家都可以把握它。
**指望。**見羅5:4；8:24；12:12註釋。
**大得勉勵。**或“得到很大的鼓勵。”
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第371，517頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–19節）**。《善惡之爭》第350頁。
18.en:
**Two immutable things.** That is, God’s promise and His oath. God’s word in itself is unchangeable. No oath can add anything to what God has said, or make it surer. That God confirmed it with an oath is entirely for our sake. Men use an oath for confirmation, and so God condescends to do the same, to help us in our faith. This oath was doubtless a definite help to the people living before Christ. If any doubt should come up in their minds, they could fall back on the fact that not only had God promised but He had confirmed it with an oath. He would therefore surely keep His word. Thus the oath would help strengthen their faith.
**Strong consolation.** Rather, “strong encouragement.”
**Fled for refuge.** The illustration may be taken from the ancient practice of a person who, believing himself to be in danger, fled to the tabernacle as a place of refuge (see Ex. 21:13, 14; 1 Kings 2:28–34).
**To lay hold.** Or, “to seize.” The phrase should be connected with “consolation” (encouragement).
**Hope.** See on Rom. 5:4; 8:24; 12:12.
**Set before us.** Or, “lying, before us.” The hope of salvation is set before all and may be grasped by all.

19.zh:
我們有這指望，如同靈魂的錨，又堅固又牢靠，且通入幔內。

**錨。**在比喻上的一個改變。錨使船隻在暴風中穩定，使它不漂到礁石上。錨有滑脫的時候。但“指望”的錨卻不是這樣。在聖經中，關於錨的比喻只在這裡出現過。
**通入。**就是進入的指望。
**幔。**katapetasma，“簾，”“幕。”該詞在《新約》中出現六次。三次指耶穌釘十字架時聖殿中撕裂的幔子（太27:51；可15:38；路23:45）。其他三次出現在《希伯來書》中（來6:19；9:3；10:20）。Katapetasma在七十士譯本中指聖所時描述：一，把聖所和至聖所隔開的幔子（出26:31,33）；二，會幕門口的門簾（出26:37；36:37；民3:26）；三，院子的門簾（出38:18）。會幕門口的門簾和將聖所與至聖所隔開的內幔都被稱為katapetasma，說明來9:3的“第二幔子[katapetasma]”是是裡面的幔子。問那麼作者在來6:19所說我們有指望通入幔內，指的是哪個幔子呢？
一些非復臨派的聖經學者教導說，基督在昇天之後立即進入天上的至聖所開始祂的工作。他們認為這裡的katapetasma是指的把至聖所和聖所隔開的幔子。他們注意到“通入幔內”譯自希臘語esōteron tou katapetasmatos。這個短語在七十士譯本中出現四次（出26:33；利16:2,12,15），都是指至聖所。但如果這裡的“幔內”是指將聖所與至聖所分開的幔子，不一定就意味基督昇天後即開始在至聖所中從事中保的工作（見下面第一點）。
下面是“幔內”的三種解釋，均符合安息日復臨信徒有關聖所的觀點。
一，“幔”是指把聖所與至聖所分開的幔子。但保羅說的是基督在就任大祭司時進入至聖所，將它連同聖所的其餘部分一同奉獻。在但9:24中提到了這次奉獻（見該節註釋）。地上的聖所建立以後的抹油中預表了這一奉獻（出40章；參出30:26-29）。
二，在來6:19中，保羅沒有給“幔”下定義。他要人注意的不是幔子，而是“幔內”（或“幔後”），就是我們的大祭司基督服務的地方。換一句話說，保羅並不是用“幔”（katapetasma）對天上聖所的結構作技術性的討論，而是一種修辭的手法，描述那把看得見和看不見的，地上的和天上的事物分開的東西。所以“幔內”只是指上帝的臨格。根據這種觀點，所指望的就是進到基督已經親自前往的上帝面前（第20節；參來9:24）。
三，保羅在《希伯來書》的其他地方特別提到把聖所與至聖所分開的幔子為“第二幔子”（來9:3）。所以當他只說“幔子”時（來6:19），一定是指會幕門口的簾子。況且地上聖所的崇祀所預表的是天上的聖所及其崇祀的程序，所以當基督升到天上時，祂就“進入” 第一層聖所，開始祂天上服務的第一個階段（見《善惡之爭》420頁）。
**內。**esōteros，“裡面，”“後面。”該詞在《新約》中只出現在本節和徒16:24，那裡指保羅和西拉被下到內監。Esōteros七十士譯本里較為常見（見出26:33；利16:2,12,15等）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第72頁；《證言》卷一第300，566頁；《證言》卷二第304頁；《證言》卷五第113頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–20節）**。《善惡之爭》第421，489頁；《今日的生活》第8頁；《證言》卷五第742頁。
19.en:
**Anchor.** A change in metaphor. An anchor holds a ship in a storm and keeps it from drifting on the rocks. There are times when anchors slip. But not so with the anchor of “hope.” The metaphor of an anchor occurs only here in Scripture.
**Which entereth.** That is, the hope entereth.
**Within.** Gr. esōteros, “inner,” “behind.” The word occurs in the NT only here and in Acts 16:24, where it describes the inner prison into which Paul and Silas were cast. Esōteros is more frequent in the LXX (see Ex. 26:33; Lev. 16:2, 12, 15; etc.).
**Veil.** Gr. katapetasma, “curtain,” “veil.” The word occurs six times in the NT. Three times it is used of the veil of the Temple that was rent at the time of the crucifixion (Matt. 27:51; Mark 15:38; Luke 23:45). The other occurrences are in Hebrews (ch. 6:19; 9:3; 10:20). In the references to the sanctuary in the LXX katapetasma is used to describe (1) the curtain that separated the holy and most holy places (Ex. 26:31, 33), (2) the curtain at the door of the tabernacle (Ex. 26:37; 36:37; Num. 3:26), (3) the curtain for the gate of the court (Ex. 38:18). The fact that the curtain at the door of the tabernacle and the inner curtain separating the holy from the most holy place were both called katapetasma provides a simple explanation for the use of the term “second veil [katapetasma]” in Heb. 9:3 to describe the inner curtain. The question is: To which curtain does the author refer in ch. 6:19, as the one within which our hope enters?
Some non-Adventist Bible students who teach that Christ, immediately upon His ascension, entered on His work in the most holy place of the heavenly sanctuary hold that katapetasma here refers to the curtain separating the most holy place from the holy place. They note that “within the veil” is a translation of the Greek phrase esōteron tou katapetasmatos, which, in its four occurrences in the LXX (Ex. 26:33; Lev. 16:2, 12, 15), always describes the most holy place. However, it does not necessarily follow that if “the veil” here refers to the veil dividing the holy from the most holy place, Christ therefore began, at His ascension, to carry on His mediatorial work in the most holy place (see under “1” below).
Following are three possible explanations of the expression “within the veil,” all of which are consonant with the Seventh-day Adventist view of the sanctuary.
**1. “The veil” means the dividing curtain between the two apartments.** But Paul is speaking of Christ’s entrance into the most holy place of the heavenly sanctuary in order to dedicate it, along with the rest of the sanctuary, upon His assumption of His high-priestly office. This dedication is mentioned in Dan. 9:24 (see comment there) and typified in the anointing of the earthly sanctuary following its erection (Ex. 40; cf. ch. 30:26–29).
**2. In Heb.** 6:19 Paul leaves the word “veil” undefined. He wishes to call attention, not to the veil, but to that which is “within [or “behind”] the veil,” namely, the place where Christ our High Priest ministers. In other words, Paul is using the word “veil” (katapetasma), not in terms of a technical discussion of the structure of the heavenly sanctuary, but as a figure of speech to describe that which divides the seen from the unseen, the earthly from the heavenly. Hence, “within the veil” means simply to be in the presence of God. According to this view, hope is represented as entering the very presence of God, where Christ Himself has gone (v. 20; cf. ch. 9:24).
**3.** Paul, elsewhere in Hebrews, specifically describes the veil separating the holy from the most holy place, as “the second veil” (ch. 9:3). Hence, when he speaks simply of “the veil” (ch. 6:19) he must refer to the veil at the door of the tabernacle. Further, inasmuch as the heavenly sanctuary, and the sequence of its services, was prefigured by the earthly, when Christ ascended prefigured by the earthly, when Christ ascended to heaven He “entered” the holy place—the first apartment—to begin the first phase of His heavenly ministry (see GC 420).

20.zh:
作先鋒的耶穌，既照著麥基洗德的等次成了永遠的大祭司，就為我們進入幔內。

**先鋒。**prodromos，“走（或“跑”）在前面。”該詞在《新約》中只出現在本節。它在七十士譯本中曾出現兩次，一次在民13:20，另一次在賽28:4，表示初熟的（prodromoi）無花果。該詞用在耶穌身上似乎表示祂已先到了上帝面前；我們也要跟從祂去。這種觀念與來2:10的archēgos（見該詞註釋）相似。
**永遠的大祭司。**見來5:6註釋。作者巧妙地回到了他在5:11至6:19暫時放下的主題。第7章詳細論述這個主題。
20.en:
**Whither.** Or, “where.”
**Forerunner.** Gr. prodromos, “going [or “running”] before.” The word occurs only here in the NT. It occurs twice in the LXX, once in Num. 13:20 and once in Isa. 28:4, of first-ripe (prodromoi) figs. Applied to Jesus, the thought seems to be that He has gone before to be in the presence of God and we will follow after Him. The idea is similar to that expressed in Heb. 2:10 in the term archēgos (see comment there).
**High priest for ever.** See on ch. 5:6. The author now skillfully comes back to the topic from which he digressed in chs. 5:11 6:19. The subject is fully discussed in ch. 7.

1.en: **Melchisedec.** The historical facts mentioned in this verse are recapitulated from Gen. 14:18–20 (see comment there).
1.zh:
這麥基洗德就是撒冷王，又是至高神的祭司，本是長遠為祭司的。他當亞伯拉罕殺敗諸王回來的時候，就迎接他，給他祝福。

**麥基洗德。**本節扼要重述了創14:18-20（見該處註釋）的史實。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第578頁；《先祖與先知》第136，157，703頁；《證言》卷三第393頁。

12.en:
**The priesthood being changed.** That is, from the Levitical to the Melchisedec.
**Change also of the law.** The law provided that only the Levites could serve at the tabernacle, and that only the sons of Aaron could be priests. Furthermore, it regulated the services of the priests with reference to the dispensation in which they served. It would be necessary to change the law if a priest were selected from another tribe (v. 13) and a new order of things were introduced (ch. 8:13).
12.zh:
祭司的職任既已更改，律法也必須更改。

**祭司的職任既已更改。**就是從利未變到了麥基洗德。
**律法也必須更改。**律法規定只有利未人才能在會幕中服務，只有亞倫的子孫才能擔任祭司。律法還規定了分派給祭司所擔任的各項工作。如果要從另一個支派（第13節）選立祭司並採用新的制度（來8:13），就必須更改律法。

28.en:
**The law.** See vs. 11, 12, 16.
**Maketh men.** Or, “appoints men.”
**Infirmity.** Or, “weakness” (cf. ch. 5:2).
**The oath.** See vs. 20, 21.
**Since the law.** The ceremonial system expired at the cross (see on Rom. 6:14; Eph. 2:15; Col. 2:14). Christ assumed His high-priestly office following the expiration of the law that regulated the Levitical priesthood.
**Maketh the Son.** Or, “appoints One who is Son.” The article is not present in the Greek. However, to translate “a Son” instead of “the Son” does not correctly convey the force of the Greek. The absence of the article lays stress on quality; hence the preferred rendering, “One who is Son” (cf. on Dan. 7:9, 13).
**Consecrated.** Gr. teleioō, “to perfect” (see on ch. 2:10).
**For evermore.** In contrast with the temporary service of the Levitical priests.
28.zh:
律法本是立軟弱的人為大祭司；但在律法以後起誓的話，是立兒子為大祭司，乃是成全到永遠的。

**律法。**見第11,12,16節。
**立。**或“指定。”
**軟弱。**或“虛弱”（參來5:2）。
**在律法以後。**儀文制度在基督釘十字架時終止了（見羅6:14；弗2:15；西2:14註釋）。基督在利未人祭司律法到期之後才就任大祭司的。
**起誓。**見第20,21節。
**立兒子。**原文沒有冠詞，故強調品質（參但7:9,13註釋）。
**成全。**teleioō，“完成”（見來2:10註釋）。
**到永遠。**與利未人祭司職任的暫時性形成對照。

16.en:
**Carnal commandment.** Doubtless called “carnal” with reference to the fact that the commandment specified succession by physical descent (Ex. 29:29, 30; Num. 20:26, 28).
**Power.** Note the contrast of this word with “law.”
**Endless.** Gr. akatalutos, “indestructible,” “not subject to dissolution.”
16.zh:
他成為祭司，並不是照屬肉體的條例，乃是照無窮（原文是不能毀壞）之生命的大能。

**屬肉體的條例。**無疑指按肉身繼任的條例（出29:29,30；民20:26,28）。
**無窮。**akatalutos，“不能毀壞，”“不會分解。”
**大能。**注意該詞與“律法”的對比。

27.en:
**Who needeth not daily.** There is no record of the high priest’s bringing a sin offering daily. There was an offering commanded to be offered daily by Aaron and his successors, but this appears to be a meal offering and not a sin offering (Lev. 6:20–22). The difficulty is therefore with the statement that the high priest of old presented a sin offering daily, and that Christ did not need to do this.
This difficulty has been explained by the consideration that whatever services the priests performed, they did as deputies of the high priest. They officiated in his place, and what they did was counted as though the high priest himself did it. They were merely helpers, and as they did offer sin offerings daily, the high priest can be said to offer daily.
**For his own sins.** On the Day of Atonement the high priest offered first for his own sins and then for the sins of the people (Lev. 16:11, 15). This was necessary. Being sinful, he could not appear before God in the most holy place unless and until he had brought an offering for himself. Christ did not need to do this. He was sinless.
**This he did once.** The question has been raised as to what is meant by “this.” Did Christ offer for His own sins once, as did the high priest, and then for the people? Christ had no sin of His own. The only sins He had were those He bore for us. He was made to be sin (2 Cor. 5:21). When, therefore, He offered Himself once, He provided for all the sins He carried. Those sins were our sins, which He bore in His body on the tree. They were His sins only as He had taken upon Himself the responsibility for them. He bore them vicariously.
**Offered up himself.** Christ was both priest and victim.
27.zh:
他不像那些大祭司，每日必須先為自己的罪，後為百姓的罪獻祭；因為他只一次將自己獻上，就把這事成全了。

**祂不像那些大祭司，每日必須。**聖經上並沒有大祭司每日獻贖罪祭的記錄。經上確有一個要亞倫和他的繼承人每日獻祭的命令，但這顯然是素祭，而不是贖罪祭（利6:20-22）。難點在於這節經文說古時的大祭司每日獻贖罪祭，而基督不必要這樣做。
這個難點可以這樣解釋：祭司們的一切侍奉都代表著大祭司。他們是代替大祭司工作的。他們所作的一切都算為大祭司本人作的。他們只是助手。他們既每日獻贖罪祭，就可以說成是大祭司每日獻祭了。
**為自己的罪。**到了贖罪日，大祭司先為自己的罪獻祭，然後為百姓的罪獻祭（利16:11,15）。這是必要的。大祭司自己既然有罪，他在為自己獻贖罪祭之前，就不能來到至聖所上帝面前。基督不需要這樣作。因為祂是無罪的。
**祂只一次將自己獻上。**基督既是祭司又是祭牲。
**就把這事成全了。**有人問“這事”是什麼意思。難道基督象大祭司那樣為自己的罪一次獻祭，然後再為百姓獻祭嗎？基督自己並沒有罪。祂只是承擔我們的罪孽。祂替我們成為罪（林後5:21）。所以當祂一次將自己獻上時，祂就除去了祂所承擔的一切罪。這些罪原是我們的。祂在木頭上親身擔當了這些罪。祂承擔了別人的罪。祂是代人受過的。

14.en:
**Juda.** See Micah 5:2; Matt. 1:1; Mark 10:47, 48; Luke 3:33; Rom. 1:3; Rev. 5:5.
**Moses spake nothing.** The laws regulating the priesthood were given through Moses (Num. 3; 4).
14.zh:
我們的主分明是從猶大出來的；但這支派，摩西並沒有提到祭司。

**猶大。**見彌5:2；太1:1；可10:47,48；路3:33；羅1:3；啟5:5。
**摩西並沒有提到。**有關祭司制度的律法是藉著摩西所賜的（民3；4章）。

3.en:
**Without father, without mother.** These words have given rise to the speculation that Melchisedec was some supernatural being, as he must of necessity have been if he was actually without parents, without beginning of days and without end of life. Such an assertion in its totality can be literally true of the persons of the Godhead only. However, it is not necessary to take this view of the wording. The author may simply mean that there is no record of who Melchisedec’s father and mother were.
**Without descent.** Gr. agenealogētos, literally, “without genealogy.” The Jews were very careful to record and preserve their genealogies. This was especially true concerning the priests (see Ezra 2:61–63). No one could serve as priest unless he belonged to the family of Aaron of the tribe of Levi, and this he must be able to prove without any doubt whatever. If there was a break in the line somewhere, he would be counted out and thus lose the privileges accorded the priests. For this reason every Jew, and particularly the priests, preserved carefully their genealogical records. Of melchisedec no genealogy exists.
**Beginning of days.** That is, there is no record of his birth, or of his death, as indicated by the phrase “nor end of life.”
**Made like.** Or, “resembling.” Melchisedec was a type of Christ. Nothing is known of his birth or death because there is no record of either. All this fits into the picture of Christ, who had no beginning or end of days (see on John 1:1–3).
**Abideth a priest.** There is no record of the termination of his high-priestly office.
3.zh:
他無父，無母，無族譜，無生之始，無命之終，乃是與神的兒子相似。

**無父、無母。**麥基洗德既無父，無母，無族譜，無生之始，無命之終，有人就據此認為他是超自然的生靈。嚴格地說，超自然的生靈只能指上帝的位格上。但這樣的措辭不一定如此理解。作者可能只是說沒有麥基洗德父母的記錄。
**無族譜。**agenealogētos，猶太人很注意記錄和保存他們的家譜。尤其是祭司（見拉2:61-63）。只有利未支派的亞倫家族的人，在確認無疑的情況下，才可以擔任祭司。如果家譜中斷了，他就會被排除在外，喪失了祭司的特權。因此每一個猶太人，特別是祭司，都認真保存他們的家譜。可是麥基洗德卻沒有家譜。
**無生之始，無命之終。**就是沒有出生記錄和死亡記錄。
**相似。**麥基洗德是基督的預表。關於他的出生與死亡毫無所知，因為沒有他出生和死亡的記錄。這一切都適合於基督的形象，因為祂既無生之始，也無命之終（見約1:1-3註釋）。有文本還在後面加上“長期擔任祭司”。即沒有他大祭司職務終止的記錄。

7.en:
**Without all contradiction.** Or, “apart from all dispute.”
**The less … the better.** The matter of superiority is settled by the fact that Abraham was the one who paid tithe and who received a blessing.
7.zh:
從來位分大的給位分小的祝福，這是駁不倒的理。

**大的……小的。**亞伯拉罕是繳納十分之一併接受祝福的事實，解決了地位誰高的問題。
**駁不倒的理。**或“無可爭議的。”

26.en:
**Became.** Gr. prepō, “to suit,” “to be fitting,” “to be becoming.” Compare the use of prepō in ch. 2:10. It was fitting that we should have a high priest of Christ’s nature.
**Holy.** Gr. hosios, “devout,” “pious,” “pleasing to God” (see on Acts 2:27).
**Harmless.** Gr. akakos, “guileless,” “innocent,” not vindictive.
**Undefiled.** Gr. amiantos, “pure, in a religious and moral sense.” Compare the use of the word in Heb. 13:4; James 1:27; 1 Peter 1:4.
**Separate from sinners.** Or, “having been separated from sinners.” Some believe this refers to Christ’s ability to mingle with sinners and yet be separate from them during the incarnation. Others believe the description is of Christ, not in His incarnation, but in His role as high priest, and that therefore “separate from sinners” refers to the completion of His work for sinners as far as His sacrificial death was concerned (see ch. 9:28). They believe the phrase should be interpreted in the light of the following phrase, which refers to Christ’s removal from this world and thus from literal contact with sinners, to be in the very presence of God. Those who hold this second view believe as truly as do those who hold the first, that Christ was ever “holy, harmless, undefiled.”
**Made higher than the heavens.** Christ, in His exaltation, is at the Father’s right hand. It is this kind of high priest that is fitting for us.
26.zh:
像這樣聖潔、無邪惡、無玷汙、遠離罪人、高過諸天的大祭司，原是與我們合宜的。

**聖潔。**hosios，“虔誠，”“討上帝喜悅”（見徒2:27註釋）。
**無邪惡。**akakos，“不狡詐的，”“無害的，”不報復的。
**無玷汙。**amiantos，“宗教和道德意義上的純潔。”參該詞用於來13:4；雅1:27和彼前1:4中。
**遠離罪人。**或“與罪人分開。”有人認為這是指基督道成肉身時雖在罪人中間，卻與他們分別。有人認為這不是指基督道成肉身，而是指祂擔任大祭司的時候，所以“遠離罪人”是說祂犧牲受死，完成了為罪人所作的工作（見來9:28）。他們認為應按下面的句子來進行解釋，指基督離開世界，來到上帝面前，不再與罪人接觸。持這兩種觀點的人都認為基督永遠是“聖潔、無邪惡、無玷汙的。”
**高過諸天。**基督昇天後坐在天父的右邊。祂是適合於我們的大祭司。
**合宜的。**prepō，“適合於”。參該詞用於來2:10。我們有基督這樣性質的大祭司是合適的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第570頁；《歷代願望》第25頁；見來9:14懷愛倫註釋。

15.en: **More evident.** This seems to refer to the proposition set forth in v. 12, namely, that a change in law was necessary. Some hold that it refers to the temporary character of the Levitical priesthood. The prophecy referred to in v. 17, predicting that the new priesthood would be of a different order, makes it more evident that there must be a change in the laws of the priesthood, or that the Levitical priesthood was provisionary.
15.zh:
倘若照麥基洗德的樣式，另外興起一位祭司來，我的話更是顯而易見的了。

似乎是指12節的主張，就是需要更改律法。有人認為這是指祭司制度的暫時性。第17節所提到的預言，說新的祭司制度將按照不同的等次，所以祭司制度的暫時性和祭司的律法需要改變就“更是顯而易見的了”。

25.en:
**Uttermost.** Gr. pantelēs “completely,” “fully,” “wholly,” “forever,” “for all time.” Commentators are divided as to which meaning applies here. Both are true, for Christ saves both completely and for all time.
**Come unto God.** See on v. 19.
**Ever liveth.** See on v. 24.
**Make intercession.** Gr. entugchanō (see on Rom. 8:34).
25.zh:
凡靠著他進到神面前的人，他都能拯救到底；因為他是長遠活著，替他們祈求。

**進到上帝面前。**見19節註釋。
**到底。**pantelēs，“完全，”“永遠”。關於該詞的解釋註釋家有分歧。兩種意思都對，因為基督的拯救既是完全的，又是永遠的。
**長遠活著。**見24節註釋。
**祈求。**entugchanō（見羅8:34註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒家庭》第544頁；《基督比喻實訓》第149，156頁；《安息日學訓言》第111頁；《歷代願望》第166，751，835頁；《基督教育原理》第178，184頁；《善惡之爭》第482頁；《傳道良助》第155頁；《福山寶訓》第9頁；《服務真詮》第243，424頁；《今日的生活》第33頁；《醫療佈道論》第33，181頁；《給青年人的信息》第407頁；《拾級就主》第102頁；《論節制》第280頁；《給傳道人的證言》第20頁；《證言》卷一第543頁；《證言》卷二第60，321頁；《證言》卷五第200，633，741頁；《證言》卷六第123，231頁；《證言》卷八第287頁；《論福利工作》第193頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（25–27節）**。見羅8: 34懷愛倫註釋。

5.en: **Commandment to take tithes.** The Levites had the right to receive tithes by virtue of a divine command (see Num. 18:21). However, they were not the first to take tithes. Melchisedec did so before them. If they were divinely ordained, so was Melchisedec. And the fact that “even the Patriarch Abraham” paid tithes to Melchisedec shows that Melchisedec had the highest endorsement. If the Levites were authorized by God to receive tithes, Melchisedec was even more so.
5.zh:
那得祭司職任的利未子孫，領命照例向百姓取十分之一，這百姓是自己的弟兄，雖是從亞伯拉罕身（原文是腰）中生的，還是照例取十分之一；

**領命照例向百姓取十分之一。**利未人有權接受十分之一，是由於上帝的命令（見民18:21）。但他們不是最早收取十分之一的。麥基洗德比他們還要早。利未人既為上帝所任命，麥基洗德當然也是。連“先祖亞伯拉罕”也向麥基洗德納十分之一，說明麥基洗德得到了可最高的認可。上帝既授權利未人接受十分之一，麥基洗德就更不用說是上帝授權的了。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第336頁。

11.en:
**Perfection.** The Levitical priesthood and the ceremonial law were provisional and shadowy, pointing forward to the work that Christ was to perform. Perfection came not through the law but through the Christ to whom it pointed. This thought is further developed in chs. 9; 10.
**Law.** Here, the entire Jewish system instituted at Sinai (see on Gal. 3:17).
**What further need.** The Levitical system was never intended to be an end in itself. It was to point men to Christ, in whom alone is salvation. If the system could have provided salvation apart from the work of Christ, then there would have been no need for the ministry of Christ.
11.zh:
從前百姓在利未人祭司職任以下受律法，倘若藉這職任能得完全，又何用另外興起一位祭司，照麥基洗德的等次，不照亞倫的等次呢？

**律法。**指在西奈山設立的整個猶太制度（見加3:17註釋）。
**完全。**祭司制度和儀文律法都是暫時的，是影子，指向基督所要作的工作。“完全”並不是藉著律法而來的，而是藉著律法所指的基督而來的。第9和10章進一步闡述了這種思想。
**又何用另外。**祭司制度本身從來就不是目的。它是要向人指出基督，只有在祂裡面才能得救。如果祭司制度離開基督的工作仍能提供救恩的話，那就不需要基督的服務了。

13.en:
**He.** That is, Christ (v. 14).
**Another tribe.** See on v. 14.
**Gave attendance.** Or, “officiated.”
13.zh:
因為這話所指的人本屬別的支派，那支派裡從來沒有一人伺候祭壇。

**這話所指的人。**就是基督（第14節）。
**別的支派。**見第14節註釋。
**伺候。**或“供職。”

2.en:
**Abraham gave a tenth.** See on Gen. 14:20. Abraham would not have given Melchisedec a tenth of all had he not known him to be a priest, and hence to have a right to receive the tithe.
There has been much discussion as to who Melchisedec was. Information concerning him is meager. He is mentioned in the OT only in Gen. 14:18–20; Ps. 110:4, and in the NT only in the book of Hebrews. There are some who believe that He was Christ; others, the Holy Spirit; others, Shem; still others, a supernatural being from another world. In the absence of good evidence for any of these positions, this commentary holds that Melchisedec was one of the contemporaries of Abraham, king of one of the small principalities of that time (see on Gen. 14:18). He is set forth in Hebrews as a type of Christ, a representation based on the Messianic prediction in Ps. 110:4.
**King of righteousness.** Attention is called to the name because of its significance when applied to the Messiah (see on Ps. 72:3; 85:10).
**King of Salem.** See on Gen. 14:18.
**Peace.** A term appropriately applied to the Messiah (see Isa. 9:5, 6; Zech. 9:10). See Ps. 72:3; 85:10, where righteousness and peace are mentioned together as characteristics of the Messianic kingdom.
2.zh:
亞伯拉罕也將自己所得來的，取十分之一給他。他頭一個名翻出來就是仁義王，他又名撒冷王，就是平安王的意思。

**亞伯拉罕也將自己所得來的，取十分之一給他。**見創14:20註釋。亞伯拉罕如果不知道麥基洗德是祭司，有權接受什一，就不會將自己所得的十分之一給他了。
麥基洗德的身份有許多說法。有關他的信息很少。《舊約》只在創14:18-20和詩110:4中提到他。《新約》只在《希伯來書》中提到他。有人認為他是基督；有人認為他是聖靈；有人認為他是閃；也有人認為他是外星球的超自然生靈。上述說法均缺少有力的證據。故本註釋認為麥基洗德是亞伯拉罕的同時代人；是當時一個小國的國王（見創14:18註釋）。《希伯來書》把他作為基督的預表，依據的是詩110:4的彌賽亞。
**仁義王。**讓人注意這個稱呼是因為它用於彌賽亞時的意義（見詩72:3；85:10註釋）。
**撒冷王。**見創14:18註釋。
**平安王。**指彌賽亞十分合適（見賽9:5,6；亞9:10）。見詩72:3；85:10，公義和平相提並論，作為彌賽亞國度的特徵）。

4.en:
**How great.** The Jews held Abraham in high esteem (see John 8:52). The author of Hebrews now proceeds to prove that Melchisedec was still greater. And if he was greater, then Christ’s priesthood, which was after the manner of Melchisedec (see on Heb. 5:6), was greater than the Aaronic.
**Even.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 10) between retaining and omitting this word.
**Patriarch.** Gr. patriarchēs, “father of a nation.” Abraham is here called “patriarch” to heighten the effect. Melchisedec was so great that “even the patriarch” paid him tithe. In doing so, Abraham acknowledged the superior, priestly authority of Melchisedec.
**Tenth.** See v. 2.
**Spoils.** Doubtless the spoils of the recent battle (Gen. 14:14–16).
4.zh:
你們想一想，先祖亞伯拉罕將自己所擄來上等之物取十分之一給他，這人是何等尊貴呢！

**先祖。**patriarchēs，“一國之父。”稱亞伯拉罕為“先祖”是為了加強效果。麥基洗德非常偉大，連“先祖”付給他十分之一。亞伯拉罕這樣作，就是承認麥基洗德至高的祭司權威。
**擄來上等之物。**無疑指最近一次戰爭的戰利品（創14:14-16）。
**十分之一。**見第2節註釋。
**何等尊貴。**猶太人非常敬重亞伯拉罕（見約8:52）。《希伯來書》的作者現在要證明麥基洗德比他更加偉大。如果麥基洗德更加偉大，那麼按照他等次的基督祭司職任（見來5:6註釋），就比亞倫的祭司職任更加偉大。

8.en:
**Here.** That is, in the Levitical system.
**There.** That is, with reference to the Melchisedec priesthood.
**He liveth.** This, of course, would not be literally true of Melchisedec, nor is the explanation adequate that this simply means that there is no record in the Bible of Melchisedec’s death. It appears that these words reach beyond Melchisedec to the greater One whom he represents. Of Christ it is affirmed that “he ever liveth” (v. 25). The Melchisedec priesthood lives in Jesus Christ’s priesthood.
8.zh:
在這裡收十分之一的都是必死的人；但在那裡收十分之一的，有為他作見證的說，他是活的；

**這裡。**在祭司制度中。
**那裡。**指麥基洗德的祭司職務。
**他是活的。**這當然不符合麥基洗德的實際情況，也不足以解釋聖經中沒有麥基洗德死亡記錄的問題。這句話似乎超越了麥基洗德，乃是指他所代表的那更偉大的一位。聖經論到基督說：“他是長遠活著”（第25節）。麥基洗德的祭司職任藉著耶穌基督的祭司職任而“活”著。

9.en: **Levi … payed tithes.** This observation is set forth to give further evidence that the Melchisedec priesthood was superior to the Levitical. The manner in which Levi paid tithe to Melchisedec is shown in v. 10.
9.zh:
並且可說那受十分之一的利未，也是藉著亞伯拉罕納了十分之一。

這裡進一步證明了麥基洗德的祭司職任比利未人優越。第10節說明了利未納十分之一給麥基洗德的方式。

10.en: **In the loins.** Whatever Abraham the patriarch did, his posterity did also. Thus when he paid tithe Levi paid tithe. This the author cites as another proof of the greatness of Melchisedec.
10.zh:
因為麥基洗德迎接亞伯拉罕的時候，利未已經在他先祖的身（原文是腰）中。

先祖亞伯拉罕所作的，他的後裔也作了。他繳納十分之一，就等於是利未繳納的。作者以此作為證明麥基洗德偉大的又一個證據。

6.en:
**Descent is not counted from them.** See on v. 3. Only Levites could receive tithe. Melchisedec was not a Levite, and yet he received tithe from Abraham. Abraham has met a man greater than he is. He recognizes Melchisedec’s superiority and pays the priest tithe.
**Blessed him.** See Gen. 14:19.
**Had the promises.** See on ch. 6:13, 15.
6.zh:
獨有麥基洗德，不與他們同譜，倒收納亞伯拉罕的十分之一，為那蒙應許的亞伯拉罕祝福。

**不與他們同譜。**見第3節註釋。只有利未人可以接受十分之一。麥基洗德不是利未人，但他卻接受了亞伯拉罕的十分之一。亞伯拉罕遇見了一個比他更偉大的人。他承認麥基洗德的崇高地位，並繳納十分之一給那位祭司。
**為亞伯拉罕祝福。**見創14:19。
**蒙應許的。**見來6:13,15註釋。

17.zh:
因為有給他作見證的說：你是照著麥基洗德的等次永遠為祭司。

作者一再引用詩110:4的這句話（來5:6,10；6:20；7:21），以此作為他的論據。凡人不能永遠為祭司。一位利未人祭司只能供職若干年。所以如果有一位永遠供職的要來到，他就必須超越凡人，超越利未人。要這樣的祭司任職，改變祭司的律法就“更是顯而易見的了”（第15節）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。(創14:18-20；詩110:4)麥基洗德等次的大祭司——以特殊的方式所任命的大祭司是要代表基督的。祂是照著麥基洗德的等次永遠為大祭司的。這個祭司的等次沒有交給別人，或由別人來代替的(《救贖論：基督第一次降臨》第14頁)。。
17.en: **Priest for ever.** The author returns to this statement from Ps. 110:4 again and again (Heb. 5:6, 10; 6:20; 7:21). On this rests his argument. No mere man could be a priest forever. The Levitical priests served only a few years. If, therefore, one is to come who is to serve forever, he must be more than a man, more than a Levite. Hence, it is “far more evident” (v. 15) that there must be a change of the priestly law if that kind of priest is to officiate.

18.zh:
先前的條例，因軟弱無益，所以廢掉了，

**先前的。**或“以前的。”
**因。**第18，19節之間原文的關係如下：“一方面廢掉先前的條例……，另一方面引進了更美的指望。”
**軟弱無益。**這是上帝親自設立的，原來並不是這樣。它軟弱無益是因為百姓對它的態度。他們以律法本身作為目的，認為順從律法就能得救。福音傳給他們，他們卻沒有受益，因為沒有與信心相結合（來4:2）。
**廢掉。**比“更改”（第12節）的語氣更強。祭司制度的律法要延續到大祭司耶穌基督的就任。然後就廢除了。
18.en:
**For there is.** According to the Greek the connection between vs. 18, 19 is as follows: “There is, on the one hand, a disannulling of the commandment … and on the other, the bringing in of a better hope.”
**A disannulling.** A stronger term than “being changed” (v. 12). The law of the Levitical priesthood was designed to operate only until Jesus Christ, the great High Priest, took over His office. Then it was to be annulled.
**Going before.** Or, “preceding,” “former.”
**Weakness and unprofitableness.** Not that it was so inherently for God Himself had instituted it. But it failed because of the people’s attitude toward it. They made the law an end in itself and believed that obedience to it would bring them salvation. They had the gospel preached unto them, but it did not profit them, not being mixed with faith (ch. 4:2).

19.zh:
（律法原來一無所成）就引進了更美的指望；靠這指望，我們便可以進到神面前。

**律法原來一無所成。**就律法本身而言。這並不意味著舊約時代的人就不可能得救了。“完全”是有可能的，獲得的方法與今日一樣，就是信耶穌基督。“律法是我們蒙訓的師傅，引我們到基督那裡……但這信既然來到，我們從此就不在師傅的手下了”（見加3:24,25註釋）。
**引進了更美的指望。**關於這句話與上下文的關係，見18節註釋。更美的指望集中在基督身上。祂代替了利未人的祭司職務。這就是“擺在我們前頭的”指望，也就是我們的“錨”，“且通往幔內”（來6:18-20）。
**進到上帝面前。**這曾是利未人祭司制度的目的，但因錯誤的教訓和管理，人以為上帝遠離了他們。現在大祭司耶穌基督已進入“幔內”（來6:19），坐在“高天至大者的右邊”（來1:3），所以人可以“坦然無懼地來到施恩的寶座前”（來4:16），以完全的信心進到上帝面前。
19.en:
**The law made nothing perfect.** That is, the law in and of itself. This does not mean that salvation was impossible for men in OT times. Perfection was possible, but by the same means it is achieved today—faith in Jesus Christ. “The law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ. … But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster” (see on Gal. 3:24, 25).
**Bringing in of a better hope.** For the connection of this phrase with its context see on v. 18. The better hope centers in Christ. He takes the place of the Levitical priesthood. This is the hope that is “set before us,” our “anchor,” “which entereth into that within the veil” (ch. 6:18–20).
**Draw nigh unto God.** This had been the purpose of the Levitical priesthood, but through faulty instruction and administration men felt that God was far removed from them. Now Jesus Christ, the High Priest, has entered “within the veil” (ch. 6:19). He is seated “on the right hand of the Majesty on high” (ch. 1:3); therefore men may “come boldly unto the throne of grace” (ch. 4:16) and in full assurance draw near to God.

20.zh:
再者，耶穌為祭司，並不是不起誓立的。

**並不是不起誓立的。**見來6:17註釋。
20.en: **Not without an oath.** See on ch. 6:17.

21.zh:
至於那些祭司，原不是起誓立的，只有耶穌是起誓立的；因為那立他的對他說：主起了誓，決不後悔，你是永遠為祭司。

**起誓立的。**這裡的對比顯示麥基洗德大祭司職任的優越性。關於起誓的重要性，見來6:17註釋。
**後悔。**metamelomai，“改變主意”（見林後7:8,9註釋）。
有文本在本節最後還有“照著麥基洗德的等次”。如第17節。
21.en:
**With an oath.** The contrast is here set forth to show the superiority of the Melchisedec high priesthood. For the importance of the oath see on ch. 6:17.
**Repent.** Gr. metamelomai, “to change one’s mind,” “to regret” (see on 2 Cor. 7:8, 9).
**After the order of Melchisedec.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 10) as to the retention or omission of this phrase. It is fully attested in v. 17.

22.zh:
既是起誓立的，耶穌就作了更美之約的中保。

**既是起誓立的。**而利未人的祭司職任則依賴暫時的條例。
**耶穌。**這個名字強調祂的人性（見太1:1註釋）。
**約。**diathēkē（見加3:15註釋。見太26:28；林前11:25；林後3:6；路1:72；加3:15；來8:6-10等）。在本節指的是新約（diathēkē）。這是作者在來8:6-13中闡述的主題。
**中保。**egguos，“保證，”“擔保。”指一個人為履行某個協議而負責任或擔保。這裡的協議是“更美之約”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。見來8:6，7懷愛倫註釋。
22.en:
**By so much.** That is, in that it was confirmed by an oath, whereas the Levitical priesthood rested on a temporary command.
**Jesus.** This name emphasizes his human side (see on Matt. 1:1).
**Surety.** Gr. egguos, “a pledge,” “a guarantee.” The word here has the meaning of one who becomes responsible for, or guarantees, the performance of some agreement, here, the “better testament.”
**Testament.** Gr. diathēkē (see on Gal. 3:15). This word is rendered both “testament” (Matt. 26:28; 1 Cor. 11:25; 2 Cor. 3:6; etc.) and “covenant” (Luke 1:72; Gal. 3:15; Heb. 8:6–10). In the text under consideration “covenant” would be a preferable translation, because the author is speaking of the new covenant (diathēkē), a subject he develops in ch. 8:6–13. Diathēkē is the word used elsewhere for “covenant.”

23.zh:
那些成為祭司的，數目本來多，是因為有死阻隔，不能長久。

這裡把利未制度下的許多祭司與麥基洗德等次下的一位祭司進行對比。
23.en: **Many priests.** The contrast here is between the many priests under the Levitical system and the one priest under the order of Melchisedec.

24.zh:
這位既是永遠常存的，他祭司的職任就長久不更換。

**不更換。**aparabatos，“永久的，”“不變的。”利未人擔任祭司因死亡而不能持久。但基督卻“長遠活著，替他們祈求”（來7:25；參啟1:18）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第52頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（24–26節）**。見來4:14-16懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（24–28節）**。見羅8:26，34. 懷愛倫註釋。
24.en: **Unchangeable.** Gr. aparabatos, “permanent,” “unchangeable.” The Levitical priests could not continue by reason of death. But Christ “ever liveth to make intercession” (Heb. 7:25; cf. Rev. 1:18).

18.en:
**Being tempted.** Gr. peirazō, “to test,” “to prove,” “to tempt” (see on Matt. 4:1). The human nature of Christ felt the full force of temptation. Otherwise, Christ would not have understood the terrific struggle of a poor sinner who is mightily tempted to yield. Christ was tempted in all points “like as we are” (Heb. 4:15). He actually suffered under temptation.
How much Christ suffered in resisting temptation, the wilderness, Gethsemane, and Golgotha reveal. In the first two cases the temptation was so overwhelming that it seems He would have died under the impact had not an angel been sent to strengthen Him (Matt. 4:11; Luke 22:43). The cup was not removed, despite His prayer. He must drink it. To these experiences the author evidently refers when he says, “Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin” (Heb. 12:4). Christ did resist unto blood.
**Able to succour.** Or, “able to help.” By successfully resisting temptation and patiently enduring suffering Christ overcame the tempter. We are now contending with a defeated foe. Christ’s victory is our assurance of victory. See on Matt. 4:1.
It is an ever-present source of comfort to the Christian to know that Christ understands our sorrows and perplexities, and sympathizes with us. If Christ had not become man, the question might easily have arisen, How can we know that God loves and cares for us when He has never experienced the trials we encounter, has never been poor or forsaken, and has never known what it is to be alone and face an unknown future? He asks us to be faithful to death, but has He ever faced the issues we face? If He were one of us and one with us, He would know how hard it is to meet certain trials. But if He has never been man, does He really know all our sorrows, and can He sympathize with us when we stray?
To this the answer is that God does know, and that it was not for His sake, but for ours, that He became poor; it was not for His sake but for ours that He suffered and died. We needed the demonstration that Christ came to give, or we would never have known the deep love of God for suffering humanity. Besides, we would never have known the suffering that sin has brought to the heart of God.
18.zh:
他自己既然被試探而受苦，就能搭救被試探的人。

**被試探。**peirazō，“考驗，”“證明”（見太4:1註釋）。基督的人性充分體驗了試探的力量。否則基督就不會體諒經受強烈試探的可憐罪人所進行的可怕掙扎了。基督在凡事上受過試探“與我們一樣”（來4:15）。祂真實地忍受了試探。
曠野，客西馬尼和髑髏地證明基督在抵擋試探時受了多大的苦。在頭兩種情況下，試探非常強烈，要不是有一位天使奉差遣來堅固祂，在這樣的衝擊之下祂可能會死去（太4:11；路22:43）。雖然祂禱告了，那杯卻沒有撤去。祂必須喝下。作者說“你們與罪惡相爭，還沒有抵擋到流血的地步”，顯然是指這些經驗（來12:4）。基督確實抵擋到流血的地步。
**能搭救。**或“能幫助。”基督藉著成功地抵擋試探並忍受苦難，戰勝了那試探者。我們現在所面對的，是一個已經被打敗的敵人。基督的勝利是我們得勝的保障。見太4:1註釋。
對於基督徒來說，知道基督理解我們的悲傷和困惑並同情我們，會給我們帶來不斷的安慰。如果基督沒有成為人，就很可能引發以下問題：上帝既然從來沒有經歷過我們所受的考驗，沒有遭遇過貧窮或被拋棄，不知道什麼是孤獨和渺茫的前途，我們怎麼知道祂愛我們並關心我們呢？祂要求我們至死忠心，但祂面對過我們所面對的問題嗎？如果祂是我們中的一員並與我們同在，就會知道應付某些考驗是多麼艱難的了。但如果祂從未作過人，祂真的能知道我們的一切悲傷嗎？當我們迷路時，祂能同情我們嗎？
回答是上帝完全知道。祂成為貧窮，不是為祂自己的緣故，而是為了我們；祂受難和受死，不是為祂自己，而是為了我們。我們需要基督來給我們作出證明，否則我們不知道上帝深愛受苦的人類，不知道罪給上帝的心所帶來的痛苦。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第78頁；《早期著作》第150頁；《基督教育原理》第106頁；《善惡之爭》第416頁；《福山寶訓》第13頁；《今日的生活》第335頁；《先祖與先知》第64，480頁；《救贖的故事》第43頁；《給傳道人的證言》第391頁；《證言》卷二第201頁；《證言》卷四第294頁；《證言》卷五第422頁；《證言》卷九第185頁。

17.en:
**Wherefore.** That is, because He was concerned with man (see on v. 16).
**In all things.** Christ must become man so completely and fully that it can never be said that He is a stranger to any temptation, any sorrow, any trial or suffering that men must pass through.
**Behoved.** Gr. opheilō, “to owe,” “to be indebted,” “must,” “ought.” Compare the use of the verb and related nouns in Matt. 18:30, 34; 23–16; Luke 16:6, 7; John 13:14; 1 Cor. 5:10; 2 Thess. 2:13.
**Made like.** For the reason stated subsequently, namely, to qualify Him for the position of high priest. Although this does not mean that His experiences must be identical with ours in every respect—for a thousand lifetimes would not be sufficient for that—it does mean that the trials must be representative, and must in principle include all that man has to suffer, and that in severity they must fully measure up to all that men have to bear.
**Might be.** Or, “might become.”
**Merciful and faithful.** These two characteristics are necessary to a just ministry. Mercy alone might be too lenient and might ignore justice. Faithfulness provides a balance to mercy, as it considers the rights and duties of both the offender and the offended. As high priest Christ must be kind and understanding toward the offender, but He must also be true to justice and not ignore the law. Faithfulness will keep the delicate balance between unconditional mercy and unrelenting justice. The high priest must consider the sinner, but he must also consider the one sinned against. He must be faithful to his trust as well as merciful to the transgressor.
**High priest.** The subject of Christ as high priest is here introduced and is later more fully developed (see chs. 3; 5; 7–10).
**Things pertaining to God.** That is, matters of divine service. The Greek phrase thus translated occurs in the LXX of Ex. 4:16, with reference to Moses’ relationship to God in regard to Aaron.
**To make reconciliation.** Gr. hilaskomai. For the meaning of this verb and related nouns see on Rom. 3:25. The verb occurs only here and in Luke 18:13, where it is rendered “to be merciful.”
17.zh:
所以，他凡事該與他的弟兄相同，為要在神的事上成為慈悲忠信的大祭司，為百姓的罪獻上挽回祭。

**所以。**因為祂牽掛著人類（見第16節註釋）。
**凡事。**基督必須完全徹底地成為人，以致別人不會說祂不瞭解人類所必經的一切試探，悲傷或考驗。
**該。**opheilō，“有義務，”“必須，”“應當。”參太18:30,34；23-16；路16:6,7；約13:14；林前5:10；帖後2:13中該動詞和相關名詞的用法。
**相同。**因為祂要獲得擔任大祭司的資格。雖然這並不意味著祂必須在各方面有與我們完全一樣的經驗——這樣的話活一千次也不夠——但它意味著試煉必須是具有代表性的，並且在原則上包括人類所必經的一切考驗，其強度必須完全達到人類所必須遭受的程度。
**上帝的事上。**就是侍奉上帝的事。該詞還出現在七十士譯本的出4:16中，指亞倫的事上摩西與上帝的關係。
**成為。**或“可以成為。”
**慈悲忠信。**這兩個特徵是公正的服務所必需的。單有慈悲可能太寬鬆了，會忽略公義。忠信為慈悲提供了平衡，因為它考慮到犯罪的人和被得罪的人雙方的權利和義務。作為大祭司，基督必須是仁慈的，能體諒犯罪的人，但祂也必須忠於公義，不可忽視律法。忠信會在無條件的慈悲和不寬恕的公義之間維持微妙的平衡。大祭司必須體諒犯罪的人，也必須體諒被得罪的人。他既要慈悲地對待犯罪的人，也必須忠於職守。
**大祭司。**這裡引出了基督為大祭司的話題，下面再加以詮釋（見來3；5；7-10）。
**獻上挽回祭。**hilaskomai。關於該動詞及其相關名詞的含義，見羅3:25註釋。該動詞只出現在這裡和路18:13，那裡譯為“開恩可憐”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第472頁；《歷代願望》第24頁；《基督教育原理》第442頁；《服務真詮》第422頁；《今日的生活》第297頁；《證言》卷八第286頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–18節）**。《基督教育原理》第275頁；《給傳道人的證言》第225，355頁；《證言》卷三第93頁。

16.en:
**Verily.** Gr. dēpou, “of course.”
**Took … on.** Gr. epilambanomai, “to take hold of,” “to grasp,” “to be concerned with,” “to take an interest in,” “to help.” The question is, Which of these varied meanings applies in the text under consideration? The KJV supplies the word “nature,” but the tense of the Greek verb is against this. The Greek reads, “is taking hold of,” if the meaning “to take hold of” is adopted. The incarnation would hardly be described as an event now going on, as the present tense would imply. Furthermore, the “wherefore” of v. 17 does not naturally follow a reference to the incarnation in v. 16.
The meaning “to help,” is well suited to the context and the Greek construction. It suggests the reading, “It is not angels that Christ is helping but members of the human family.” The meaning “to be concerned with” also makes good sense. Adopting it, the verse would read, “For surely he is not concerned with angels, but he is concerned with the seed of Abraham.” Man is in need of redemption and capable of restoration, and it is he about whom Christ is anxious as far as the plan of redemption is concerned. The meaning “to take an interest in” is also suitable.
**The seed of Abraham.** Here probably synonymous with “man.” There is no attempt to exclude the Gentiles. Perhaps the spiritual seed is designated (Gal. 3:29).
16.zh:
他並不救拔天使，乃是救拔亞伯拉罕的後裔。

**並不。**dēpou，“當然。”
**救拔。**epilambanomai，“握住，”“抓住，”“牽掛，”“關心，”“幫助。”這裡採用什麼意思呢？原文動詞是現在時態，故不大可能用“握住，”“抓住”的意思來指基督成肉身。況且第17節既用了“所以”，16節自然就不可能指道成肉身。
“幫助”的意思很適合於上下文和原文結構，可理解為“基督所幫助的不是天使，而是人類家庭的成員。”“牽掛”的意思也很適合，可理解為“祂所牽掛的不是天使，而是亞伯擔罕的後裔。”人類需要救贖，有恢復的可能性；就救贖計劃而論，基督所牽掛的乃是人類。“關心”的意思也合適。
**亞伯拉罕的後裔。**在這裡也許是“人類”的同義詞，並沒有排斥外邦人的意思，也可能指屬靈的後裔（加3:29）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷八第207頁。

14.en:
**The children.** That is, the children mentioned in v. 13.
**Are partakers.** Or, “have been made sharers.” The children share a common human nature.
**He also.** That is, Christ.
**Took part.** The form of the Greek verb suggests the thought of taking hold of something not previously possessed. This was true of Jesus: He was divine, but He took our human nature, mysteriously blending the two natures in one (see on John 1:14). That He might enter into all the experiences of mankind, Christ became man.
**Through death.** That is, his sacrificial death on the cross (cf. v. 9). When Jesus died on the cross, Satan appeared to have triumphed; for it seemed that even the Son of God acknowledged Satan’s power of death and became subject to it. But God had another purpose.
**Destroy.** Gr. katargeō, “to render null and void,” “to destroy” (see on Rom. 3:3). Already Satan’s power over death has been broken, for though natural death still reigns, the resurrection is assured (see 1 Cor. 15:20–22, 51–57). Finally the originator of sin and the author of death will himself be annihilated (see on Rev. 20:10).
**That had the power.** Satan has the power of death because he is the originator of sin, and death results from sin (see on Rom. 5:12). His kingdom is a kingdom of death, and in it he rules. As sin rules in our lives, so death rules, and so Satan rules.
Christ was the one who entered the strong man’s house (Mark 3:27), bound the enemy, and took away his prisoners. Christ entered the realm of death—Satan’s stronghold—and wrested from Satan his prey. When he thought he had Christ in his power, when the tomb was sealed and Christ locked in, Satan exulted. But Christ burst the bonds of death and walked forth from the grave, for “it was not possible that he should be holden of it” (Acts 2:24). Not only did Christ Himself rise, but “the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose, and came out of the graves after his resurrection” (Matt. 27:52, 53). And so, though the “strong man armed keepeth his palace, … a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him” (Luke 11:21, 22). The stronger man, Christ, entered the realm of death, and in death overcame him who had the power of death, took away his captives, and spoiled his house (Matt. 12:29); “and having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it” (Col. 2:15). Henceforth, death for the believers is but a sleep; they rest in peace until God calls them. For many it will even be a blessed sleep (Rev. 14:13). Christ “hath abolished death” (2 Tim. 1:10). He has “the keys of hell and of death” (Rev. 1:18; cf. 1 Cor. 15:51–57).
**Devil.** Gr. diabolos (see on Matt. 4:1).
14.zh:
兒女既同有血肉之體，他也照樣親自成了血肉之體，特要藉著死敗壞那掌死權的，就是魔鬼，

**兒女。**就是第13節所提到的兒女。
**既同有。**兒女享有共同的人性。
**祂也。**就是基督。
**親自成了。**原文動詞的形式暗示獲得了原來所沒有的東西。耶穌確實是如此。祂是上帝，卻取了人性，神奇地將這神人兩性結合在一起（見約1:14註釋）。基督為了分享人類的一切經驗而成為人。
**藉著死。**就是祂犧牲在十字架上（參第9節）。當耶穌死在十字架上時，撒但在表面上取得了勝利；因為似乎就連上帝的兒子都承認了撒但掌有死權並且服從了它。但是上帝卻有外的目的。
**敗壞。**katargeō，“使無效，”“毀滅”（見羅3:3註釋）。撒但的死權已經被打破了，因為肉身的死亡雖然仍在掌權，但復活已經確定（見林前15:20-22,51-57）。罪的創始者和死亡的作者本身最後都必滅絕（見啟20:10註釋）。
**掌死權的。**撒但掌死權是因為他是罪惡的創始者，死是由罪而生的（見羅5:12註釋）。他的國度是死亡的國度。他在裡面掌權。因為罪統治著我們的生活，所以死亡和撒但就作了王。
基督進入壯士的家中（可3:27），捆綁了仇敵，帶走了他的囚犯。基督進入了死亡的領域，就是撒但的堡壘，從撒但手中奪取他的擄物。當撒但以為基督落入他的權下時，當墳墓把基督被封在裡面時，撒但是非常高興的。但是基督掙脫了死亡的捆綁，從墳墓中出來，因為“祂原不能被死拘禁”（徒2:24）。不僅基督自己復活了，而且“墳墓也開了，已睡聖徒的身體，多有起來的。到耶穌復活以後，他們從墳墓裡出來”（太27:52,53）。所以雖然“壯士披掛整齊，看守自己的住宅，……但有一個比他更壯的來，勝過他”（路11:21,22）。那更壯的人就是基督。祂進入死亡的領域，藉著死戰勝了那掌死權的，帶走了他的俘擄，並且劫掠了他的家（太12:29）；“既將一切執政的掌權的擄來，明顯給眾人看，就仗著十字架誇勝”（西2:15）。自此以後，死亡對於信徒來說不過是睡覺；他們平靜地安息直到上帝叫呼喚他們。對許多人來說，這甚至是有福的睡眠（啟14:13）。基督“已經把死廢去”（提後1:10）。祂“拿著死亡和陰間的鑰匙”（啟1:18；參林前15:51-57）。
**魔鬼。**diabolos（見太4:1註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第151頁；《善惡之爭》第503頁；《先知與君王》第701頁；《先祖與先知》第65頁；《救贖的故事》第214頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。《歷代願望》第320頁。

11.en:
**He that sanctifieth.** In this context Christ (cf. ch. 9:13, 14).
**They who are sanctified.** These are the “many sons” who are led to glory (v. 10).
**Of one.** That is, of God the Father. Christ the Son and the “many sons” have all one Father.
**Not ashamed.** In spite of His vast superiority over the angels (Heb. 1:4; cf. Luke 9:26).
**Brethren.** See on Matt. 12:49, 50; cf. John 20:17.
11.zh:
因那使人成聖的和那些得以成聖的，都是出於一。所以，他稱他們為弟兄也不以為恥，

**那使人成聖的。**在這裡指基督（參來9:13,14）。
**那些得以成聖的。**指被領進榮耀裡去的“許多的兒子”（第10節）。
**出於一。**就是出於父上帝。聖子基督和那“許多的兒子”有一位共同的父。
**弟兄。**見太12:49,50註釋；參約20:17。
**不以為恥。**儘管祂比天使遠為高貴（來1:4；參路9:26）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第25頁；《善惡之爭》第477頁；《福山寶訓》第103頁；《今日的生活》第289頁；《喜樂的泉源》第14頁；《成聖的人生》第41頁；《證言》卷五第230，740頁。

10.en:
**It became.** Gr. prepō, “to suit,” “to be fitting,” “to be becoming.”
